Gnome Warlock

entries.name: Playing a Warlock
entries: To play a warlock, choose the {@class Warlock|XPHB|Warlock class} from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and Eldritch Invocations: affliction, demonology, or destruction.

entries.name: Affliction Specialization
entries: Affliction warlocks draw primarily on the power of the Void, a power often called shadow magic. Their spells cause intense pain, corrupting minds and agonizing souls, leaving their enemies in a state of ongoing torment.
The following choices will help you focus on this specialization (Eldritch Invocations marked with an asterisk are described in "{@area Eldritch Invocations|167|x}" in this section):

items.name: Level 1
items.entry: Choose the {@optfeature Pact of the Legion|WoW}* Eldritch Invocation. Choose the following cantrips: {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB} and {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB}. Prepare the following spells to start: {@spell Hex|XPHB} and {@spell Witch Bolt|XPHB}.

items.name: Level 2
items.entry: Choose these Eldritch Invocations: {@optfeature Agonizing Blast|XPHB} and {@optfeature Curse of Corruption|WoW}.*

items.name: Level 3
items.entry: Choose the {@class Warlock|WoW|Great Old One Patron subclass|Great Old One|WoW}.

items.name: Eldritch Invocations
items.entry: Consider the following Eldritch Invocations as you reach level 5 and higher: {@optfeature Call of the Void|WoW},* {@optfeature Eldritch Mind|XPHB}, {@optfeature Gift of the Depths|XPHB}, {@optfeature Legion Summoning|WoW},* and {@optfeature Visions of Distant Realms|XPHB}.

items.name: Spells
items.entry: Consider the spells on the table below as you gain levels.

entries.name: Demonology Specialization
entries: Demonology warlocks harness the power of demons on the field of battle. They harvest soul energy from their foes and use it to pull abominations from the chaos of the Twisting Nether, maintaining absolute control over the summoned creatures.
The following choices will help you focus on this specialization (Eldritch Invocations marked with an asterisk are described in "{@area Eldritch Invocations|167|x}" in this section):

items.name: Level 1
items.entry: Choose the {@optfeature Pact of the Legion|WoW}* Eldritch Invocation. Choose the following cantrips: {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB} and {@spell Toll the Dead|XPHB}. Prepare the following spells to start: {@spell Arms of Hadar|XPHB} and {@spell Hex|XPHB}.

items.name: Level 2
items.entry: Choose these Eldritch Invocations: {@optfeature Health Funnel|WoW}* and {@optfeature Repelling Blast|XPHB}.

items.name: Level 3
items.entry: Choose the {@class Warlock|WoW|Fiend Patron subclass|Fiend|WoW}.

items.name: Eldritch Invocations:
items.entry: Consider the following Eldritch Invocations as you reach level 5 and higher: {@optfeature Call of the Void|WoW},* {@optfeature Expendable Minions|WoW},* {@optfeature Gift of the Depths|XPHB}, {@optfeature Legion Summoning|WoW},* {@optfeature Master Demonologist|WoW},* and {@optfeature Visions of Distant Realms|XPHB}.

items.name: Spells
items.entry: Consider the spells on the table below as you gain levels.

entries.name: Summon Fiend
entries: When you cast {@spell Summon Fiend|XPHB} as a Warlock, the fiendish spirit resembles a demon of the Burning Legion: an infernal (choose the Devil option), a demonic tyrant (choose the Yugoloth option), or a vilefiend (choose the Demon option).

entries.name: Destruction Specialization
entries: Destruction warlocks favor magic of pure chaos and aggression in battle. They wield shadow, fire, fel, and raw chaos magic with equal ease, rattling the souls and immolating the flesh of their foes. They revel in the sheer destruction they cause, thrilling at the opportunity to watch the world burn.
The following choices will help you focus on this specialization (Eldritch Invocations marked with an asterisk are described in "{@area Eldritch Invocations|167|x}" in this section):

items.name: Level 1
items.entry: Choose the {@optfeature Pact of the Legion|WoW}* Eldritch Invocation. Choose the following cantrips: {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB} and {@spell Thunderclap|XPHB}. Prepare the following spells to start: {@spell Hellish Rebuke|XPHB} and {@spell Hex|XPHB}.

items.name: Level 2
items.entry: Choose these Eldritch Invocations: {@optfeature Agonizing Blast|XPHB} and {@optfeature Repelling Blast|XPHB}.

items.name: Level 3
items.entry: Choose the {@class Warlock|WoW|Fiend Patron subclass|Fiend|WoW}.

items.name: Eldritch Invocations:
items.entry: Consider the following Eldritch Invocations as you reach level 5 and higher: {@optfeature Call of the Void|WoW},* {@optfeature Gift of the Depths|XPHB}, {@optfeature Legion Summoning|WoW},* and {@optfeature Visions of Distant Realms|XPHB}.

items.name: Spells
items.entry: Consider the spells on the table below as you gain levels.

entries.name: Warlock Spells
entries: The following new spells are added to the Warlock spell list for {@i World of Warcraft} warlocks. In the Special column, {@i C} means the spell requires Concentration.

entries.name: Eldritch Invocations
entries: Several new Eldritch Invocations are available to Warlocks.

entries.title: An Orc Warrior

entries.name: Playing a Warrior
entries: To play a warrior, choose the {@class Fighter|XPHB|Fighter class} from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and feats: arms, fury, or protection.

entries.name: Arms Specialization
entries: Warriors' choices of weapons and fighting style determine their role on the battlefield. Arms warriors favor two-handed weapons that allow them to deliver devastating blows. These warriors combine these overpowering attacks with heightened mobility to strike where their foes are least defended.
The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

items.name: Level 1
items.entry: Choose {@feat Great Weapon Fighting|XPHB} for a Fighting Style feat. Choose at least one of {@item Greataxe|XPHB|Greataxes}, {@item Greatsword|XPHB|Greatswords}, or {@item Maul|XPHB|Mauls} for your Weapon Mastery feature.

items.name: Level 3
items.entry: Choose the {@class Warrior|WoW|Battle Master subclass|Battle Master|WoW}. Consider the following maneuvers: {@optfeature Battle Shout|WoW},* {@optfeature Disarming Attack|XPHB}, {@optfeature Distracting Strike|XPHB}, {@optfeature Mortal Strike|WoW},* {@optfeature Pushing Attack|XPHB}, {@optfeature Sweeping Attack|XPHB}, and {@optfeature Trip Attack|XPHB}. Maneuvers marked with an asterisk are described below.

items.name: Feats
items.entry: Consider the following feats at higher levels: {@feat Charger|XPHB}, {@feat Crusher|XPHB}, {@feat Great Weapon Master|XPHB}, {@feat Piercer|XPHB}, {@feat Speedy|XPHB}, and {@feat Slasher|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fury Specialization
entries: Through a lifetime of training and sparring, fury warriors become masters of carnage, wielding a weapon in each hand to maximize the destruction they cause. Though they forgo the protection of a shield, they surround themselves with whirling blades that leave little opportunity for their opponents to strike without suffering grievous wounds in return. Fury warriors dive into the fray in a breathtaking display of brute force, savoring the frenzy of battle.
The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

items.name: Level 1
items.entry: Choose {@feat Two-Weapon Fighting|XPHB} for a Fighting Style feat. Choose {@item Scimitar|XPHB|Scimitars} among your other weapons for your Weapon Mastery feature.

items.name: Level 3
items.entry: Choose the {@class Warrior|WoW|Champion subclass|Champion|WoW}.

items.name: Feats
items.entry: Consider the following feats at higher levels: {@feat Charger|XPHB}, {@feat Crusher|XPHB}, {@feat Dual Wielder|XPHB}, {@feat Piercer|XPHB}, and {@feat Slasher|XPHB}.

entries.name: Protection Specialization
entries: Protection warriors favor a more measured approach to battle than other warriors, countering incoming attacks and using their shields to protect their allies as well as themselves. For the protection warrior, being the toughest soldier on the battlefield means nothing if allies are left vulnerable. These warriors stand as an unbreakable wall protecting their friends from their foes.
The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

items.name: Level 1
items.entry: Choose {@feat Interception|XPHB} or {@feat Protection|XPHB} for a Fighting Style feat. Choose at least one of {@item Battleaxe|XPHB|Battleaxes}, {@item Longsword|XPHB|Longswords}, or {@item Morningstar|XPHB|Morningstars} for your Weapon Mastery feature.

items.name: Level 3
items.entry: Choose the {@class Warrior|WoW|Battle Master subclass|Battle Master|WoW}. Consider the following maneuvers: {@optfeature Bait and Switch|XPHB}, {@optfeature Battle Shout|WoW},* {@optfeature Demoralizing Shout|WoW},* {@optfeature Goading Attack|XPHB}, {@optfeature Maneuvering Attack|XPHB}, {@optfeature Parry|XPHB}, and {@optfeature Warding Maneuver|WoW}.* Maneuvers marked with an asterisk are described below.

items.name: Feats
items.entry: Consider the following feats at higher levels: {@feat Crusher|XPHB}, {@feat Durable|XPHB}, {@feat Heavy Armor Master|XPHB}, {@feat Piercer|XPHB}, {@feat Sentinel|XPHB}, {@feat Shield Master|XPHB}, and {@feat Slasher|XPHB}.

entries.name: Berserker Barbarians
entries: Although D&D's {@class Fighter|XPHB} class is the best match for a warrior in {@i World of Warcraft}, you could also play a {@class Barbarian|XPHB}. Choose the {@class Shaman|WoW|Path of the Berserker subclass|Berserker|WoW}, and otherwise follow the guidance for building a fury warrior as a {@class Fighter|XPHB}.

entries.name: Warrior Maneuvers
entries: Additional maneuver options for Battle Master Fighters are presented here in alphabetical order.

data.name: Chapter 2: Character Origins

entries.title: A gnome welcomes the adventurous of all species to the Darkmoon Faire.

entries: Many different peoples call Azeroth home. Some are native to its lands, while others have settled there from far-flung worlds. Most of these peoples have aligned themselves with either the Alliance or the Horde.

When you make a character to adventure on Azeroth, choose a background from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}, then choose one of the species described in this chapter. Your choice of species might also give you a starting Renown Score with one of Azeroth's factions (detailed in {@book chapter 4|WoW|4}).

entries.name: Languages
entries: When choosing languages for a character in a {@i World of Warcraft} campaign, use the tables here instead of the ones in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. Your character knows either Common (if they belong to the Alliance) or Orcish (if they belong to the Horde), plus two languages you roll or choose from the appropriate table—Alliance Languages or Horde Languages. If the origin you choose isn't affiliated with either faction, you can choose your three starting languages from either table. (At least one of the common languages of the Alliance and the Horde—Common or Orcish—is recommended.)
The Rare Languages table lists languages that are either secret or derived from other planes of existence and thus less widespread on Azeroth. Some features let a character learn a rare language.

The First Ones, the enigmatic architects of the entire cosmos, left fragments of language that are akin to mathematics and largely incomprehensible to mortals. Kalimag, the language of elementals, is equivalent to Primordial in D&D, and Shath'Yar, the language of the Old Gods, is equivalent to Deep Speech.

entries.title: Dracthyr shift freely between natural and visage forms.
Many draenei cherish the lore collected during their long sojourn from their home world.
Some awakened earthen find kinship among the dwarves of Ironforge.
Millennia of conflict have sharply divided the elves of Azeroth.

entries.name: Elf Spells
entries: These two new spells are available only as part of the Nightborne and Void Elf elven lineages.

entries.title: For many of the Forsaken, life continues much as it did before their transformation.
Technological advancement is both a means of survival and a source of joy for many gnomes.
Explosives are a proud part of goblin history.
Several species of giant bats live among the haranir in Harandar.
The descendants of the Seven Kingdoms still find much to unite them.

entries.name: Human Origin Feats
entries: These feats are available for Human characters.

entries.title: Despite their troubled history on Azeroth, orcs are now thriving in Durotar.
Pandaria flourished in isolation from the rest of Azeroth for ten thousand years.
The tauren of Mulgore use kodos as mounts and beasts of burden.
Trolls honor the loa at a temple in Zandalar.
Vulpera in Vol'dun use alpacas to pull their wagon-homes.
Worgen—in both human and bestial form—plan their part in the Fourth War.

data.name: Chapter 3: Professions and Gear

entries.title: Adventurers bid on precious treasures in the Stormwind auction house.

entries: Beyond choosing class and origin, you can customize your character in a {@i World of Warcraft} campaign through their professions and equipment—especially mounts, pets, and magic items. This chapter covers those options.

entries.name: Professions and Crafting
entries: Characters in Azeroth can use their tool proficiencies to practice professions, allowing them to gather resources and craft them into equipment and magic items. A character can practice any profession as long as the character has the prerequisite proficiency.

The rules in this chapter build on the {@book crafting rules|XPHB|6|Crafting Equipment} in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} and {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}. With these rules, characters can use gathering professions (such as fishing, mining, and skinning) to collect abstract resources that are measured in GP value. For example, a character might use the herbalism profession to collect 50 GP worth of herbalism resources. The character can then use any combination of those resources and the character's own money to craft items using their production professions (such as blacksmithing, cooking, and leatherworking). Having gathered 50 GP worth of herbalism resources, a character might spend those resources, along with 50 GP of coins or other monetary resources, to craft a {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG}.

Optionally, a DM can make the resources less abstract, but this approach requires the DM to invent or research recipes for magic items characters wish to create and name the resources characters gather. A character who wants to craft a {@i Potion of Water Breathing} might need to gather 50 GP worth of stranglekelp, not just abstract herbalism resources, and also acquire 50 GP worth of blackmouth oil (or use fishing to catch oily blackmouth fish). Listing specific resources and recipes is beyond the scope of this book.

entries.name: Proficiency Levels
entries: A character's Proficiency Bonus is the measure of how skilled the character is at a profession. A character with a +2 Proficiency Bonus is an apprentice in a profession, a +3 bonus makes the character a journeyman, and so on, as shown on the Profession Levels table below. Each recipe used in a crafting profession requires a minimum Proficiency Bonus, which is determined by the rarity of the magic item the recipe creates. (Most nonmagical equipment requires apprentice recipes.)

This chapter assumes characters work with trainers to improve their professions between adventures. If your campaign uses the {@book variant rule|XDMG|1|Variant: Training to Gain Levels} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} that characters must spend time and money training to gain levels, characters must also spend time and money training with profession trainers to improve their skill in the profession. This training requires a number of days equal to the character's new Proficiency Bonus and costs 2 GP per day. So when a character reaches level 5 and a Proficiency Bonus of +3, the character must spend 3 days and 6 GP training to achieve a journeyman proficiency level in each profession they practice.

entries.name: Gathering Professions
entries: Gathering professions allow characters to collect resources, which can be sold or used for crafting.

Most gathering professions work like foraging during travel, as {@book described|XDMG|1|Foraging} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}. You can make a Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check using a gathering profession once per journey stage (or once per day if a stage is shorter than a day). The DC is set by the DM based on the general level range of the region where you're traveling, as described in {@book chapter 5|WoW|5}. (Archaeology and skinning work differently, as described below.)

You find nothing on a failed check. On a successful check, you find one resource per day of the journey stage. If you beat the DC by 5 or more, one of the resources you find on that journey stage is a rare (more valuable) resource. The DM decides what resources you find.

entries.name: Archaeology
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency in {@skill History|XPHB}}

You can use the archaeology profession to gather archaeology fragments from the sites of ancient ruins. Unlike the resources gathered with other gathering professions, these resources aren't used in crafting. Rather, you can piece these archaeology fragments together into items of historical interest.

entries.name: Gathering Fragments
entries: To gather archaeology fragments, you must visit a dig site. The DM determines whether an area is a dig site and where the relics originate from. The {@book Dig Sites table|WoW|3|Dig Sites} shows the regions where relics of different origins can be found.

After spending 1 hour exploring a dig site (which can be concurrent with a Short Rest), you make an Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. The DC of the check depends on the region level, as shown on the {@area Gathering Professions table|20f|x}. On a successful check, you unearth {@dice 1d6} archaeology fragments. If you beat the DC by 5 or more, you unearth a complete relic with the value of a rare resource for that region, as shown on the Gathering Professions table. On a natural 20, you instead find one magic fragment.

entries.name: Assembling a Relic
entries: You can assemble six archaeology fragments with the same origin into a completed relic by succeeding on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. The value of the assembled relic equals the value of a common resource for your level (rather than the region level), as shown on the {@area Gathering Professions table|20f|x} table. On a failed check, you can't try again until you've collected at least one additional archaeology fragment with the same origin.

entries.name: Assembling a Magic Item
entries: You can assemble six magic fragments with the same origin into an item of the DM's choice whose rarity corresponds with your Proficiency Bonus, as shown on the Profession Levels table. For example, if you collect six magic fragments from dwarf dig sites, and you are a master archaeologist (Proficiency Bonus +6), you can assemble the pieces into a {@item Staff of the Magi|XDMG} that was wielded by Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan.

entries.caption: Dig Sites
rows: Northern and southern {@area Eastern Kingdoms|35a|x}, {@area Northrend|386|x}

entries.title: Fishing can yield unexpected treasures.

entries.name: Fishing
entries: {@i Requires No Proficiency}

The primary use for fishing is {@book foraging for food|XDMG|1|Foraging}, which uses the rules in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}. If you roll a natural 20 on a Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check to forage for food using fishing, you might pull up a chest, crate, or lockbox containing other resources—such as ores, fabrics, or leather—at the DM's discretion. The value of such a find equals the value of a rare resource for the region's level.

If you are searching for particular fish to use in a recipe, you can make a Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check once per journey stage to see whether you can catch the desired fish, using a DC chosen from the {@area Gathering Professions table|20f|x}.

entries.title: A Forsaken herbalist collects a ghost mushroom.

entries.name: Herbalism
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}}

You can use the herbalism profession to gather herbs, flowers, and mushrooms. These resources are primarily useful in crafting items with the {@area alchemy|220|x} and {@area inscription|226|x} professions.

Using herbalism follows the general rules described in "{@area Gathering Professions|20f|x}." In unusual circumstances, you can use herbalism to gather rare resources from Plant creatures. Use the rules for {@area skinning|218|x} as a guideline to determine the DC for gathering such resources and their value.

entries.name: Mining
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Mason's Tools|XPHB}}

You can use the mining profession to gather metal ores, stones, and gems. These resources are primarily useful in crafting items with the {@area blacksmithing|221|x}, {@area engineering|225|x}, and {@area jewelcrafting|22b|x} professions.

entries.name: Smelting
entries: If you are gathering specific resources to use in detailed recipes, metal mining resources might need to be smelted into bars before they can be used in crafting. You need access to a smith's forge or a refinery to smelt ore, and the time required is 1 hour for every 10 GP of the metal resource's value. So copper and tin (10 GP mining resources) can be refined into bars in 1 hour, while creating an empyrium bar (a 500 GP resource) takes 50 hours.
You can use the same rules to combine metal resources to create alloys, which can be important in blacksmithing.

entries.name: Skinning
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB}}
You can use the skinning profession to gather leather or hide. These resources are primarily useful in crafting items with the leatherworking profession.
You use skinning on dead creatures rather than as part of travel, and the quality of leather or hide gathered depends on the Challenge Rating of the creature rather than the level of the region.

Skinning a Beast or an animallike Monstrosity yields leather or hide. You must be in the same space as the corpse and spend 10 minutes skinning the creature, and then you make a Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check using {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB}. The check DC depends on the Challenge Rating of the creature, using the Region Level column of the {@area Gathering Professions table|20f|x} and treating a CR above 20 as Endgame. If you make a successful check, the effort yields a leather resource worth the value of a common resource. If you beat the DC by 5 or more, the effort yields hide instead, which has the value of a rare resource.

You can also skin certain Fiends and Dragons. Skinning an animal-like Fiend, such as a {@creature felhound|WoW}, requires journeyman-level skinning (a Proficiency Bonus of +3 or higher). Skinning a Dragon requires artisan-level skinning (a Proficiency Bonus of +5 or higher). A successful check in either case yields hide with the value of a rare resource.

entries.name: Production Professions
entries: Production professions allow characters to use resources—whether gathered using gathering professions, found as treasure, or purchased from merchants—to craft nonmagical and magical items.

Production professions use the {@book rules for crafting equipment|XPHB|6|Crafting Equipment} in the {@i Player's Handbook} and the {@book rules for crafting magic items|XDMG|6|Crafting Magic Items} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}, with one key change: Ingredients provide the magic. Characters can craft magic items even if they lack proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill. They also don't need to have spells prepared in order to craft magic items that produce spells. Instead, they need to know specific recipes and use ingredients—many of which are infused with magic—to create items. Characters learn recipes as described below and in the profession descriptions that follow.

entries.name: Crafting Recipes
entries: "Recipe" is a general term that encompasses recipes for alchemy and cooking, plans for blacksmithing, formulas for enchanting, schematics for engineering, techniques for inscription, designs for jewelcrafting, and patterns for leatherworking and tailoring. As characters advance their crafting skills, they learn basic recipes automatically. Basic recipes let a character create mundane items and Common, Uncommon, and Rare magic Armor, Potions, Scrolls, Wands, and Weapons. Other recipes can be purchased from specialist trainers, found as treasure, or granted as renown rewards (see {@book chapter 4|WoW|4}). Artisan and master recipes can be acquired only by extraordinary means, as described below.

The specific recipes mentioned here are examples only, inspired by crafting recipes in the {@i World of Warcraft} game. The DM is free to create unique recipes or to ignore the specifics and require only some combination of abstract resources and money.

entries.name: Apprentice Recipes
entries: Apprentice recipes require some combination of two or three different resources. For example, using alchemy to craft a Common potion costs 25 GP. The DM might look up alchemy recipes from {@i World of Warcraft} and decide that this requires 20 GP of herbalism resources plus 5 GP of miscellaneous ingredients. Crafting a {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG} might require one peacebloom and one silverleaf, while a {@item Potion of Mana|WoW} might require a mageroyal and a silverleaf. All these are common resources found in level 1–4 regions (worth 10 GP each). Similarly, using blacksmithing to craft a suit of {@item Plate Armor|XPHB} in {@i World of Warcraft} requires iron bars and heavy stones, so the DM might decide that the 750 GP cost to craft the armor consists of twelve iron bars and three heavy stones, which are all common resources found in level 5–10 regions (50 GP each).

entries.name: Journeyman Recipes
entries: Journeyman recipes sometimes involve more complex steps than simply combining two or three resources of the same type. For example, crafting an elixir of water breathing in {@i World of Warcraft} requires the combination of stranglekelp (gathered with herbalism) and blackmouth oil (made with alchemy from oily blackmouth fish). So the DM might create a recipe for a {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG} (an Uncommon potion that costs 100 GP to make) that involves catching two rare fish resources in a level 1–4 region (25 GP each), then combining the oil from them with stranglekelp, a common herb resource from a level 5–10 region (50 GP). Similarly, using blacksmithing to craft a {@item +1 Greatsword|XDMG} (which costs 225 GP) might involve both mining and skinning resources: ten copper bars (10 GP each), two malachite stones (10 GP each), and two medium leather (50 GP each), plus 5 GP extra.

entries.name: Expert Recipes
entries: In addition to requiring more expensive resources, expert recipes are often quite complex and sometimes require unusual ingredients—which often give them minor properties or quirks (see "{@book Magic Item Special Features|XDMG|6|Magic Item Special Features}" in the Dungeon Master's Guide). For example, characters in {@i World of Warcraft} can use blacksmithing to create barbaric iron plate using iron bars, heavy stones, and fangs and claws from predatory animals. The DM might decide that this armor is {@item +1 Plate Armor|XDMG} with the Guardian minor property, granting the wearer a +2 bonus to Initiative rolls. Such an item costs 2,750 GP to craft, so the recipe might require forty-eight iron bars (50 GP each), five heavy stones (50 GP each), and 100 GP of fangs and claws.

entries.name: Artisan Recipes
entries: Befitting their high price, artisan recipes require rare and expensive ingredients. Learning the recipes required for these items often requires completing special quests or earning a Renown Score of 10+ with a faction that guards the secrets of creating them (see {@book chapter 4|WoW|4}). For example, an alchemy recipe called "elixir of giants"—which teaches a character to make a {@item Potion of Cloud Giant Strength|XDMG|Potion of Giant Strength} (cloud)—isn't commonly known in modern times but can be found in lockboxes and other treasure hoards across Azeroth. (It might require five Gromsblood and five sungrass, both 1,000 GP herbalism resources.)

Artisan recipes sometimes require numerous resources that must first be processed with other professions. For example, making a {@item Frost Brand Longsword|XDMG|Frost Brand} (Longsword) with blacksmithing could require eighteen arcanite bars, which are thorium bars (250 GP mining resources) that have been combined via alchemy with arcane crystals (100 GP gems). The hilt requires four enchanted leather, which are thick leather (250 GP leather resources) enhanced via enchanting using 1,200 GP of magical residue from disenchanting items. The cold magic in the blade comes from four water elemental essences (available for 100 GP each from specialized vendors). Then these items are combined with four blue sapphires (1,000 GP gems), four Azerothian diamonds (1,000 GP gems), and a dense grinding stone (125 GP mining resource).

entries.name: Master Recipes
entries: Master recipes can be acquired only as treasure or renown rewards. They often require rare resources or resources found on other worlds or planes of existence. For example, crafting a {@item Potion of Storm Giant Strength|XDMG|Potion of Giant Strength} (storm) with alchemy might require twenty rising glory—a 5,000 GP herbalism resource that grows only in the Shadowlands realm of Bastion. Similarly, crafting {@item Plate Armor of Etherealness|XDMG} with blacksmithing requires a combination of six different minerals found only in the Shadowlands: five laestrite ore (5,000 GP mining resource) and two each of elethium, solenium, phaedrum, sinvyr, and oxxein ore (7,500 GP mining resources), along with 750 GP worth of luminous flux (purchased from a vendor) to aid the mixture of metals.

entries.name: Alchemy
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}}

Using Alchemist's Supplies or an Herbalism Kit and resources mostly gathered from herbalism and following particular recipes, you can craft potions, alchemical equipment, dusts, perfumes, and the like. You can learn to make these items as your skill increases:

items.name: Apprentice (+2) Recipes:
items.entry: {@item Acid|XPHB}, {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}, {@item Component Pouch|XPHB}, {@item Fuel|WoW} (see "{@area Mounts and Vehicles|22f|x}" in this chapter), {@item Oil|XPHB}, {@item Paper|XPHB}, {@item Perfume|XPHB}, Common Potions, {@item Perfume of Bewitching|XDMG}

items.name: Journeyman (+3) Recipes:
items.entry: Uncommon Potions, {@item Alchemy Jug|XDMG}, {@item Dust of Disappearance|XDMG}, {@item Dust of Dryness|XDMG}, {@item Keoghtom's Ointment|XDMG}

items.name: Expert (+4) Recipes:
items.entry: Rare Potions

items.name: Artisan (+5) Recipes:
items.entry: Very Rare Potions, {@item Philosopher's Stone|WoW}

items.name: Master (+6) Recipes:
items.entry: Legendary Potions, {@item Sovereign Glue|XDMG}, {@item Universal Solvent|XDMG}

entries.name: Blacksmithing
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Mason's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}}

Using Mason's Tools or Smith's Tools and resources gathered from mining (including metals, gems, and stones), and following particular plans, you can craft items from metal and stone. Some plans might require cloth or leather resources as well. You can learn to make these items as your skill increases:

items.name: Apprentice (+2) Plans:
items.entry: Any Melee weapon (except {@item Club|XPHB}, {@item Greatclub|XPHB}, {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}, and {@item Whip|XPHB}); Medium armor (except {@item Hide Armor|XPHB|Hide}); Heavy armor; {@item Shield|XPHB}; {@item Ball Bearings|XPHB}; {@item Block and Tackle|XPHB}; {@item Bucket|XPHB}; {@item Caltrops|XPHB}; {@item Chain|XPHB}; {@item Crowbar|XPHB}; {@item Firearm Bullets (10)|XPHB|Firearm Bullets}; {@item Grappling Hook|XPHB}; {@item Iron Pot|XPHB}; {@item Iron Spikes|XPHB}; {@item Sling Bullet|XPHB|Sling Bullets}; Common magic ammunition, Armor, and Weapons in the above categories; {@item Dark Shard Amulet|XDMG}; {@item Dread Helm|XDMG}

items.name: Journeyman (+3) Plans:
items.entry: Uncommon magic ammunition, Armor, and Weapons in the above categories; {@item Figurine of Wondrous Power, Silver Raven|XDMG|Figurine of Wondrous Power} (silver raven); {@item Gauntlets of Ogre Power|XDMG}; {@item Helm of Comprehending Languages|XDMG}; {@item Helm of Telepathy|XDMG}; {@item Sending Stones|XDMG}; {@item Stone of Good Luck|XDMG|Stone of Good Luck (Luckstone)}

items.name: Expert (+4) Plans:
items.entry: Rare magic ammunition, Armor, and Weapons in the above categories; {@item Belt of Hill Giant Strength|XDMG|Belt of Giant Strength} (hill); {@item Bracers of Defense|XDMG}; {@item Brazier of Commanding Fire Elementals|XDMG}; {@item Dimensional Shackles|XDMG}; {@item Figurine of Wondrous Power|XDMG} (bronze griffon, golden lions, marble elephant); {@item Helm of Teleportation|XDMG}; {@item Horseshoes of Speed|XDMG}; {@item Iron Bands of Bilarro|XDMG}; {@item Stone of Controlling Earth Elementals|XDMG}

items.name: Artisan (+5) Plans:
items.entry: Very Rare magic ammunition, Armor, and Weapons in the above categories; {@item Belt of Giant Strength|XDMG} (fire, frost, or stone); {@item Helm of Brilliance|XDMG}; {@item Horseshoes of a Zephyr|XDMG}

items.name: Master (+6) Plans:
items.entry: Legendary magic ammunition, Armor, and Weapons in the above categories; {@item Belt of Giant Strength|XDMG} (cloud or storm); {@item Iron Flask|XDMG}

entries.name: Cooking
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB}}

Using Brewer's Supplies or Cook's Utensils and ingredients (typically gathered from fishing, herbalism, and hunting game), and following particular recipes, you can craft mundane and magical edible items:

items.name: Apprentice (+2) Recipes:
items.entry: {@item Antitoxin|XPHB}, {@item Rations|XPHB}, {@item Bead of Nourishment|XDMG}, {@item Bead of Refreshment|XDMG}, {@item Heward's Handy Spice Pouch|XDMG}, {@item Tankard of Sobriety|XDMG}

entries: Higher levels of skill in cooking are best reflected with the {@feat Chef|XPHB} feat. Additionally, a meal prepared by an artisan (+5) cook, given an hour of preparation time and 1,000 GP of resources (which can include fish or other meat), can duplicate the effects of the {@spell Heroes' Feast|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Enchanting
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Carpenter's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Potter's Tools|XPHB}, or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB}}

Using Carpenter's Tools, Potter's Tools, or Woodcarver's Tools, along with reagents (primarily magical residue from disenchanting items, as described below, as well as herbs, gems, and other resources), and following particular formulas, you can craft various items. You can learn to make these items as your skill increases:

items.name: Apprentice (+2) Formulas:

entries.name: Disenchanting
entries: When you reach journeyman enchanting skill, you learn to disenchant magic items. If you spend 1 hour (which can be concurrent with a Short Rest) with a permanent magic item that isn't attuned to someone else, you can remove its magic and store it in the residue, which takes the form of a magical dust or shard. The item's rarity determines the enchanting skill required to disenchant it and the value of the residue it leaves, as shown on the table below. The magical residue can be used as a crafting resource for any enchanting formula. Legendary magic items and Artifacts can't be disenchanted in this way.

entries.name: Engineering
entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}}
Using Tinker's Tools and components (typically including resources gathered from mining as well as leather or cloth), and following particular schematics, you can craft gadgets.

Magic items created with engineering typically have a mechanical appearance and seem to utilize some combination of mundane science and magic. The traditions of gnome engineers tend toward elaborate mechanical contraptions, while goblin engineering traditions are more explosive.

Part of every engineering schematic is the creation of mechanical parts and explosive powders used in crafting other items, such as transforming mined and smelted copper bars into copper bolts and mined stone into blasting powder. Crafting these components is included in the time and money required for crafting a finished item. You can learn to make these items as your skill increases:

entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, {@item Cartographer's Tools|XPHB}, or {@item Painter's Supplies|XPHB}}

Using Calligrapher's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, or Painter's Supplies, along with pigments and inks made from herbalism resources (gathered with herbalism or purchased), and using particular techniques, you can craft inks, pigments, and writings.

Part of every inscription technique is the process of milling herbs to create pigments and inks. Crafting these components is included in the time and money required for crafting a finished item. You can learn to make these items as your skill increases:

entries: {@i Requires Proficiency with {@item Glassblower's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB}}

entries.name: Cloth Resources
entries: Cloth resources have the same range of values as resources collected with gathering professions, from 10 GP linen and 25 GP wool to 7,500 GP dawnweave or duskweave, found only in Khaz Algar. Cloth is sometimes found as treasure in the hands of Humanoids who recognize its value as a trade good.

entries.title: Pets and mounts can show off a character's accomplishments.

entries.name: Mounts and Vehicles
entries: Mounts are an important tool for every adventurer, not only carrying people and goods across Azeroth but also helping adventurers express their personalities and accomplishments.

entries.name: Mounts for Purchase
entries: The {@area Mounts for Purchase table|230|x} shows mounts that characters can purchase. Many of the mounts listed there can't be purchased unless a character has achieved a certain level of renown with a particular faction (see {@book chapter 4|WoW|4}). These mounts follow the {@book mount rules|XPHB|6|Mounts and Vehicles} in the {@i Player's Handbook}.

entries.name: Crafted Mounts
entries: Characters can use the professions described earlier in this chapter to craft magic items that serve as mounts. Among the best-known such mounts are the {@item Carpet of Flying|XDMG} (crafted with artisan {@area tailoring|22d|x}), the jeweled panther {@item Figurine of Wondrous Power (Jeweled Panther)|WoW|Figurine of Wondrous Power} (crafted with expert {@area jewelcrafting|22b|x} and described later in this chapter), and vehicles made with engineering.

entries.name: Powered Vehicles
entries: Powered vehicles are similar to the {@book large airborne and waterborne vehicles|XPHB|6|Large Vehicles} described in the {@i Player's Handbook}. They include the following:

items.name: Flying Machine:
items.entry: A small gyrocopter with a rotor on top, two side-mounted engines, and skis as landing gear.

items.name: Goblin Trike:
items.entry: A three-wheeled motor vehicle with luxurious wood paneling.

items.name: Mechano-Hog and Mekgineer's Chopper:
items.entry: Two powerful motorcycles with optional sidecars, one made by the Horde, the other by the Alliance.

entries: Characters traveling in these vehicles use the vehicle's speed in miles per hour (as shown on the {@area Powered Vehicles table|232|x}) to determine their rate of travel, and they don't choose a travel pace. These vehicles require {@item Fuel|WoW}, which weighs 10 pounds and costs 1 GP for each 8 hours of travel. (Characters can use the alchemy profession to craft {@item Fuel|WoW}.)

entries.name: Special Mounts
entries: Other mounts can be acquired by characters as adventure rewards, treasure, or renown perks. These include magical mounts that can be summoned and dismissed by means of a command word, as well as more unusual creatures beyond those described above. Here are two examples:

items: A character with a Renown Score of 25+ with the Valdrakken Accord (see {@area chapter 4|31a|x}) gains a {@reward Blessing of the Wylderdrake|WoW|Blessing} allowing them to summon a draconic steed.

A character who uses archaeology to collect six magic fragments from Highmountain tauren dig sites and who is an artisan archaeologist (see "{@area Gathering Professions|20f|x}" in this chapter) can assemble the fragments into a Very Rare {@item Enspelled Staff|XDMG} with the {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} spell (level 4 version). The staff summons the spirit of Eche'ro, the famed moose mount of Huln Highmountain.

entries.caption: Mounts for Purchase
rows: Renown 10+ with the {@area Huojin|2da|x} or the {@area Tushui|2bf|x}

entries.caption: Powered Vehicles
footnotes: *A Flying Machine can't be purchased; it must be made by a character with expert {@area engineering|225|x}. Crafting the machine requires 2,000 GP of resources.

entries.name: Companion Creatures
entries: Characters can acquire companion creatures by a variety of means. Some can be purchased from merchants for a few Gold Pieces, sometimes with a minimum renown threshold. Others are found as treasure, given as rewards for completing an adventure, or even found while using gathering professions. (For example, mining elementium in level 17+ zones can sometimes release an elementium geode, a kind of elemental companion.)

Companion creatures are too small to serve as mounts, too weak to participate meaningfully in combat, and generally incapable of useful independent action. Much like mounts, though, they can serve as badges of honor, marking a character's achievements or the breadth of their travels.

entries.name: Calling a Companion
entries: Companion creatures are magically bound to a character. Some appear when summoned and disappear to some other plane when dismissed. Others are natural creatures bound to magical items (often collars or leashes) that allow a character to summon and dismiss them in the same way. Still others are mechanical or magical constructs that can be deactivated, rather than dismissed, and stored with the character's gear. In any case, summoning or dismissing a companion requires the character to take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action, and a character can have only one companion summoned in this way at a time. Summoning a new companion instantly dismisses a companion that is already present. While summoned, a companion stays within 5 feet of the character by floating or flying nearby, perching on the character's shoulder, or following on foot.

A companion creature can't take actions and can't be targeted by attacks. If it takes any damage (for example, if the character is caught in a {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell's area), it is instantly dismissed or deactivated.

entries.name: Companion Loyalty
entries: A companion creature has a Loyalty Score, using the {@book rules|XDMG|2|Loyalty} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}, but its loyalty is to an individual and not to the party. When a character acquires a companion, the companion's Loyalty Score equals the character's Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). The companion's Loyalty Score can't be higher than the character's Charisma.

A companion creature's Loyalty Score increases by {@dice 1d4} if the companion is treated particularly well, which might include buying special food for it, pampering it in other ways, or rescuing it from danger. Its Loyalty Score decreases by 1 if it is dismissed or deactivated by taking damage.

If a companion creature's Loyalty Score reaches 10 or higher, the companion gives the character a small supernatural gift while the companion is present. The nature of this gift depends on the companion's category, as described below.

entries.name: Types of Companions
entries: The following sections detail different types of companions characters might discover.

entries.name: Aquatic Companions
entries: Aquatic companion creatures include fish, crabs, frogs, octopi, water birds, turtles, otters, and other water-dwelling creatures. Sometimes they float in a bubble of water near their owners.

entries.name: Beast Companions
entries: Beast companion creatures are natural animals that neither fly nor swim. They include Tiny and Small beasts, as well as the young of larger creatures. (These beasts don't age while kept as a companion.)

entries.name: Dragonkin Companions
entries: Dragonkin companion creatures include dragon whelplings—younger and smaller than the whelps described in {@book chapter 7|WoW|7}—as well as draconic animals native to the {@area Dragon Isles|3a1|x}.

entries.name: Elemental Companions
entries: Elemental companion creatures include animate plants and remnants of the {@area Old Gods'|3f9|x} power as well as living motes of elemental energy.

entries.name: Flying Companions
entries: Flying companions include flying creatures—ordinary birds, bats, moths, bumblebees, and flying snakes—and magical versions of these creatures.

entries.name: Humanoid Companions
entries: Humanoid companions include imps, kobolds, baby murlocs, and a range of other beings that can help you in ways that don't involve combat. The DM is encouraged to develop any humanoid companion as an NPC using the {@book guidelines|XDMG|2|NPCs as Party Members} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}.

entries.name: Magic Companions
entries: Magic companions encompass a variety of beings that are fundamentally magical, including tiny fragments of {@area Old Gods|3f9|x} or other powers, stray eyes or tentacles of otherworldly origin, oozes, creatures of the Void, ghostly spirits, and animated magical tomes.

entries.name: Mechanical Companions
entries: Mechanical companions are clockwork or otherwise engineered creatures, ranging from mechanical chickens to diminutive replicas of the {@area Burning Legion's|3d2|x} terrifying fel reaver constructs.

entries.name: Undead Companions
entries: Undead companions include skeletal or ghostly animals and similar creatures.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: Many magic items are available to characters in a {@i World of Warcraft} campaign. The items described here cover the gamut from renowned weapons to simple Potions that characters skilled in alchemy can craft. They follow the {@book rules for magic items|XDMG|6|Magic Items} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}.

Crown of the Ogre King
Doomhammer
Frostmourne
Life-Staff of the Web Lair
Staff of Light and Shadow—Anathema form
Sulfuras, Hand of Ragnaros

data.name: Chapter 4: Factions and Renown

entries.title: Sylvanas Windrunner and Anduin Wrynn battle at the forefront of the Horde and the Alliance.

entries: Azeroth is defined by its factions—nations, organizations, cartels, and pacts that claim members from around the world. As characters interact with these factions, they can build a reputation and earn tangible and intangible rewards.

This chapter builds on the {@book renown rules|XDMG|2|Renown} found in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} to track characters' standing with the major factions of Azeroth. In addition, characters might gain renown with smaller groups to achieve short-term goals. {@i World of Warcraft} offers abundant examples that can be adapted into a tabletop campaign. For example, characters seeking a route from Felwood into Winterspring might work to gain renown with the furbolgs of Timbermaw Hold, who will allow passage through their tunnels once at least one member of the party has achieved a Renown Score of 10+.

entries.name: Starting Renown
entries: Most characters created using the origins in chapter 2 have a starting Renown Score of 3 with one of the subfactions associated with either the Alliance or the Horde. A few species and class options give starting Renown Scores with other factions.

entries.name: General Renown Perks
entries: The perks listed here apply to all the factions described in this chapter:

items.name: Friendly (Renown 3+)
items.entry: Other members of the faction are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you by default.

items.name: Honored (Renown 10+)
items.entry: You can purchase equipment found in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}, as well as Common or Uncommon magic items, from merchants of the faction at a 10% discount.

items.name: Revered (Renown 25+)
items.entry: Your discount increases to 15% and extends to Rare magic items.

items.name: Exalted (Renown 50+)
items.entry: Your discount increases to 25% and extends to Very Rare magic items.

entries: Certain mounts (see {@book chapter 3|WoW|3}) and magic items are available only from merchants associated with a particular faction and might require a minimum Renown Score with that faction to purchase.

entries.name: The Alliance
entries: The peoples of the Alliance are bound together by proud traditions of nobility, honor, faith, justice, and sacrifice. The disparate cultures that make up this faction contribute technical, arcane, and spiritual wisdom toward the goal of a peaceful and just world. The highest ideals of the Alliance are tradition, justice, and duty, matching closely to the Lawful Good alignment.

The Alliance is a military coalition whose leadership is dependent on the unified will of its member peoples. By default, the high king (or other leader) of Stormwind has served as commander of the Alliance, but the commander has authority over only the military forces that other Alliance leaders commit to the Alliance's cause. Thus, in practice, the human king leads as part of a council made up of all the Alliance leaders.

entries.name: Alliance Renown Perks
entries: The Alliance consists of many subfactions. Instead of having a Renown Score with the Alliance, haracters gain renown perks based on their Renown Scores with the subfactions of the Alliance, as described below. The perks listed in "{@area General Renown Perks|293|x}" apply to specific subfactions, not to the Alliance as a whole.

entries.name: Alliance: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Any Alliance Subfaction}
Creatures associated with the Alliance are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you by default.

entries.name: Alliance: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Any Alliance Subfaction}

If your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in territory controlled by the Alliance, when you issue the Maintain order to your Bastion, the DM rolls twice on the {@table Bastion Events|XDMG|Bastion Events table}, and you pick which event occurs.

entries.name: Ambassador of the Alliance
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Darnassus, the}{@i Exodar}{@i , Gilneas, Gnomeregan, Ironforge, and Stormwind}

You have the title Ambassador of the Alliance. You can gain an audience with the leader of any Alliance subfaction at any time, and you can summon the leaders of the Alliance forces into council, given 1 week's notice. For a worthy cause, any or all of these leaders will commit troops to aid you, at the DM's discretion. You can also call on {@creature Alleria Windrunner|WoW}, {@creature Anduin Wrynn|WoW}, or {@creature Jaina Proudmoore|WoW} to assist you on one adventure.

entries.name: Training
entries: Several renown perks give you the opportunity to work with a trainer to learn a language or gain a proficiency. The days required needn't be consecutive, but you must spend 8 consecutive hours with the trainer for a day to count. You can gain only one tool proficiency from each renown perk.

entries.name: Alliance Subfactions

entries.title: Leaders of the Alliance (Left to Right): Shandris Feathermoon, Anduin Wrynn, Muradin Bronzebeard, Aysa Cloudsinger, Gelbin Mekkatorque, Prophet Velen, and Tess Greymane

entries: The Alliance is made up of members of many different species, and the most prominent among those species are the subfactions of the Alliance. Most of these subfactions are named for their capital city, as shown on the list below. The species descriptions in {@book chapter 2|WoW|2} provide more information about these subfactions.

entries.name: Alliance Subfactions
entries: If your species gives you a starting Renown Score with an Alliance subfaction, gaining renown with different Alliance subfactions also increases your Renown Score with your starting faction as described below:

items.name: Friendly
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 3, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 1.

items.name: Honored
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 10, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 2.

items.name: Revered
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 25, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 3.

items.name: Exalted
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Alliance faction other than your starting faction reaches 50, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 5.

entries.name: Darnassus Renown Perks
entries: The Darnassus faction represents the {@race Elf|WoW|night elves} of Azeroth, wherever they actually reside, who acknowledge the leadership of Shandris Feathermoon (in the present age) or her parents, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage. The faction also encompasses the void elves led by Alleria Windrunner, based in Telogrus Rift.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Darnassus or Teldrassil (or in Bel'ameth or Amirdrassil after the destruction of Teldrassil), your Renown Score with Darnassus increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Darnassus gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Darnassus: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Darnassus}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Darnassian or Thalassian or to gain proficiency with the {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar).

entries.name: Darnassus: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Darnassus}
When you succeed on a check to gather herbs using herbalism (see {@area chapter 3|215|x}), you gain one extra resource, and you find a rare resource if you beat the check DC by 4 or more.

entries.name: Darnassus: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Darnassus}

You can request a Blessing from the leaders of Darnassus before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive one of the {@book Blessings|XDMG|2|Blessings} described in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} (your choice), and it lasts until you complete or abandon the quest. Once you request this Blessing, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Darnassus increases.

entries.name: Darnassus: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Darnassus}

You can call on a Warden ({@creature Questing Knight|XMM}), a leading Sentinel ({@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}) with three Sentinel scouts ({@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains}), or a leading priestess of Elune ({@creature Archpriest|XMM}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Darnassus increases.

entries.name: Exodar Renown Perks
entries: The {@i Exodar} faction represents the {@race draenei|WoW} who came to Azeroth aboard that vessel under the leadership of Prophet Velen, as well as the Lightforged draenei of the {@i Vindicaar}.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is within the {@i Exodar}, within the {@i Vindicaar}, or on the Azuremyst Isles, your Renown Score with the {@i Exodar} increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with the {@i Exodar} gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Exodar: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the}{@i Exodar}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Draenei language or gain proficiency with {@item Glassblower's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Exodar: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the}{@i Exodar}
When you use jewelcrafting to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|22b|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Exodar: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the}{@i Exodar}

You can request a {@book Charm|XDMG|2|Charms} from the leaders of the {@i Exodar} before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive a {@reward Charm of Heroism|XDMG}, {@reward Charm of Restoration|XDMG}, or {@reward Charm of Vitality|XDMG} (your choice; see the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}), which lasts until you expend it or you complete or abandon the quest. Once you request a Charm, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the {@i Exodar} increases.

entries.name: Exodar: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the}{@i Exodar}

You can call on fifty draenei soldiers ({@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM}) led by three sergeants ({@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}) and one commander ({@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the {@i Exodar} increases.

entries.name: Gilneas Renown Perks
entries: The Gilneas faction represents the nation of Gilneas and its people, including its {@race worgen|WoW}. Its leader is Queen Tess Greymane since the abdication of her father, Genn Greymane.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is anywhere in Gilneas, your Renown Score with Gilneas increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Gilneas gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Gilneas: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Gilneas}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Common or Common Sign Language or gain proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Gilneas: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Gilneas}
You gain a +2 bonus to ability checks you make to skin a creature (see {@area chapter 3|218|x}).

entries.name: Gilneas: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Gilneas}

You can request a {@reward Charm of Animal Conjuring|XDMG} from the leaders of Gilneas before you undertake a quest on their behalf, which lasts until you expend it or you complete or abandon the quest. When you use the Charm, the conjured animal spirits appear as worgen spirits from the Emerald Dream. Once you request a Charm, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Gilneas increases.

entries.name: Gilneas: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Gilneas}

You can call on a pack of six worgen skirmishers ({@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers}) with one leader ({@creature Berserker Commander|XMM}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Gilneas increases.

entries.name: Gnomeregan Renown Perks
entries: The Gnomeregan faction encompasses {@race Gnome|WoW|gnomes} and {@race Mechagnome|WoW|mechagnomes} who acknowledge the leadership of King Gelbin Mekkatorque. (Before the reclamation of Gnomeregan, the faction was known as Gnomeregan Exiles.) Most of them live in Tinkertown (a neighborhood of Ironforge) or the settlement of New Tinkertown.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Gnomeregan, in New Tinkertown, or on Mechagon Island, your Renown Score with Gnomeregan increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Gnomeregan gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Gnomeregan: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Gnomeregan}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Gnomish or gain proficiency with {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Gnomeregan: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Gnomeregan}
When you use engineering to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|225|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Gnomeregan: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Gnomeregan}

You can request a {@item Gnomeregan Engineering Device|WoW|complicated engineering device} from the leaders of Gnomeregan before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive a mechanical device that functions as a {@item Wand of Wonder|XDMG}, but it can't regain charges, and it explodes dramatically but harmlessly when its last charge is expended. The device doesn't require Attunement, but it functions only for you.

entries.name: Gnomeregan: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Gnomeregan}
In recognition of your service to gnomekind, you are given a {@creature Shield Guardian|XMM} that serves you. If your Renown Score with Gnomeregan falls below 50, the guardian turns on you.

entries.name: Ironforge Renown Perks
entries: The Ironforge faction encompasses {@race Dwarf|WoW|dwarves} who acknowledge the leadership of the Council of Three Hammers, the government formed by the union of the Bronzebeard, Dark Iron, and Wildhammer clans, which includes some Frostborn and other dwarves who are affiliated with the Alliance.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Ironforge, elsewhere in Khaz Modan (except gnome settlements), in or near Aerie Peak, or in Shadowforge City, your Renown Score with Ironforge increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Ironforge gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Ironforge: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Ironforge}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Dwarven or gain proficiency with {@item Mason's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Ironforge: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Ironforge}
When you use blacksmithing to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|221|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Ironforge: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Ironforge}

You can request a dwarven relic from the leaders of Ironforge before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive a {@item Belt of Dwarvenkind|XDMG}, {@item Dwarven Plate|XDMG}, or a {@item Dwarven Thrower|XDMG} (your choice). You must return the relic on the completion of the quest; failure to do so reduces your Renown Score with Ironforge by {@dice 1d8}.

entries.name: Ironforge: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Ironforge}

You can call on fifty dwarf soldiers ({@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM}) led by three sergeants ({@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}) and one commander ({@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Ironforge increases.

entries.name: Obsidian Warders Renown Perks
entries: The Obsidian Warders is the {@race dracthyr|WoW} weyrn that has joined the Alliance, led by Scalecommander Azurathel.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Obsidian Warders gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Obsidian Warders: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Obsidian Warders}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Draconic or gain proficiency in {@skill History|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Obsidian Warders: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Obsidian Warders}

You can request a Blessing from the leaders of the Obsidian Warders before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive the {@reward Blessing of Protection|XDMG} (see the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}), and it lasts until you complete or abandon the quest. Once you request this Blessing, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the Obsidian Warders increases.

entries.name: Obsidian Warders: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Obsidian Warders}

You can call on a {@creature Black Dragonflight Whelp|WoW} to assist you for a single adventure. If the dragon is killed, your Renown Score with the Obsidian Warders is reduced by {@dice 2d6}. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the Obsidian Warders increases.

entries.name: Stormwind Renown Perks
entries: The Stormwind faction encompasses the remnants of most of the {@race human|WoW} kingdoms of Azeroth, including Kul Tiras, Dalaran (but see "{@area Kirin Tor|30e|x}" later in this chapter), and Stromgarde but excluding Gilneas. Stormwind remains the strongest human nation on Azeroth, under the leadership of {@creature Anduin Wrynn|WoW} (and the regent of Stormwind, Turalyon, in his absence). Lady {@creature Jaina Proudmoore|WoW} of Kul Tiras and Danath Trollbane of the League of Arathor (in the rebuilt Stromgarde Keep) acknowledge Stormwind's place as the keystone of the Alliance.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Elwynn Forest, Kul Tiras, Stormwind City, Stromgarde, or Westfall, your Renown Score with Stormwind increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Stormwind gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Stormwind: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Stormwind}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Common or Common Sign Language or gain proficiency with {@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Stormwind: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Stormwind}
When you use tailoring to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|22d|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Stormwind: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Stormwind}

You can request a supernatural gift from the leaders of Stormwind before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive any {@book Blessing|XDMG|2|Blessings} or {@book Charm|XDMG|2|Charms} from the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}, and it lasts until you complete or abandon the quest or expend it. Once you request this gift, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Stormwind increases.

entries.name: Stormwind: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Stormwind}
You can call on Stormwind forces to assist you for a single adventure. You receive your choice of one of the following groups:

items: Fifty human soldiers ({@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM}) led by three sergeants ({@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}) and one commander ({@creature Warrior Commander|XMM})
Three SI:7 agents ({@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains}) and their leader ({@creature Spy Master|XMM})
A champion of the Holy Light ({@creature Questing Knight|XMM})
A Kul Tiran admiral ({@creature Pirate Admiral|XMM}) with a {@item Warship|XPHB} (you must hire the ship's crew)

entries: Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Stormwind increases.

entries.name: Tushui Renown Perks
entries: The Tushui faction, led by Aysa Cloudsinger, represents those {@race pandaren|WoW} who have given their allegiance to the Alliance.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Tushui gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Tushui: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Tushui}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Pandaren language or gain proficiency with {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Tushui: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Tushui}
If you spend a Short Rest in silent meditation, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} when you finish the rest.

entries.name: Tushui: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Tushui}
You receive the {@reward Blessing of Understanding|XDMG} (see the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}). You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Tushui falls below 25.

entries.name: Tushui: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Tushui}

A Tushui monk establishes a {@facility Meditation Chamber|XDMG} special facility in your Bastion. This facility doesn't count toward the total number of special facilities in your Bastion. The monk departs and the facility becomes unusable if your Renown Score with the Tushui falls below 50.

entries.name: The Horde
entries: The proud nations of the Horde are loosely joined in an alliance of convenience against a hostile world that would see them destroyed. Focused and ferocious, the Horde values strength and honor but struggles to keep its members' aggression in check. The Horde's ideals are unity, freedom, and hope, matching closely to the Chaotic Good alignment.

From the time of its founding until the end of the Fourth War, the Horde was led by a single warchief. The orc shaman {@creature Thrall|WoW} held that position from before the Third War until he stepped down to join the {@area Earthen Ring|300|x} (described later in this chapter) during the Cataclysm. He was succeeded by the warmongering Garrosh Hellscream, who was in turn deposed by a combination of Alliance pressure and a rebellion of the Darkspear trolls. The troll chieftain Vol'jin then took up the mantle, becoming the first non-orc to hold the title, but Vol'jin died during the Burning Legion's third invasion of Azeroth. The undead high elf {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW} then became warchief, but she ultimately abandoned the Horde to pursue her own agenda. Since her departure, a Horde Council made up of the leaders of the Horde's subfactions has governed the Horde.

entries.name: Horde Renown Perks
entries: The Horde is composed of subfactions. Instead of having a Renown Score with the Horde, characters gain renown perks based on their Renown Scores with the subfactions of the Horde, as described below. The perks listed in "{@area General Renown Perks|293|x}" apply to specific subfactions, not to the Horde as a whole.

entries.name: Horde: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Any Horde Subfaction}
Creatures associated with the Horde are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you by default.

entries.name: Horde: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Any Horde Subfaction}

If your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in territory controlled by the Horde, when you issue the Maintain order to your Bastion, the DM rolls twice on the {@table Bastion Events|XDMG|Bastion Events table}, and you can pick which event occurs.

entries.name: Ambassador of the Horde
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Bilgewater Cartel, Darkspear Tribe, Orgrimmar, Silvermoon City, Thunder Bluff, and Undercity}

You carry the title Ambassador of the Horde. You can gain an audience with the leader of any Horde subfaction at any time, and you can summon the leaders of the Horde forces into council, given 1 week's notice. For a worthy cause, any or all of these leaders will commit troops to aid you, at the DM's discretion. You can also call on {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW} or {@creature Thrall|WoW} (both described in chapter 7) to assist you on one adventure.

entries.name: Horde Subfactions

entries.title: Leaders of the Horde (Left to Right): Lilian Voss, Thrall, Monte Gazlowe, Lor'themar Theron, Baine Bloodhoof, Rokhan, and Ji Firepaw

entries: The Horde is made up of members of many different species, and the most prominent among those species are the subfactions of the Horde. These subfactions are generally identified by their capital city, as shown on the list below. The species descriptions in chapter 2 provide more information about these subfactions.

entries.name: Horde Subfactions
entries: If your species gives you a starting Renown Score with a Horde subfaction, gaining renown with different Horde subfactions also increases your Renown Score with your starting faction as described below:

items.name: Friendly
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Horde faction other than your starting faction reaches 3, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 1.

items.name: Honored
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Horde faction other than your starting faction reaches 10, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 2.

items.name: Revered
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Horde faction other than your starting faction reaches 25, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 3.

items.name: Exalted
items.entry: The first time your Renown Score with each Horde faction other than your starting faction reaches 50, increase your Renown Score with your starting faction by 5.

entries.name: Bilgewater Cartel Renown Perks
entries: The Bilgewater Cartel represents {@race Goblin|WoW|goblins} aligned with the Horde. The cartel's capital is Bilgewater Harbor in Azshara, and it has significant holdings across Azeroth. The cartel's leader is Trade Prince Monte Gazlowe, who succeeded Jastor Gallywix in that role after Jastor abandoned the cartel. The cartel's business has been described as "the classical goblin arts: building things and blowing them up." Engineering, construction, infrastructure, and demolitions are all in the Bilgewater wheelhouse.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Bilgewater Harbor or any other Bilgewater holding, your Renown Score with the Bilgewater Cartel increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Bilgewater Cartel gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Bilgewater Cartel: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Bilgewater Cartel}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Goblin language or gain proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Bilgewater Cartel: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Bilgewater Cartel}
When you use alchemy to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|220|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Bilgewater Cartel: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Bilgewater Cartel}

You can call on a cartel captain ({@creature Pirate Admiral|XMM}) with six crew members ({@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates}) to assist you for a single adventure. The captain has a {@item Sailing Ship|XPHB}, but you need to hire additional crew (at your own expense) to use the ship. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the Bilgewater Cartel increases.

entries.name: Dark Talons Renown Perks
entries: The Dark Talons is the {@race dracthyr|WoW} weyrn that has joined the Horde, led by Scalecommander Cindrethresh.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Dark Talons gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Dark Talons: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Dark Talons}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Draconic or gain proficiency in {@skill History|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Dark Talons: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Dark Talons}

You can call on a {@creature Black Dragonflight Whelp|WoW} to assist you for a single adventure. If the dragon is killed, your Renown Score with the Dark Talons is reduced by {@dice 2d6}. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the Dark Talons increases.

entries.name: Darkspear Tribe Renown Perks
entries: The Darkspear tribe was the first group of {@race Troll|WoW|trolls} to join forces with the Horde. Trolls on the Echo Isles (off Durotar) are part of this faction, and the Zandalari Empire, on joining the Horde, aligned with the Darkspears to form a united troll faction. Chieftain Rokhan leads the Darkspear tribe, having succeeded Vol'jin, who died during the third invasion of the Burning Legion.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is anywhere on the Echo Isles or Zandalar, your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Darkspear Tribe: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Darkspear Tribe}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Zandali or gain proficiency in {@skill Religion|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Darkspear Tribe: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Darkspear Tribe}

During a Short Rest, you can make offerings to the loa revered by trolls to gain a {@reward Darkspear Tribe Charm|WoW|Charm}. When you finish the rest, make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, you gain a {@book Charm|XDMG|2|Charms} that allows you to gain the benefit of one of the following Potions as a Bonus Action (choose when you gain the Charm): {@item Potion of Animal Friendship|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Climbing|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Comprehension|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Fire Breath|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Hill Giant Strength|XDMG|Potion of Giant Strength} (hill), {@item Potion of Growth|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Potion of Healing} (greater), {@item Potion of Mana (Greater)|WoW|Potion of Mana} (greater), {@item Potion of Pugilism|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Resistance|XDMG} (your choice of damage type), or {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG}.

The Charm vanishes from you after you use it, if you use this feature again, or if your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe falls below 10. Once you receive a Charm in this way, you can't gain another until your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe increases.

entries.name: Darkspear Tribe: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Darkspear Tribe}

When you request a {@reward Darkspear Tribe Charm|WoW|Charm} from the loa, you can choose from the following additional Potion effects for your Charm: {@item Potion of Clairvoyance|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Diminution|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Gaseous Form|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Fire Giant Strength|XDMG|Potion of Giant Strength} (fire), {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG|Potion of Healing} (superior), {@item Potion of Mana (Superior)|WoW|Potion of Mana} (superior), {@item Potion of Heroism|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Invulnerability|XDMG}, or {@item Potion of Mind Reading|XDMG}.
If you choose one of the options listed above, the Charm vanishes from you if your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe falls below 25.

entries.name: Darkspear Tribe: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Darkspear Tribe}

You can call on a shadow hunter ({@creature Cultist Hierophant|XMM}) and six hexxers ({@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe increases.

entries.name: Huojin Renown Perks
entries: The Huojin faction, led by Ji Firepaw, represents those {@race pandaren|WoW} who side with the Horde.
