Increasing your Renown Score with the Huojin gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Huojin: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Huojin}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Pandaren language or gain proficiency with {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Huojin: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Huojin}
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Initiative rolls as long as your Renown Score with the Huojin is 10+.

entries.name: Huojin: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Huojin}
You receive the {@reward Blessing of Health|XDMG} (see the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}). You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Huojin falls below 25.

entries.name: Huojin: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Huojin}

A group of Huojin monks establishes a {@facility Training Area|XDMG} special facility in your Bastion. This facility doesn't count toward the total number of special facilities in your Bastion. The monks depart and the facility becomes unusable if your Renown Score with the Huojin falls below 50.

entries.name: Orgrimmar Renown Perks
entries: Orgrimmar is the capital city of the {@race Orc|WoW|orcs} in Azeroth and is practically synonymous with the Horde. Most orcs across Azeroth consider themselves citizens of Orgrimmar, including the Mag'har orcs who recently joined the Horde. The orc shaman Thrall founded Orgrimmar and now leads the faction once again, after abdicating for a time in favor of Garrosh Hellscream and then Varok Saurfang.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Orgrimmar or elsewhere in Durotar (except the Echo Isles), your Renown Score with Orgrimmar increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Orgrimmar gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Orgrimmar: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Orgrimmar}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Orcish, Orcish Sign Language, or Vulpera or to gain proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Orgrimmar: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Orgrimmar}
When you use leatherworking to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|22c|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Orgrimmar: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Orgrimmar}

You can request a {@book Blessing|XDMG|2|Blessings} from the leaders of Orgrimmar before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive one of the Blessings described in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}, and it lasts until you complete or abandon the quest. Once you request a Blessing, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Orgrimmar increases.

entries.name: Orgrimmar: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Orgrimmar}

You can call on a warband leader ({@creature Berserker Commander|XMM}), a shaman ({@creature Elemental Cultist|XMM}), and three experienced warriors ({@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers}), all mounted on {@creature Dire Wolf|XMM|Dire Wolves}, to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Orgrimmar increases.

entries.name: Silvermoon City Renown Perks
entries: As the capital of the kingdom of Quel'Thalas, Silvermoon City represents the entirety of the {@race Elf|WoW|blood elf} kingdom, as well as other blood elves who have aligned themselves with the Horde. Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron has ruled the kingdom since the fall of Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider, who made a traitorous pact with the Burning Legion. The {@race Elf|WoW|nightborne elves} of Suramar are also considered part of this faction.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Silvermoon City, elsewhere in Quel'Thalas, or in Suramar, your Renown Score with Silvermoon City increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Silvermoon City gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Silvermoon City: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Silvermoon City}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Shalassian or Thalassian or to gain proficiency with {@item Carpenter's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Potter's Tools|XPHB}, or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Silvermoon City: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Silvermoon City}
When you use enchanting to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|223|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Silvermoon City: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Silvermoon City}

You can call on a single Magister ({@creature Archmage|XMM}) or four {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages} to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Silvermoon City increases.

entries.name: Thunder Bluff Renown Perks
entries: The Thunder Bluff faction represents those united {@race tauren|WoW} tribes who have aligned themselves with the Horde, including the Highmountain tauren of the Broken Isles and some taunka of Northrend. The leader of the faction is High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof, who succeeded his father, Cairne Bloodhoof, when Cairne died in an ill-fated duel against Garrosh Hellscream.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Thunder Bluff or elsewhere in Mulgore or Highmountain, your Renown Score with Thunder Bluff increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Thunder Bluff gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Thunder Bluff: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Thunder Bluff}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Taur-ahe or gain proficiency with the {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Thunder Bluff: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Thunder Bluff}
When you succeed on a check to gather herbs using herbalism (see {@area chapter 3|215|x}), you gain one extra resource, and you find a rare resource if you beat the check DC by 4 or more.

entries.name: Thunder Bluff: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Thunder Bluff}

You can call on a tauren shaman ({@creature Elemental Cultist|XMM}) and eight assistant shaman ({@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Thunder Bluff increases.

entries.name: Undercity Renown Perks
entries: The Undercity faction encompasses the {@race Forsaken|WoW} aligned with the Horde. The faction was long led by {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW}, who originally led the Forsaken who broke free from the control of the Lich King. When Sylvanas stepped into the leadership of the Horde as warchief, the Desolate Council was formed to govern the Forsaken in her place. The council, based now in the Ruins of Lordaeron, is made up of five leaders: Calia Menethil, Lilian Voss, Master Apothecary Faranell, Deathstalker Commander Belmont, and Dark Ranger Velonara.
While your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} is in Undercity or the Ruins of Lordaeron, your Renown Score with Undercity increases by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with Undercity gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Undercity: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Undercity}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Forsaken language or gain proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Undercity: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Undercity}
When you use alchemy to craft an item (see {@area chapter 3|220|x}), the time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Undercity: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Undercity}

You can call on two Forsaken necromancers ({@creature Ghast Gravecaller|XMM|Ghast Gravecallers}) and five unliving soldiers ({@creature Wight|XMM|Wights}) to assist you for a single adventure. Once you request this assistance, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with Undercity increases.

entries.name: Argent Dawn
entries: The knightly Order of the Argent Dawn is dedicated to protecting Azeroth from the Burning Legion, the Scourge, and other forces that seek to destroy the world. Neutral in the continual conflict between the Alliance and the Horde (and generally Neutral Good in alignment), the Argent Dawn calls both factions allies in its higher purpose of resisting these forces of evil. The order's headquarters is Light's Hope Chapel, in the Eastern Plaguelands—a beacon of hope and comfort in a barren and twisted land—and the knights operate across the Plaguelands and anywhere evil rears its head.

In addition to pursuing quests assigned to them by the Argent Dawn, characters can increase their Renown Score by killing powerful Fiends and Undead and bringing evidence of the monsters' destruction to Argent Dawn agents.

entries.name: Argent Dawn Renown Perks
entries: Increasing your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Argent Dawn: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Argent Dawn}

For a cost of 15,000 GP, the Argent Dawn will add a magical property to any Rare magic item you are attuned to. While attuned to the item, you have Resistance to one of the following damage types (chosen when the property is added): Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder. The item's rarity then increases to Very Rare.

entries.name: Cenarion Circle

entries.title: Malfurion Stormrage, the First Druid

entries: Named for Cenarius—the demigod who trained Malfurion Stormrage, the first druid—the Cenarion Circle is a worldwide order keeping watch over Azeroth's druids and protecting the natural balance. Since the end of the Third War, the circle has accepted druids from both the Alliance and the Horde, reflecting a generally Neutral alignment. In the druidic sanctuary of Moonglade, night elf and tauren druids live and work in harmony, and in recent years, druids from other peoples—Kul Tiran humans, worgen, trolls, and even haranir—have joined the ranks of the Cenarion Circle. The order is still led by Cenarius himself, with the involvement of Malfurion and the tauren druid Hamuul Runetotem.

The Cenarion Circle is most active in Kalimdor. Besides Moonglade, which is inaccessible to anyone but circle members, the order also has a base in Desolace (Karnum's Glade). It has launched expeditions into Silithus, the Plaguelands, and Outland, and its members are on the forefront of any effort to preserve, protect, or restore nature.
Adopting the {@class Druid|WoW|Druid class}, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character's Renown Score with the Cenarion Circle by 3.
There's no time like the present to start saving the future!

entries.name: Cenarion Circle Renown Perks
entries: Increasing your Renown Score with the Cenarion Circle gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Cenarion Circle: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Cenarion Circle}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Druidic or gain proficiency in {@skill Nature|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Cenarion Circle: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Cenarion Circle}
If you spend a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in a Cenarion Circle sanctuary, you gain the {@reward Charm of Restoration|XDMG} (see the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}).

entries.name: Cenarion Circle: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Cenarion Circle}

You carry the title Guardian of Cenarius. For a cost of 2,000 GP, you can purchase a {@item Cenarion war hippogryph|WoW} mount ({@creature Hippogriff|XMM}). If your Renown Score falls below 50, you lose the title, and your mount no longer obeys your commands.

entries.name: Earthen Ring
entries: The Earthen Ring is a gathering of Azeroth's most powerful shaman, working together to preserve the balance among the elements. The members of the Earthen Ring oppose destructive forces such as the Twilight's Hammer cult, the rampaging black dragon Deathwing, and the Burning Legion, and they work tirelessly to heal the wounds inflicted on Azeroth by such forces. Insisting on a neutral stance in mortal conflicts (and a generally Neutral alignment), the Earthen Ring welcomes members from both the Alliance and the Horde, though the peoples of the Alliance—particularly draenei, Wildhammer dwarves, and humans of Kul Tiras—are recent additions to the organization. It also includes murlocs, the Krokul draenei, and other druids who haven't chosen a side in the Alliance–Horde conflict.

The Earthen Ring is governed by the Elder Council, which gathers at a shrine perched at the edge of the Maelstrom called the Heart of Azeroth. The order also maintains a ritual circle just outside Stormwind's walls (the Eastern Earthshrine) and another above Orgrimmar (the Western Earthshrine). Both circles include portals leading to the Elemental Plane and other areas of Earthen Ring activity, which Earthen Ring shaman allow only those who are at least Honored with the faction to use.

Adopting the {@class Barbarian|XPHB} class (as a shaman; {@class Shaman|WoW|see chapter 1}), either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character's Renown Score with the Earthen Ring by 3.

entries.name: Earthen Ring Renown Perks
entries: Increasing your Renown Score with the Earthen Ring gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Earthen Ring: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Earthen Ring}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Kalimag language (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter). Elementals that haven't been corrupted by the Old Gods are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you by default.

entries.name: Earthen Ring: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Earthen Ring}
You can freely use the portals located in the Eastern and Western Earthshrine.

Additionally, if you spend a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in an Earthen Ring sanctuary, you gain the {@reward Charm of the Earthen Ring|WoW}, which allows you to cast {@spell Summon Elemental|XPHB}. The {@book Charm|XDMG|2|Charms} vanishes from you once used three times, after 7 days, or if your Renown Score with the Earthen Ring falls below 10.

entries.name: Explorers' League and Reliquary
entries: Affiliated with the Alliance and the Horde respectively, the Explorers' League and the Reliquary are scholarly organizations dedicated to the practice of archaeology and the study of history, seeking to understand the origins of life and culture on Azeroth.

Magni Bronzebeard, the king of Ironforge, founded the Explorers' League by decree after dwarf-led expeditions uncovered surprising facts about the dwarves' connection to the ancient titans. Declaring that learning this history was more important than mining and engineering, Magni directed the Explorers' League to focus on archaeological work and plumbing the secrets of the ancient world. The league quickly expanded its scope to encompass natural history as well as the history of all Azeroth's peoples, and it soon accepted citizens of other Alliance nations as members. High Explorer Muninn Magellas is the leader of the Explorers' League, and the organization's headquarters remains in Ironforge, in the Hall of Explorers.

The Reliquary, in contrast, began as an effort to harness the power of ancient relics for the benefit of the blood elves and their allies in the Horde. The leader and founder of the Reliquary, Tae'thelan Bloodwatcher, believed such artifacts should be carefully studied, not feared. Tae'thelan's ultimate goal in founding the Reliquary was to free the blood elves from their magical addiction and reunite them. When the blood elves joined the Horde, the Reliquary opened its membership to all members of the Horde, but its headquarters (also called the Reliquary) remains in Silvermoon City.

entries.name: Relic Rivals
entries: Despite their different origins (and different alignments, corresponding to the difference between the Alliance and the Horde), the Explorers' League and the Reliquary use similar methods and often vie for access to the same sites. For most of recent history, the organizations were bitter rivals, with the tension between them often erupting into violent conflict. During this time, the factions are mutually hostile (see the "{@area Mutually Hostile Factions|30d|x}" sidebar).

However, with the reemergence of the Dragon Isles and the subsequent discovery of Khaz Algar, the two organizations have set aside their old rivalry and formed joint expeditions. During this period, a character's Renown Score with either faction applies to both factions, so having a Renown Score of 3+ with either one makes members of both factions {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} by default.

entries.name: Explorers' League/Reliquary Renown Perks
entries: Increasing your Renown Score with either the Explorers' League or the Reliquary gives you the following additional benefits. Characters can't increase their Renown Score with both factions; typically, characters affiliated with the Alliance work with the Explorers' League and Horde characters work with the Reliquary.

entries.name: Explorers' League/Reliquary: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Faction}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn any language from the {@area language tables in chapter 2|17f|x} or gain proficiency in {@skill History|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Explorers' League/Reliquary: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Faction}

When you gather archaeology fragments from a dig site (see {@area chapter 3|210|x}), you gain one additional fragment on a successful check, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) checks to assemble fragments into a complete relic.

entries.name: Explorers' League/Reliquary: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Faction}

If you spend 7 days studying the relics in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge or the Reliquary in Silvermoon City (or some other significant Explorers' League or Reliquary facility, at the DM's discretion) and then finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} there, you gain a {@book Charm|XDMG|2|Charms} that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. You can't gain another Charm from this feature while you still have one. The effect of the Charm depends on the origin of the relics you study; you can choose one of the following options:

items.name: {@reward Charm of Draenor|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know Draenei and Orcish. You can expend the Charm to cast {@spell Conjure Minor Elementals|XPHB}.

items.name: {@reward Charm of Pandaria|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know the Pandaren language. You can expend the Charm to cast {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB}, targeting yourself. The effect lasts for 1 hour or until you end the effect as a Bonus Action.

items.name: {@reward Charm of the Burning Legion|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know the Eredun language. You can expend the Charm to cast {@spell Rain of Fire|WoW} (level 4 version).

items.name: {@reward Charm of the Highborne|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know Thalassian. You can expend the Charm to cast {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB}.

items.name: {@reward Charm of the Old Gods|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know Shath'Yar. You can expend the Charm to cast {@spell Summon Aberration|XPHB}.

items.name: {@reward Charm of the Titan-Forged|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know Titan. You can expend the Charm to gain Resistance to all damage for 1 minute as your flesh takes on a mineral appearance.

items.name: {@reward Charm of the Zandalari|WoW}
items.entry: While you have this Charm, you know Zandali. You can expend the Charm to cast {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB} (level 4 version). The summoned {@creature Bestial Spirit|XPHB} resembles a loa.

entries.name: Explorers' League/Reliquary: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Faction}

You can request the use of a powerful magic item stored in your organization's vaults to assist you for a single adventure that is relevant to your organization's interests and aims. It takes 7 days for top agents in your organization to retrieve the item, which can be any Legendary magic item of your choice (subject to the DM's discretion). If the item isn't consumable, you must return it at the conclusion of the adventure, or your Renown Score decreases by {@dice 2d12}. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with your organization increases.

entries.name: Mutually Hostile Factions
entries: {@i World of Warcraft} features many opposing factions that are so hostile to each other that any renown gain with one faction automatically results in a loss of renown with the other. The Explorers' League and the Reliquary were mutually hostile before they were forced to cooperate in exploring the Dragon Isles. Other examples include the Scryers and the Aldor of Shattrath City, as well as the Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar and the gorlock Oracles of Sholazar Basin. In situations like these, a character's Renown Score with a faction can drop below 0, which means members of that faction are {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to the character by default.

entries.name: Kirin Tor

entries.title: Archmage Khadgar of the Kirin Tor

entries: The Kirin Tor began as a secretive mages' guild within the Empire of Arathor, the first great human civilization of the Eastern Kingdoms. Viewed with suspicion by much of the populace, the mages of Arathor secluded themselves in their own city, Dalaran, which became a beacon to mages from across Azeroth. With the fall of Arathor, Dalaran became a nation in its own right, one of Arathor's seven successor kingdoms, and the Council of Six who led the Kirin Tor became the rulers of this city-state. Razed during the Third War, Dalaran was rebuilt behind powerful warding spells and later transformed into a flying island that could be relocated to safety when needed. From its original site in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Dalaran moved first to Northrend's Crystalsong Forest, then above Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, then to the Broken Isles, then above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar. There it met its doom at the hands of Xal'atath's forces of the Void, but the survivors of the Kirin Tor remain in Dornogal, coordinating the magical defense of Azeroth.

The Council of Six, the leadership of the Kirin Tor, is made up of the most senior members of the Kirin Tor. Its leaders have included Archmage Rhonin, who oversaw the rebuilding of Dalaran after the Third War, Lady {@creature Jaina Proudmoore|WoW}, and Archmage Khadgar, who was imprisoned by Xal'atath just before Dalaran's destruction. The Kirin Tor is generally Lawful Neutral in alignment.
Adopting the {@class Mage|WoW} class, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character's Renown Score with the Kirin Tor by 3.

entries.name: Kirin Tor Renown Perks
entries: Establishing your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} in Dalaran increases your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Kirin Tor: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Kirin Tor}
You can enjoy a {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Lifestyle Expenses} lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost. You can also request a favor from the archmages of the Kirin Tor, which can take one of the following forms:

items: An archmage casts for you a spell of level 3 or lower at half the usual cost.
An archmage provides you with a Common or Uncommon magic item from the {@book Arcana tables|XDMG|6|Arcana Tables} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} at half the usual cost.

An archmage spends 30 days teaching you, so you learn a language from the {@area tables in chapter 2|17f|x} or gain proficiency with a tool (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries: You can request such a favor a number of times equal to your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor. If your Renown Score falls below the number of favors you have requested, a higher-ranking member of the Kirin Tor might call in a favor from you, sending you on a mission for the organization.

entries.name: Kirin Tor: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Kirin Tor}
You can enjoy a {@book Comfortable|XPHB|6|Lifestyle Expenses} lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost.
If your Bastion is in Dalaran, when you issue the Maintain order to your Bastion, the DM rolls twice on the {@table Bastion Events|XDMG|Bastion Events table} and you can pick which event occurs.
In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor (see "{@area Kirin Tor: Friendly|310|x}"), it can take one of the following additional forms:

items: An archmage casts for you a spell of level 4 or lower at half the usual cost.
An archmage provides you with a Rare magic item from the {@book Arcana tables|XDMG|6|Arcana Tables} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} at half the usual cost.
Whenever you take a Bastion turn, you can issue the Research order to the Kirin Tor as if it were a {@facility Library|XDMG} facility in your Bastion.

entries.name: Kirin Tor: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Kirin Tor}
You can enjoy a {@book Wealthy|XPHB|6|Lifestyle Expenses} lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost.
In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor (see "{@area Kirin Tor: Friendly|310|x}"), it can take one of the following additional forms:

items: An archmage casts for you a spell of level 6 or lower at half the usual cost.
An archmage provides you with a Very Rare magic item from the {@book Arcana tables|XDMG|6|Arcana Tables} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} at half the usual cost.
Whenever you take a Bastion turn, you can issue the Craft order to the Kirin Tor as if it were a {@facility Scriptorium|XDMG} facility in your Bastion.

entries.name: Kirin Tor: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Kirin Tor}
You can enjoy an {@book Aristocratic|XPHB|6|Lifestyle Expenses} lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost.
In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor (see "{@area Kirin Tor: Friendly|310|x}"), it can take one of the following additional forms:

items: An archmage casts for you a spell of level 8 or lower at half the usual cost.
An archmage provides you with a Legendary magic item from the {@book Arcana tables|XDMG|6|Arcana Tables} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} at half the usual cost.
When you craft a magic item, two Kirin Tor apprentices assist you, reducing the time required to craft the item accordingly.

entries.name: Steamwheedle Cartel
entries: The Steamwheedle Cartel is one of the largest and richest goblin cartels, having maintained a careful neutrality in the conflict between the Alliance and the Horde since the Second War (and a generally Neutral alignment). From its headquarters in Gadgetzan (in Tanaris), the cartel oversees operations across Azeroth and even Outland. It also runs Booty Bay (in Stranglethorn), Ratchet (in the Northern Barrens), and Everlook (in Winterspring), as well as smaller outposts. The cartel's hands are in virtually every line of work, with a specialty in premium-grade alchemy (at least since the alchemist Marin Noggenfogger assumed the position of trade prince). Besides potions, the cartel also deals in fuels, poisons, and industrial chemicals—what some goblins describe as "liquid assets."

entries.name: Steamwheedle Cartel Renown Perks
entries: Establishing your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} in Gadgetzan or another Steamwheedle Cartel territory increases your Renown Score with the Steamwheedle Cartel by 1.

Increasing your Renown Score with the Steamwheedle Cartel gives you the following additional benefits. (Steamwheedle Cartel merchants appear in many locations across the world, making their discounts particularly notable.)

entries.name: Steamwheedle Cartel: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel}

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Goblin language or gain proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Steamwheedle Cartel: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel}

You can request a supply of {@dice 1d4} flasks of {@item Noggenfogger Elixir|WoW} from the leaders of the cartel before you undertake a quest on their behalf. Once you request these elixirs, you can't do so again until your Renown Score with the cartel increases.

entries.name: Steamwheedle Cartel: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel}
You can purchase an {@item Experimental Goblin Jetpack|WoW} from the Steamwheedle Cartel for 2,000 GP (with no further discount).

entries.name: Steamwheedle Cartel: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel}
You can purchase a {@item Steamwheedle Apparatus|WoW} (which functions as an {@item Apparatus of Kwalish|XDMG}) from the Steamwheedle Cartel for 100,000 GP (with no further discount).

entries.name: Valdrakken Accord
entries: The Valdrakken Accord is the unified might of all dragonkind, seeking to protect not only the Dragon Isles but all of Azeroth according to the ancient charge given to the five Dragon Aspects (see {@area chapter 6|3dc|x}). The accord has also expanded its mission to include dragons beyond the five flights—in particular those who follow Vyranoth, who has been empowered as the Aspect of Storms.

The mission of the Dragon Aspects means that what is good for dragonkind is generally beneficial for all of Azeroth. The dragons oppose the Burning Legion, the lingering forces of the Old Gods and elementals they have corrupted, the remnants of the Scourge, the powers of the Void, and any other force that might threaten Azeroth and its inhabitants. That said, working with the dragons means viewing the world's conflicts from their perspective (which is generally Neutral) and solving problems their way.

The leaders of the Valdrakken Accord are the six Dragon Aspects: Alexstrasza, Nozdormu, Kalecgos, Merithra, Ebyssian, and Vyranoth. Their base of operations is the city of Valdrakken in the Dragon Isles.
Before the Dragon Isles reappeared, the Wyrmrest Accord carried out a similar mission but without the black dragonflight.

entries.name: Valdrakken Accord Renown Perks
entries: Establishing your {@book Bastion|XDMG|10} in Valdrakken or elsewhere in the Dragon Isles increases your Renown Score with the Valdrakken Accord by 1.
Increasing your Renown Score with the Valdrakken Accord gives you the following additional benefits.

entries.name: Valdrakken Accord: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Valdrakken Accord}
You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Draconic (see the "{@area Training|299|x}" sidebar earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Valdrakken Accord: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Valdrakken Accord}

You receive the {@reward Blessing of the Proto-Whelp|WoW}. This {@book Blessing|XDMG|2|Blessings} allows you to cast {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} with no Material components. When you cast the spell in this way, your familiar is a crimson proto-whelp ({@creature Pseudodragon|XMM}). Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You lose the Blessing and your proto-whelp familiar vanishes if your Renown Score with the Valdrakken Accord falls below 10.

Also, if you establish your Bastion in the Dragon Isles, it includes a {@facility Garden|XDMG} special facility. This facility doesn't count toward the total number of special facilities in your Bastion. The hireling departs and the facility becomes unusable if your Renown Score with Valdrakken Accord falls below 10.

entries.name: Valdrakken Accord: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Valdrakken Accord}

The Valdrakken Accord grants you the title Ally of Dragons. Dragons are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you by default unless they are corrupted. You can petition one of the Dragon Aspects for a favor, which takes the form of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell. Once you are granted such a favor, you can't ask for another one, even if your Renown Score falls below 50 and later reaches 50 again.

data.name: Chapter 5: The World of Warcraft

entries.title: Illidan Stormrage schemes before the Dark Portal.

entries: The planet called Azeroth floats through the Material Plane—what its scholars call the Great Dark Beyond. This plane of existence, the physical universe, is an infinite living realm composed of innumerable stars, worlds, and mortal civilizations. Some worlds, like Azeroth, have souls, and the titans believe that these Worldsouls, properly nourished, will eventually develop into more titans.

The Twisting Nether is how sages of Azeroth refer to the Wildspace of the Astral Plane: a parallel dimension to the Great Dark Beyond, defined by perpetual strife between the cosmic forces of Light and Shadow. At times, the volatile magic that pervades the Twisting Nether intrudes on the physical universe, warping reality beyond measure.

entries.name: The Cosmic Forces
entries: Beyond the Great Dark Beyond and the Twisting Nether, various cosmic forces inhabit their own extradimensional realms. The conflicts among these forces shape the nature of reality on the Material Plane. These forces include both elemental substance and spiritual energy—comparable to the influence of the {@book Inner and Outer Planes|XDMG|5|The Planes} described in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}—and they are best understood as pairs or groups of oppositional forces.

entries.name: Light and Shadow
entries: Light and Shadow are fundamental forces. Although contradictory by nature, they are bound together on a cosmic scale; neither can exist without the other. Pure Light and Shadow dwell in realms outside the borders of reality, but manifestations of their presence are found in the physical universe. Light manifests as holy magic, while Shadow (also referred to as "the Void") appears as shadow magic.

entries.name: Naaru
entries: The naaru are benevolent creatures of living holy energy. They are perhaps the purest expression of the Light that exists in the Great Dark Beyond. The naaru have vowed to bring peace and hope to all mortal civilizations and waylay the forces of the Void that seek to engulf creation.

entries.name: Church of the Holy Light
entries: In the wake of a devastating war against the trolls of the Amani Empire millennia ago, a group of humans received visions of strange angelic beings who introduced them to the Light. These beings were the naaru, and these encounters led to the foundation of the religion that commands the loyalty of most humans on Azeroth: the Church of the Holy Light. This faith was codified in a series of holy texts, teaching the three virtues of respect, tenacity, and compassion, based on the idea that the Light dwells in all living things.
Since its founding, the faith of the Holy Light has spread to the high elves of Quel'Thalas and the dwarves of Khaz Modan.

entries.name: Void Lords
entries: The void lords are monstrous entities composed of pure Shadow energy. These beings are cruel and merciless beyond mortal comprehension. Driven by an insatiable hunger, the void lords seek to devour all matter and energy in the physical universe.

In their natural state, the void lords exist outside reality. Only the most powerful of these entities can manifest in the physical universe, and only for limited amounts of time. To maintain their presence in reality, the void lords must consume untold amounts of matter and energy.

entries.name: Old Gods
entries: The Old Gods are physical manifestations of the Void. They are nightmares incarnate: mountains of blighted flesh and writhing tentacles that grow like cancers within the worlds of the Great Dark Beyond. These malignant entities serve the void lords by transforming the worlds they infest into places of despair and death. The Old Gods are detailed in {@area chapter 6|3f9|x}.

entries.name: Twilight's Hammer
entries: Twilight's Hammer is a cult that reveres the Old Gods and seeks to bring about the end of the world. It has been active since before the First War, but it grew to particular prominence amid the cataclysmic events surrounding the return of Deathwing.

entries.name: Life and Death
entries: The forces of Life and Death hold sway over every living thing in the physical universe. The energies of Life, known commonly as nature magic, promote growth and renewal. Death, in the form of necromantic magic, breeds despair in mortal hearts and pushes everything toward a state of entropic decay and eventual oblivion.

entries.name: Elune
entries: Elune, called the Mother Moon and the Night Warrior, is the primary deity of the night elves of Kalimdor. Tauren also revere her as Mu'sha, the left eye of the Earth Mother. Mu'sha's twin, An'she, is the right eye (the sun), a force of Light.

entries.name: Wild Gods
entries: Wild Gods are primal manifestations of Life and nature. They are creatures of two realms, inhabiting the physical world of Azeroth while their spirits are bound to the ethereal Emerald Dream. Many Wild Gods appear in the form of enormous animals, such as wolves, bears, tigers, or birds.

entries.name: Eternal Ones
entries: The Eternal Ones, who rule the afterlife realms of the Shadowlands, are incarnations of the cosmic force of Death, and they're sometimes known as the Pantheon of Death (in contrast to the titans of the Pantheon of Order, described below).

entries.name: Order and Disorder
entries: The forces of Order and Disorder govern the cosmic systems of the universe. Order is most commonly perceived as arcane magic. This type of energy is intensely volatile, and wielding it requires precision and concentration.

Disorder manifests as highly destructive fel magic. This brutal and addictive energy is fueled by drawing life from living beings. The Burning Legion (described in {@area chapter 6|3d2|x}) is the ultimate expression of Disorder in the physical world.

entries.name: The Pantheon
entries: Titans are colossal, godlike beings of Order, composed of the primordial matter from which the universe was born.

A group of titans called the Pantheon (or the Pantheon of Order) roam the cosmos, imbued with the raw power of creation. The titans use this incredible force to find and awaken others of their kind who still slumber, in the form of Worldsouls, among the many worlds of the Great Dark. These titans created the keepers, lesser but still godlike beings who shaped and ordered Azeroth, created the other titan-forged, and empowered the Dragon Aspects.
The original pantheon included seven titans, all but one of whom imbued one or more keepers with their likeness and power:
{@b Aman'Thul}, Highfather of the Pantheon, has mastery over time magic. His keepers are Odyn and Ra.
{@b Eonar} the Life-Binder is the protector of life, nature, and health. Her keeper is Freya.
{@b Golganneth} the Thunderer is the lord of the skies and oceans. His keepers are Hodir and Thorim.
{@b Khaz'goroth}, the Shaper and Forger of Worlds, is the ultimate artisan and guardian of the deep places of the world. His keeper is Archaedas.
{@b Norgannon}, known as Keeper of Celestial Magic and Lore, is the master of all magic, knowledge, secrets, and mysteries. His keepers are Loken and Mimiron.

{@b Sargeras}, known first as the Defender and then as the Destroyer, was the champion of the Pantheon until he decided that the only way to prevent the void lords from corrupting a Worldsoul and making titans of their own was to destroy the cosmos and start creation over again. To that end, he created the Burning Legion (see {@area chapter 6|3d2|x}).
{@b Aggramar}, the Avenger, was the lieutenant of Sargeras and inherited his role as champion of the Pantheon. He is charged with combating the Burning Legion. His keeper is Tyr.

entries.name: The Elements
entries: The elements of air, earth, fire, and water serve as the basic building blocks of all matter in the universe. {@class Shaman|WoW} call on the primordial forces of Spirit and Decay to attain power over the elements. Those who seek to bring balance to the elements rely on Spirit (sometimes referred to as the "fifth element" by shaman). This life-giving force interconnects and binds all things in existence as one. Decay is the tool of shaman seeking to subjugate and weaponize the elements.

entries.name: Elemental Spirits
entries: Elemental spirits are wild and chaotic beings of air, earth, fire, or water. They were among the first sentient creatures to inhabit the nascent worlds of the waking universe. They appear in an almost infinite variety of shapes and sizes, with personalities and temperaments strongly influenced by the spirit's elemental nature. The mightiest of these elemental spirits are the elemental lords, described in more detail in {@area chapter 6|3eb|x}.

entries.name: World of Azeroth
entries: Azeroth is a realm not merely shaped by war, but defined by it. No region, no nation, arguably not one contiguous square mile has escaped it. Wars have raged through all the ages.

When modern citizens of Azeroth contemplate war, most think first of the long-running conflict between the Alliance and the Horde. This struggle is the cause of three of the great wars of modern history. Yet the Alliance–Horde struggle is but one of many conflicts: tribe against tribe, nation against nation, mortals against demons, mantid versus pandaren, naga incursions against land dwellers, the forces of nature against corruptions of the {@area Old Gods|3f9|x}.

This dreadful cycle has raged at least ten millennia, since the Highborne night elves drew the cosmic eye of Sargeras the Destroyer because of their exorbitant use of the Well of Eternity. The corrupted titan gathered countless demons he had imprisoned in Mardum, the Plane of Banishment, and unleashed them on Azeroth as the {@area Burning Legion|3d2|x}.

This War of the Ancients wreaked untold destruction and led to the devastation of the Great Sundering. Continents shattered and land sank into the oceans, reshaping coastlines. The Well of Eternity was destroyed and became the Great Sea's all-consuming Maelstrom.
In those grim days, extinction loomed, and the seeds of most of Azeroth's subsequent rivalries and hatreds were planted.
The world has been at war ever since.

Yet Azeroth is more than just a giant battlefield. In villages, cities, and towns, people work, worship, celebrate, and love. Natural wonders from vast forests to lush grasslands stretch between mountain and river, hill and sea.

Life thrives and civilization endures. Secret magic and lost technologies wait to be rediscovered in the deepest dungeons—marvels that, depending on who finds them first, could improve lives or end them en masse. Villains and monsters, many unrelated to the ongoing wars, threaten the innocent.
Azeroth is a world that might never lose its need for soldiers, but more than that, it needs heroes.

entries.name: Alliance and Horde
entries: An armistice has held the Alliance and the Horde in a semblance of peace since the end of the Fourth War. Yet their conflict continues through scattered skirmishes on a hundred fronts—even in regions that largely stayed outside this terrible struggle.

Some areas are under the control of one faction or the other, and members of the opposing faction are unwelcome. Most areas are contested—both factions have a presence, and open conflict sometimes erupts there. A few neutral places welcome members of both factions and frown on conflict. The druidic territory of Moonglade (in Kalimdor) is a prime example of a neutral territory; druids set aside their factional differences to learn and commune with nature together in this tranquil valley.

entries.name: Adventures in Azeroth
entries: The many regions of Azeroth contain ample opportunities for adventure. Some locations merit special attention due to their historic, cultural, or mystical significance.

Several of the regions covered in this chapter list such locations. A few are detailed substantially in chapter 6 and are referenced here only briefly. The summaries of other sites offer an understanding of what the dungeon or adventure site is and why it's important. DMs can use these descriptions as springboards for expansion and development.

entries.title: Orgrimmar is the capital of Durotar and a safe haven for the Horde.

entries.name: Zone Progression
entries: In early versions of {@i World of Warcraft}, characters often followed a predictable path through the world as they advanced in level, entering more dangerous regions as their power increased. While that strict progression is no longer in place, some parts of the world are still more dangerous than others—and regions on other worlds and planes are more dangerous still. Thus, each region's description in this chapter includes a parenthetical notation of the tier of play (1–4, 5–10, 11–16, 17–20, or endgame) during which it's most appropriate for characters to adventure in that region. DMs can use this information along with the conflict arcs in {@book chapter 6|WoW|6} to decide where in the vast world of Azeroth their adventures will unfold—or DMs can ignore it entirely and let the players decide where their characters will roam.

entries.name: Kalimdor
entries: Kalimdor is the broken western remnant of the much larger continent of the same name that was torn apart during the Great Sundering. It still bears the scars of that ancient catastrophe and the more recent Cataclysm wrought by Deathwing.

The northern forests and mountains of Kalimdor bear the imprint of thousands of years of night elf civilization. Night elves built majestic cities before the War of the Ancients, and the ruins of cities such as Mathystra, Ameth'Aran, Ordil'Aran, and Kel'Theril still remain.

Night elves zealously defend the portions of Northern Kalimdor they still hold, as this is the heart of their former empire and the home of the World Trees. The night elves joined the Alliance to face the Horde, but a significant minority consider both factions equally distasteful.

They maintain that their home territories belong to the night elves alone; {@race Human|WoW|humans}, {@area furbolgs|4dd|x}, and {@race draenei|WoW} are no more welcome than {@race Orc|WoW|orcs}, {@race Troll|WoW|trolls}, or {@race Goblin|WoW|goblins}. Some of these night elves keep to themselves, but others wage a guerrilla insurgency against all other groups, adding more uncertainty to areas torn by struggles between the Alliance and the Horde.

Southern Kalimdor is a blasted and broken land that bears the scars of the Cataclysm, the failed experiments of titans, the castoffs of the Old Gods, and the ruins of empires older than the night elf civilization to the north. From flooded chasms to baking deserts, it is a place of misery, want, and ancient death, with only a few stretches of verdant forest or savanna in which life can thrive.

A defining feature of Southern Kalimdor is the remnant of the ancient qiraji empire. Fallen spires, broken towers, and sand-buried avenues are testaments to an empire formed by the the insectile qiraji, who were corrupted by the influence of the imprisoned Old God C'Thun. By accessing the prison-laboratory of the titans, the qiraji learned secrets now buried with the rest of their nation.

entries.title: Devilsaurs are among the most dangerous predators of Un'Goro Crater.

entries.name: Kalimdor Regions
entries: Kalimdor stretches from the charred remains of Teldrassil in the northwest, across the Great Divide that cuts across the Barrens, and down to the southern tip of Uldum.

entries.name: Ahn'Qiraj
entries: Ahn'Qiraj, the fallen kingdom of the insectile qiraji, is a wasted ruin older than most civilizations, still containing ancient horrors linked to the Old Gods. (Contested; 17–20)

entries.name: Ashenvale
entries: Tensions between {@race Elf|WoW|night elves} in the north and west and Horde loggers in the south and east have long defined the lush forest of Ashenvale. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Azshara
entries: Azshara is a region cloaked in eternal autumn, stalked by naga, and haunted by ghosts. It has been partially pacified by Bilgewater Cartel {@race Goblin|WoW|goblins}. (Horde; 5–10)

entries.name: Azuremyst Isles
entries: Consisting of Azuremyst Isle and the neighboring Bloodmyst Isle, the Azuremyst Isles have been under the uncontested control of the {@race draenei|WoW} since their arrival in the Exodar. Bloodmyst Isle, though, is polluted by an arcane red mist that chokes the land and causes dangerous mutations of local fauna. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Darkshore
entries: The shadow-choked strip of coastline called Darkshore is littered with the monster-occupied ruins of ancient night elf fortifications as well as recent battlefields. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Desolace
entries: Having grown increasingly green and fertile since the climate-altering effects of the Cataclysm, the former wasteland of Desolace is now the site of constant struggle between the Alliance, the Horde, the Burning Blade, the Cenarion Circle, and multiple centaur tribes. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Durotar
entries: Durotar is a harsh region of dusty badlands, deep canyons, flooding rivers, and vicious predators. It is also the new homeland of the {@race Orc|WoW|orcs} and a haven for all the Horde. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Dustwallow Marsh
entries: Neither the Alliance nor the Horde has made much headway in Dustwallow Marsh, a viciously inhospitable wetland. The Alliance holds a few outposts of the now obliterated Theramore Isle, and a few small communities such as Brackenwall Village and Mudsprocket support the Horde. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Felwood
entries: The corrupted forest of Felwood, full of infernally tainted elementals and rotting treants, stands between Alliance and Horde territories. It is a highly contested land; neither side wants it, but neither side can afford to cede it. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Feralas
entries: Deadly clans and communities of local inhabitants, of which the Gordunni ogres are the most numerous, prevent both the Alliance and the Horde from claiming much of the resource-rich Feralas jungle. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Moonglade
entries: {@area Cenarion Circle|2f9|x} druids and their powerful Moonglade Warden guards swiftly quash any sectarian violence that threatens the peace of the lush Moonglade vale. (Neutral; 11–16)

entries.name: Mount Hyjal
entries: Boasting the roots of the World Tree Nordrassil and the Second Well of Eternity beneath its peak, Mount Hyjal is frequently the target of countless factions, armies, and would-be warlords who desperately seek its power. (Contested; 17–20)

entries.name: Mulgore
entries: The game-rich grasslands of Mulgore are {@race tauren|WoW}'s ancestral home. While this area is relatively peaceful, it is also the home of dangerous beasts and the violent extremists of the Grimtotem tribe. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Northern Barrens
entries: The vast savanna of the Northern Barrens is now separated from the south by the lava-filled Great Divide. Horde warriors coming of age use this region to prove their readiness for battle. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Silithus
entries: Silithus is a blazing desert containing portions of lost Ahn'Qiraj. Despite dangers such as the all-consuming silithid, the allure of the mystical Silithyst crystal dust attracts the interest of Alliance, Horde, and independent explorers.

At the end of the Burning Legion's third invasion of Azeroth, Sargeras tried to destroy the world by plunging his enormous sword into the heart of the planet. He struck Silithus, creating a massive wound that now dominates the desert surrounding the titan's sword. The wound has caused the lifeblood of Azeroth to seep to the surface, not just in Silithus but across the world, in the form of a mineral called Azerite. Efforts to control the damage and heal the wound continue. {@i (Contested; 11–16)}

entries.name: Southern Barrens
entries: After the Southern Barrens were blasted by Deathwing and rocked by earthquakes during the Cataclysm, many local Horde strongholds were lost or abandoned. The Alliance has since launched multiple incursions into this ill-defended region. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Stonetalon Mountains
entries: The slopes of the Stonetalon Mountains are home to fortified outposts of the Alliance and the Horde. Stonetalon Peak houses caverns sacred to tauren and night elves who, despite their allegiance to opposing factions, avoid shedding blood on holy ground. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Tanaris
entries: The desert of Tanaris is haunted by many of the same monsters as Silithus, but it also serves as home to the Steamwheedle Cartel goblins in communities such as Steamwheedle Port and Gadgetzan. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Teldrassil
entries: Formerly one of the great World Trees, Teldrassil was burned during the War of Thorns. Night elves work to restore life to its charred remnants and rebuild the community it once held. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Thousand Needles
entries: Countless stone spires and small mesas rise from the waters of a massive flooded canyon, giving the Thousand Needles region its name. Many of these islets host camps and small communities that must deal with pirates and dangerous fauna. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Uldum
entries: The wastes of Uldum, which link the larger deserts of Silithus and Tanaris, are home to the feline tol'vir—and to uncounted creations and weapons of the ancient titans. (Contested; 17–20)

entries.name: Un'Goro Crater
entries: Full of surprisingly lush greenery considering its position amid great deserts, Un'Goro Crater might have served as both home and laboratory for the titans. Its strange creatures and alien magic lend credence to that idea. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Winterspring
entries: The snowy vale of Winterspring—one lair of the {@area blue dragonflight|4cf|x}, which watches over the flow of magic—sees frequent conflict between goblin trading posts and night elves working to reclaim their ancient fortifications. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Alliance and Horde in Kalimdor
entries: Judging solely by the size of claimed territories, Kalimdor would seem solidly Horde aligned. The Bilgewater goblins dominate Azshara. Durotar is held by the orcs, and Orgrimmar serves as the capital of both the orcs and the Horde. The Mulgore plains, ancestral birthplace of the tauren and now populated by countless tribes, anchor the Horde's claims in the southern part of the continent. Whether they're from cities such as the tauren capital of Thunder Bluff or wandering nomadic bands, even peace-loving tauren are quick to arms when it comes to defending their communities.

Compared to those bastions, the territories of the Alliance are minuscule. Yet small doesn't equal unimportant. Kalimdor is the ancestral home of the night elves, whose bonds to these lands are historical, cultural, and spiritual. The draenei are equally bound to and fortified within the Azuremyst Isles, where they first arrived on the world of Azeroth. The night elves and draenei fanatically defend their homelands, and their willingness to battle over neighboring territories has long prevented the Horde from cementing control over all Kalimdor.

Perhaps the fiercest conflicts occur in the forests of Ashenvale and Felwood, which stand directly between Alliance and Horde strongholds. The factions skirmish in Ashenvale over territory and its rich lumber and herbal resources. On the other hand, nobody wants the toxic and monster-ravaged Felwood, but its strategic location means neither side can allow the other to claim it.

While the Northern Barrens are firmly Horde territory on paper, guarding the large and open area is a logistical nightmare. Alliance scouting parties regularly slip into the Barrens to spy on or sabotage Horde endeavors. These missions become bloody when Alliance teams encounter inexperienced Horde warriors training on the proving grounds. Eliminating bands of soldiers is a tempting and strategically sound objective for Alliance teams.

Across the southern reaches of Kalimdor, the Alliance and the Horde maintain strongholds in scattered outposts, towns, and small cities, all of which stand in contested territories. None of these strongholds are secure enough to consider themselves safe, let alone to serve as a launching point for wider conquest.

Given the dangers that haunt Kalimdor, neither the Alliance nor the Horde would likely bother trying to expand its grasp were it not for the ancient magic and other secrets so prevalent in the region. The Alliance regularly lands military forces on the coasts of the Great Sea, hoping to overwhelm—or at least bypass—existing Horde strongholds and acquire those mystical or mysterious wonders.

entries.name: Kalimdor Adventures
entries: The adventure sites of Kalimdor range from cultural and holy places of lost or fallen cultures to hidden repositories of the most ancient powers of Azeroth.

entries.name: Blackfathom Deeps
entries: The dungeon of Blackfathom Deeps, located on the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, is detailed in {@area chapter 6|425|x}.

entries.name: Dire Maul
entries: Formerly the Highborne elven city of Eldre'Thalas, the vast ruin known as Dire Maul is overrun by ogres, undead, and satyrs. It is detailed in {@area chapter 6|459|x}.

entries.name: Maraudon
entries: Maraudon is a combination of elemental temple and centaur burial ground located within the Valley of Spears in Desolace. Giants, oozes, and demons roam the tunnels of this sprawling complex, as do centaur ghosts and corrupted dryads.

entries.name: Master's Glaive
entries: Deep in the wilds of southwestern Darkshore, a colossal adamantine blade protrudes from the near-fossilized remains of a grotesque, tentacled aberration. The Master's Glaive was the weapon of Kronn, the only survivor of a band of twenty giant soldiers sent by the titans to battle Soggoth the Slitherer, herald of the Old Gods. Kronn might have left his weapon in Soggoth's corpse as a symbol of victory, or perhaps because he was so greatly wounded that he lacked the strength to retrieve it. Many believe the blade's presence prevents Soggoth from reawakening. The area is occupied by Twilight's Hammer, a nihilistic sect that seeks to revive the Slitherer—and then the Old Gods.

entries.name: Onyxia's Lair
entries: The lair of the black dragonflight's broodmother, Onyxia, is located in Dustwallow Marsh and detailed in {@area chapter 6|491|x}.

entries.name: Ragefire Chasm
entries: Ragefire Chasm is a cleft within the city of Orgrimmar. Despite its location in the heart of the city, it has long served as a hideout for cultists—first demonic cultists of the Burning Blade clan, and later a group called the Dark Shaman, made up of former members of Twilight's Hammer after the cult's fall.

entries.name: Ruins of Theramore
entries: Once a great fortified city and the Alliance's mightiest stronghold in Southern Kalimdor, Theramore is now a blasted ruin. Destroyed by an incomprehensibly powerful mana bomb, the city is slowly being reclaimed by the Dustwallow Marsh. Salvagers of the Alliance and the Horde, as well as independent adventurers, scout partially standing buildings and any accessible underground chambers, hoping to recover weapons, goods, and treasures of old. In addition to the threats posed by rival scavengers, those who trespass on this mass grave also face ghosts and small cults and sects that maintain secret hideouts in the ruins.
{@b Temple of Ahn'Qiraj}. The ancient, sprawling Temple of Ahn'Qiraj is home to alien qiraji emperors and their secrets.

entries.name: Tower of Althalaxx
entries: In the distant past, the Tower of Althalaxx was the home of Athrikus Narassin, faithful vassal of the night elf Queen Azshara. Years of boredom and stunted ambition led Athrikus astray, and many millennia after he vanished, he reappeared as the leader of the Cult of the Dark Strand, an offshoot of the demon-worshipping Shadow Council. Athrikus was eventually defeated and his home partly burned, but the remnants of Althalaxx still attract scavengers, researchers, and adventurers. The warlock's fiendish research and the Soul Gems that empowered him—still containing the spirits of trapped Highborne night elves—are rumored to lie deep within the spirit-haunted ruins.

entries.name: Wailing Caverns
entries: The corrupted Druids of the Fang dwell in a complex network of underground chambers and defiled waters called the Wailing Caverns in the Northern Barrens. These night elf druids came to the caverns imagining that they could connect the waters inside to the Emerald Dream to restore life and growth to the Barrens, but once inside they succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare. Corruption spread through the waters and twisted the druids into serpent cultists.

entries.name: Zul'Farrak
entries: Once the adobe-walled city of the Sandfury trolls in northwestern Tanaris, Zul'Farrak was slowly whittled away by the encroaching desert and constant war. Since the Cataclysm, it has been a sun-blasted ruin, half buried in the sands. While the surviving trolls have moved on, the ruined city isn't wholly abandoned. The population of warbeasts formerly kept by the Sandfury has grown out of control, hives of silithid have moved in, and undead trolls lurk in the city's deepest levels. These threats, and strange magic worked by Sandfury occultists, remain to be discovered by adventurers.

entries.name: Eastern Kingdoms

entries.title: The former capital of Lordaeron, transformed into Undercity, is a bastion of the Forsaken.

entries: The Eastern Kingdoms is the eastern remnant of the ancient continent that broke apart in the Great Sundering. Before that catastrophe, these lands were held by the Amani and Gurubashi {@race troll|WoW} empires. In modern times, the Eastern Kingdoms have been the primary battlefield in the wars between the Alliance and the Horde, and the land still bears scars of those conflicts.

The northernmost portion of the Eastern Kingdoms, a distinct landmass called Lordaeron, was the seat of the {@race human|WoW}-led Empire of Arathor, which later fragmented into the Seven Kingdoms: Alterac, Dalaran, Gilneas, Lordaeron, Stromgarde, Kul Tiras (on an island to the southwest), and Stormwind (far to the south). These kingdoms existed in uneasy peace alongside the {@race Elf|WoW|high elves} of Quel'Thalas and the Wildhammer clan of {@race Dwarf|WoW|dwarves} in the Hinterlands until first the Horde and then the undead {@area Scourge|403|x} ravaged the entire region.

The southern part of the Eastern Kingdoms, dominated by the kingdom of Stormwind and the dwarf capital of Ironforge, also holds the Blasted Lands, the site of the Dark Portal where the Horde first entered the world.

entries.name: Eastern Kingdoms Regions
entries: The Eastern Kingdoms are made up of three landmasses:

items.name: Lordaeron
items.entry: Lordaeron in the north is divided from the rest of the Eastern Kingdoms by a narrow strait crossed by the magnificent Thandol Span, a feat of dwarvish engineering.

items.name: Khaz Modan
items.entry: Khaz Modan is the central part of the Eastern Kingdoms, encompassing the region from the Thandol Span in the north to Blackrock Mountain in the south.

items.name: Azeroth
items.entry: The southernmost region, stretching from Blackrock Mountain and the Burning Steppes in the north to the tip of the Cape of Stranglethorn in the south, is named Azeroth, but the name is more commonly used for the world as a whole.

entries: The regions that make up each of these landmasses are described below.

entries.name: Alterac Mountains
entries: Once home to a small but thriving {@race human|WoW} kingdom, the resource-rich Alterac Mountains are now locked in a struggle between the Crushridge ogre clan and the noble-led criminal organization known as the Syndicate. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Arathi Highlands
entries: The great strongholds of both the Alliance (Stromgarde Keep in the west) and the Horde (Hammerfall in the east) in the Arathi Highlands hold a tentative peace, one that extremists on both sides strive to sabotage. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Badlands
entries: The blasted and inhospitable expanse of the Badlands is claimed by both the Alliance and the Horde but is controlled by neither. It is home to fearsome beasts, savage troggs, and members of the {@area black dragonflight|4ca|x}. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Blasted Lands
entries: Scorched and devastated by the magic surrounding the appearance, destruction, and reappearance of the Dark Portal, the Blasted Lands are full of wandering beasts native to multiple worlds and timelines. Alliance and Horde teams occupy small outposts, ever watchful for further incursions. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Burning Steppes
entries: Land traffic from the southern regions to Dun Morogh and points north must traverse the mountain passes and jagged badlands of the Burning Steppes. Dark Iron dwarves, reinforced by soldiers from Stormwind, help keep travelers safe from marauding orcs of the independent Blackrock clan. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Deadwind Pass
entries: Horde invaders from Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows occasionally attempt to take sections of Deadwind Pass. Greater threats in this gray, rotting, and haunted reach, however, are the Nightbane worgen, Deadwind ogres, and armies of ghosts. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Dun Morogh
entries: The snowcapped forested mountains of Dun Morogh are the center of two major Alliance cultures, housing the {@race Dwarf|WoW|dwarves}' capital, Ironforge, and the war-torn, catastrophe-shattered city of Gnomeregan. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Duskwood
entries: Duskwood has been cursed to a twisted darkness and suffers the depredations of undead and other bloodthirsty creatures. Its many inhabitants cling defiantly to their homes and their fealty to Stormwind. (Alliance; 5–10)

entries.title: Stormwind City celebrates the victories of the Alliance.

entries.name: Elwynn Forest
entries: The communities of the lush hardwood Elwynn Forest—such as Goldshire and Stormwind City—are the heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind and modern human culture. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Eversong Woods
entries: The Eversong Woods—ancestral home of the {@race Elf|WoW|blood elves}—enjoy a near-perpetual spring. But portions of the forest are still scarred by the Scourge and suffer the constant rise of undead. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Ghostlands
entries: In the Ghostlands, a portion of the Eversong Forest never reclaimed by the blood elves, the undead blight is widespread. The dangerous Amani tribe of forest trolls also maintains a stronghold in the region. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Hillsbrad Foothills
entries: Although largely under {@race Forsaken|WoW} control, the Hillsbrad Foothills and surrounding plains see many of the bloodiest and most frequent battles between the Alliance and the Horde, rendering any claim over the area tentative at best. (Horde; 5–10)

entries.name: Hinterlands
entries: The mountainous Hinterlands are home of the Wildhammer dwarves and their famous trained gryphons. This region sees a constant back-and-forth between the Wildhammer dwarves and high elves on one side and Forsaken and Revantusk trolls on the other. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Loch Modan
entries: Drained during the Cataclysm, the dry lake bed of Loch Modan and its fertile surroundings remain under dwarves' control despite constant threats of troggs, kobolds, and Mo'grosh ogres. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Plaguelands
entries: The aptly named Plaguelands were badly infested by {@area the Scourge|403|x}, resulting in a region of constantly rising undead. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Quel'Danas
entries: The forested isle called Quel'Danas contains the Sunwell, a source of arcane and Light energy sacred to the blood elves. Its tremendous magical power makes it an attractive target to forces both mortal and demonic. (Contested; 17–20)

entries.name: Redridge Mountains
entries: The normally idyllic Redridge mountain range, home to many Stormwind communities, sees occasional raids from Blackrock orcs and the undead Scourge. (Alliance; 5–10)

entries.name: Ruins of Gilneas
entries: After many years of changing hands, the Ruins of Gilneas have been returned to the Alliance and the subjects of Queen Tess Greymane. Horde extremists still harry its streets in violation of the treaty, and scattered remnants of the Scarlet Crusade's occupation forces commit atrocities against both factions. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Searing Gorge
entries: Despite being blackened and broken by an ancient eruption and recent industrial pollution, the Searing Gorge is a constant target for the Horde, for through it runs the only viable passage between Khaz Modan and the southern part of the continent. The powerful Dark Iron dwarves live in the gorge. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Silverpine Forest
entries: The massive, primeval Silverpine Forest is silent and haunted, pockmarked with homesteads and hamlets abandoned in the struggle between the Forsaken in the north and desperate pockets of living resistance in the south. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Stranglethorn
entries: Stranglethorn is a patch of tropical jungle divided by a massive sinkhole. It boasts a wide variety of venomous flora and fauna, native trolls, and thriving communities of Blackwater Cartel pirates. (Contested; 5–10)

entries.name: Swamp of Sorrows
entries: Due to its proximity to the Dark Portal, the Swamp of Sorrows contains nearly as many Horde communities as it does Alliance. It is the site of some of the most frequent and largest faction battles fought on the subcontinent, even though it offers little in the way of desirable resources or terrain. (Contested; 11–16)

entries.name: Tirisfal Glades
entries: Green-skied and blight-tainted Tirisfal is a Forsaken stronghold, but the undead of the Horde are beleaguered by Scarlet Crusade soldiers and terrors of the Scourge. (Horde; 1–4)

entries.name: Tol Barad
entries: The desolate Tol Barad peninsula is home to the mystical prison of Baradin Hold, which is under the control of its powerful inmates. (Contested; 17–20)

entries.name: Twilight Highlands
entries: The Twilight Highlands are a boiling cauldron of conflict as the Wildhammer dwarves, the Dragonmaw orcs, the {@area red dragonflight|504|x}, a few lingering twilight dragons, and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult vie with one another for control over the region's fortresses and resources. (Contested; 17–20)

entries.name: Westfall
entries: Westfall was the site of much destruction across wars and catastrophes. It briefly broke away from Stormwind due to the costs of war. Strong economic assistance and renewed protection turned this fiefdom into the kingdom's breadbasket. (Alliance; 1–4)

entries.name: Wetlands
entries: The Alliance claims the cold, gray swamp of the Wetlands, primarily because of the useful port of Menethil Harbor. A small community of night elves, Greenwarden's Grove, and the dwarf-built fortresses of Dun Algaz and Dun Modr extend the Alliance claim over the eastern part of the swamp, but Dragonmaw orcs and a growing population of murlocs threaten the Alliance's hold. (Alliance; 5–10)

entries.name: Alliance and Horde in the Eastern Kingdoms
entries: The conflict between the Alliance and the Horde defines the modern history of the Eastern Kingdoms. After four wars, starting with the opening of the Dark Portal and continuing intermittently over the course of almost thirty-five years, the conflict has simmered down to a tenuous truce. The Horde's main power centers are the blood elf kingdom of Quel'Thalas in the north and the Ruins of Lordaeron, the new capital of the Forsaken. The Horde has only scattered holdings in the southern part of the region, with a few groups of orcs maintaining holdings in the Twilight Highlands, the Redridge Mountains, and the Swamp of Sorrows.

Gilneas is the only major Alliance holding in Lordaeron, but the Alliance is much stronger in the rest of the Eastern Kingdoms, with Ironforge, Stormwind, and Gnomeregan controlling most of the southern continent.

Despite the many horrors and indiscriminately violent groups that occupy the area—or perhaps because of them—Lordaeron has also witnessed some of the most significant strides toward peace between the Alliance and the Horde in the modern era. In the wake of {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW|Sylvanas's} departure from the Horde, the Desolate Council negotiated a peaceful turnover of the Ruins of Gilneas to the human and worgen subjects of Queen Tess Greymane, and King Danath Trollbane of Stromgarde signed treaties with Overlord Geya'rah of the Mag'har orcs. In both instances, this cooperation involves full military cooperation against shared enemies. The armies of Queen Tess and the Forsaken worked together to clear Scarlet Crusade intruders from the Ruins of Gilneas, while Danath and Geya'rah combine elements of the Kor'kron Guard and the 7th Legion into a single strike force to confront threats against both peoples.

Both situations are perilous, especially given that some members of each faction would love to see the peace fail. But if these partnerships can hold, they might provide an example of a better way forward for other factions of the Alliance and the Horde.

entries.name: Eastern Kingdoms Adventures

entries.title: The Wildhammer dwarves, based in the Hinterlands, are famous as gryphon trainers.

entries: Given the ravages of {@area the Scourge|403|x}, many key Lordaeron sites are haunted, necromantic, or otherwise connected to undeath. To the south, a wide variety of adventure sites are linked to disasters caused by the greed, pride, or fear of the people living nearby.

entries.name: Baradin Hold
entries: Originally an immense fort with potent mystical defenses, Baradin Hold was repurposed as a prison for the worst criminals and dangers Azeroth—and worlds beyond—had to offer. Today, it holds power-hungry archmages, possessed {@area Burning Legion|3d2|x} fanatics, and demons and entities from the deep Void. Baradin's Wardens have long since been driven off, leaving the inmates in control of the prison. While few adventurers would dare the halls of Baradin Hold, someone must travel there to ensure that the defenses still hold, that none of the inmates have escaped, and that no demon-worshipping or nihilistic factions are working to bring down the walls.

entries.name: Blackrock Mountain
entries: The many-layered dungeons beneath Blackrock Mountain include Shadowforge City, the capital of the Dark Iron dwarves; the Molten Core, where {@creature Ragnaros|WoW|Ragnaros the Firelord} enslaved those dwarves; and Blackrock Spire, where orcs, ogres, and trolls of the Dark Horde allied with the {@area black dragonflight|4ca|x} led by Nefarian.

entries.name: The Cauldron
entries: The massive dig site called the Cauldron is perhaps the greatest project of the Dark Iron dwarves. For much of its history, the Dark Iron clan forced prisoners to do much of the physical labor. The dwarves were taskmasters or drove mighty excavation machines. Since they rejoined other Alliance dwarven clans in the region, the Dark Iron dwarves have officially abandoned those practices, but some individuals and small companies refuse to alter their methods. Dark Iron dwarves employ adventurers to delve deep into the Cauldron's subsections to retrieve prisoners and punish those who still use them as slaves. The Cauldron is home to a variety of fire-related elemental creatures, and possibly ancient creations of the titans or the {@area Old Gods|3f9|x}.

entries.name: Dark Portal
entries: In the Blasted Lands, the orc warlock Gul'dan and the human Guardian of Tirisfal, Medivh, first opened the Dark Portal, allowing the orcs of the Old Horde to cross into Azeroth from the world of Draenor. All the struggle, bloodshed, anddevastation of the conflict between the Alliance and the Horde stem from this initial event.
The portal also led to further interplanar conflicts and invasions by linking parallel realities and alternate histories. The greatest wizards and sages aren't certain how the portal operates.

Although history provides substantial motivation for the Alliance, the Horde, and smaller factions to keep watch over the Dark Portal, the short span of mortal memory makes those observers few in number and unprepared for decisive action.

entries.name: Deadmines
entries: A sprawling set of underground gold mines extends beneath Westfall and northern Stranglethorn. Once a major source of Stormwind's wealth, the mines were abandoned during the First War and later thought to be haunted, so they went largely untouched until the brigands of the Defias Brotherhood established a base there. The Deadmines are detailed in {@area chapter 6|43c|x}.

entries.name: Gnomeregan
entries: Gassed and irradiated by a sabotaged effort at defending against trogg invasions, the gnomish kingdom of Gnomeregan was occupied by troggs and the so-called "leper gnomes" who had been mutated by the catastrophe. Today, the gnomes and their Alliance allies work to retake what was theirs. From New Tinkertown, a segment of Gnomeregan already reclaimed, they plan and launch missions into the depths of the many-layered community. Outside adventurers, whether employed by the gnomes or sneaking in as independent treasure hunters, can expect to confront troggs, leper gnomes, cunning traps of mixed technology and magic, and horrors born in the deeps.

entries.name: Karazhan
entries: Karazhan is the tower of Medivh, the Guardian responsible for the opening of the Dark Portal. The tower is rumored to hold numberless magical secrets and dangerous artifacts, as well as the haunt of countless ghosts and other evil spirits.

entries.name: Nethergarde Keep
entries: The great citadel and fortified town of Nethergarde Keep was constructed on a bluff overlooking the main road through the Blasted Lands. While its primary purpose was to guard the Dark Portal, it also served as a trading hub and a laboratory from which arcane organizations could study the portal and its magic. Nethergarde fell to the Iron Horde in the most recent otherworldly incursion, and though the ruin was eventually retaken by combined Alliance and Horde forces, it hasn't been rebuilt or refortified. Stormwind would like to reoccupy Nethergarde once any remaining dangers within are eliminated and any eldritch discoveries are cataloged and rendered safe.

entries.name: Scarlet Monastery
entries: Once the headquarters of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, the haunted Scarlet Monastery is described in {@area chapter 6|499|x}.

entries.name: Scholomance
