But times have changed. After the Lich King swept through Azjol-Nerub and reanimated the dead in his wake as his {@area Scourge|403|x} minions, the surviving nerubians fled deeper into the earth. Their tunneling awakened a greater evil: the faceless minions of the {@area Old God|3f9|x} Yogg-Saron. Faced with war from above and below, a group of living nerubians called the Azjol-anak hid underground, plotting the downfall of both the Scourge and the Faceless Ones, as well as the reclamation of their lost realm.

entries.name: Azjol-Nerub Adventures
entries: Use the suggestions in the Azjol-Nerub Adventure Hooks table to create adventures there. Multiple hooks could be active at once, creating a main quest and a side quest.

entries.caption: Azjol-Nerub Adventure Hooks
rows: While the characters flee the Scourge across Northrend, the ground collapses beneath them, casting them into nerubian tunnels. Now they must find a way back to the surface.

Seer Ixit of the Azjol-anak approaches the characters and offers them great riches if they'll help slay Anub'arak (for more on Ixit and Anub'arak, see "{@area Azjol-Nerub Characters|420|x}" below). (Renown: +3 with the {@area Kirin Tor|30e|x})

The Alliance or Horde seeks a way past the Wrath Gate into Icecrown Citadel and asks the characters to secure the route Arthas took through Azjol-Nerub long ago. (Renown: +3 with one {@area Alliance|29b|x} or {@area Horde|2ca|x} subfaction)

Explorer Brann Bronzebeard has returned to Dalaran, terrified by the presence of Yogg-Saron within the titan vault of Ulduar. He asks the adventurers to coerce the Old God's herald, Volazj, into being a guide for a return expedition. (Renown: +3 with the {@area Explorers' League|306|x})

entries.name: Azjol-Nerub Areas
entries: The characters will likely travel through the following areas of Azjol-Nerub in the listed order:

items.name: Gilded Gate
items.entry: Ice caves lead to a locked gate guarded by six {@creature Nerubian Crypt Fiend|WoW|Nerubian Crypt Fiends} and a towering nerubian sage called {@creature Krik'thir the Gatewatcher|WoW} (see "{@area Azjol-Nerub Characters|421|x}"). Krik'thir holds the key to the gate; the lock is complex (1 minute to pick) and of superior quality ({@dc 20}).

items.name: Web-Choked Chasm
items.entry: A slender bridge leads across a chasm but is broken halfway across. A wall of webs blocks further progress to the east, but a makeshift floor spun from webs allows characters access to a tunnel that spirals downward to the northeast. Halfway down, the characters are attacked by six {@creature Nerubian Crypt Fiend|WoW|Nerubian Crypt Fiends} that rush down the long staircases in the west of the chamber from their barracks (not shown).

items.name: Hadronox's Lair
items.entry: The spiraling tunnel leads down to a funnel web where {@creature Hadronox|WoW} (see "{@area Azjol-Nerub Characters|422|x}") waits for prey. Bones are piled into vast mounds beneath the stairs.

items.name: Passage of Lost Fiends
items.entry: At the bottom of the funnel web, some 100 feet below the bridge from the Gilded Gate, a 300-foot drop leads through centuries of nerubian architecture to the depths of the Brood Pit.

items.name: Brood Pit
items.entry: In the Brood Pit, thousands of nerubian eggs, already infected with undeath, prepare to hatch into new warriors for the Lich King. A {@creature N'raqi Faceless One|WoW} called Herald Volazj (see "{@area Azjol-Nerub Characters|423|x}") meditates at the bottom, watched by two {@creature Nerubian Crypt Fiend|WoW} brood keepers. Volazj psychically communes with Yogg-Saron while awaiting an audience with Anub'arak.

items.name: Throne of the Traitor King
items.entry: {@creature Anub'arak|WoW} (see "{@area Azjol-Nerub Characters|424|x}") dwells here, guarding the exit into Icecrown. A circular platform stands in the middle of the room; its top is 50 feet above a floor of webs. When the characters enter, he is burrowed into the platform, waiting to ambush anyone who crosses. Two {@creature Nerubian Venomancer|WoW|Nerubian Venomancers} lurk in the webs below.

entries.name: About Azjol-Nerub
entries: Introduced in the {@i Wrath of the Lich King} expansion, Azjol-Nerub is a dungeon designed for five characters of great power. The dungeon's story is part of the ongoing war against {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Arthas, the Lich King}. By preventing him from enslaving the living nerubians of Azjol-Nerub, the characters simultaneously gain powerful allies and rob Arthas of potential Undead reinforcements.

As presented here, Azjol-Nerub incorporates elements of a related dungeon, Ahn'kahet, called the Old Kingdom. While the focus of adventures in Azjol-Nerub is overthrowing the undead Traitor King Anub'arak, adventures in Ahn'kahet (the lower reaches of an ancient subterranean city) include the n'raqi and the malign influence of Yogg-Saron.

entries.name: Resting in Azjol-Nerub
entries: Back-to-back boss battles can exhaust the characters quickly, forcing them to rest. Nerubian structures are built into the cliffs above and below what's shown on the map. By ascending or descending 100 feet, the characters can find an empty room to rest in. The characters must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check to try to conceal themselves during a Short Rest or a {@dc 25} check during a Long Rest.

entries.name: Interrupting a Rest
entries: If more than half the party fails this check, their rest is interrupted by a patrol of four {@creature Nerubian Crypt Fiend|WoW|Nerubian Crypt Fiends}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When the characters defeat a boss listed below, choose the treasure labeled with that boss's name as a reward, or roll {@dice 4d6} to choose randomly.

entries.caption: Azjol-Nerub Treasure
rows: Nerubian sculpture and jewelry worth 5,500 ({@dice 10d10 × 100}) GP to the Explorers' League
Krik'thir the Gatewatcher: A gnomish crab tank ({@item Apparatus of Kwalish|XDMG}) that failed to breach the gate
A slain death knight's runeblade named Exile ({@item Nine Lives Stealer|XDMG})
The corpse of a dead adventurer carrying 10,000 GP worth of art and a {@item Ring of Feather Falling|XDMG} that slipped off his finger
Herald Volazj: A saronite {@item +3 Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG} etched with a thousand mouths
Hadronox: {@item Life-Staff of the Web Lair|WoW}
Anub'arak: {@item Dwarven Plate|XDMG} and a {@item Dwarven Thrower|XDMG} bearing the Bronzebeard forgemark

entries.name: Azjol-Nerub Characters
entries: Azjol-Nerub's key NPCs are mostly minions of the Lich King, but those who fight the Scourge could become unlikely allies of explorers. These NPCs are presented in the order they're most likely encountered.

entries.name: Seer Ixit

entries: Our enemies believe us vanquished. We will show them the consequence of their ignorance.

Seer Ixit, who might serve as a quest giver for this dungeon (see "{@area Azjol-Nerub Adventures|419|x}"), is an ambitious and resilient sorcerer with an enormous ego and an uncommon fondness for surface folk. He dreams of reviving the Nerubian Empire by banishing the Faceless Ones and annihilating the Scourge, starting with Traitor King Anub'arak. His dreams can be achieved only with the aid of the Alliance or the Horde.
Ixit is a {@creature Nerubian Venomancer|WoW}.

entries.title: {@creature Krik'thir the Gatewatcher|WoW}

entries.name: Herald Volazj

entries: Gaze into the void. It is the perpetuity in which they dwell.

The will of Yogg-Saron is mighty. The Old God has sent his herald, a {@creature N'raqi Faceless One|WoW} called Volazj from depths of the fallen nerubian kingdom of Ahn'kahet to cull the beleaguered nerubians and annihilate anyone foolish enough to threaten the Old God.

entries.name: Blackfathom Deeps
entries: {@i For Level 5–10 Characters • The Old Gods}

The ruins of Lathar'Lazal have become a nest of evil. Once a temple of Elune on {@area Ashenvale's|338|x} rain-drenched west coast, it has been defiled by the Twilight's Hammer, worshippers of the Old Gods. They were drawn to the ruin by a slithering scion of their slumbering masters: {@creature Aku'mai|WoW|Aku'mai the Devourer}.
To protect this burgeoning evil power, the cultists have allied with the naga and murlocs who occupy this ruin, threatening both the Alliance and the Horde.

entries.name: Blackfathom Deeps Adventures
entries: Use the suggestions in the Blackfathom Deeps Adventure Hooks table to draw adventurers there.

entries.caption: Blackfathom Deeps Adventure Hooks
rows: Kaal Grimfang, commander of Zoram'gar Outpost, has ordered a strike against the naga that haunt the Zoram Strand. He asks the adventurers to strike into their lair in Blackfathom Deeps. (Renown: +1 with {@area Orgrimmar|2df|x})

Raene Wolfrunner, a night elf tracker, seeks a lost party of Sentinels, including a trainee. She thinks they were captured by the Horde and asks the characters to search the coast. While there, the characters discover that the Sentinels were taken to Blackfathom Deeps by naga. (Renown: +1 with {@area Darnassus|29c|x})

Je'neu Sancrea, a troll shaman of the Earthen Ring, has seen naga witches carrying gems thrumming with elemental power. Consulting the spirits, he heard a name: Aku'mai. Unsure of its meaning, he asks the characters to search Blackfathom Deeps. (Renown: +1 with the {@area Earthen Ring|300|x})

Thaelrid Silversky, a night elf warrior of the Argent Dawn, has been hunting Kelris Doomfang, a shaman-turned-warlock who committed a string of ritual murders across Kalimdor. His cult lurks within Blackfathom Deeps. Thaelrid asks the characters to find him and bring him to justice—dead or alive. (Renown: +1 with the {@area Argent Dawn|2f3|x})

entries.name: Blackfathom Deeps Areas
entries: The characters will likely travel through the following areas of Blackfathom Deeps in the listed order.

entries.name: Drowned Sacellum
entries: This half-flooded grotto is filled with crumbling kaldorei ruins. Characters who touch the water alert {@area murlocs|4ec|x} of the Blindlight tribe lurking below the surface, which rush to begin combat.

entries.name: Pool of Ask'ar
entries: {@area Naga|4f1|x} warriors patrol the waters of this pool, always alert for aquatic invaders.

entries.name: Central Island
entries: {@creature Ghamoo-Ra|WoW} (see "{@area Blackfathom Deeps Characters|437|x}" below) attacks any intruders on this island. When Ghamoo-Ra attacks, two {@creature Naga Myrmidon|WoW|Naga Myrmidons} come to investigate from 30 feet away. If a character enters the water while fighting Ghamoo-Ra, there is a 50 percent chance each round the disturbance attracts another {@b Naga Myrmidon}.

entries.name: North Cavern
entries: The naga witch {@creature Lady Sarevess|WoW} (see "{@area Blackfathom Deeps Characters|438|x}" below) conducts rituals at her bone-strewn altar, guarded by two {@creature Naga Myrmidon|WoW|Naga Myrmidons}.

entries.name: South Cavern
entries: Night elf Sentinels Aluwyn and Relwyn Shadestar and trainee Issara are tied up here to be sacrificed on Sarevess's altar, guarded by a {@creature Naga Siren|WoW} and a {@creature Naga Myrmidon|WoW}.

entries.name: Blindlight Grotto
entries: Murlocs and naga patrol the Blindlight Grotto, kept in tenuous peace by their alliance with the Twilight's Hammer. The northernmost cave is the lair of {@creature Gelihast|WoW} (see "{@area Blackfathom Deeps Characters|439|x}") and ten {@creature Murloc Forager|WoW|Murloc Foragers} who attend him. If Gelihast is slain here, his altar to the Old Gods reacts to this tribute, giving each character a {@reward Charm of Heroism|XDMG}.

entries.name: Moonshrine Ruins
entries: Once-majestic bridges stretch over a vast pool toward a ruined moonwell, the centerpiece of this former temple to Elune. Members of the Twilight's Hammer patrol the entrance to their inner sanctum.

An underwater cave lies hidden under the platform leading into the Moonshrine Sanctum. A huge threshadon called Old Serra'kis, a creature similar to a plesiosaurus (use the {@creature Giant Shark|XMM} stat block), lurks in that cave and rarely emerges.

entries.name: Moonshrine Sanctum
entries: When the naga took over the Moonshrine Sanctum, they erected a statue of Queen Azshara; when the Twilight's Hammer seized the temple, the cultists kept the statue, for Azshara communed with the Old Gods. {@creature Twilight Lord Kelris|WoW} (see "{@area Blackfathom Deeps Characters|43a|x}" below) makes sacrifices on an altar here, then offers the bodies to Aku'mai.

entries.name: Lair Doors
entries: Behind the altar are stone doors that open when all four braziers are lit (see below).

entries.name: Ritual Braziers
entries: Twilight Lord Kelris's rituals corrupt the elements with the power of the Void. Four ritual braziers at the corners of the altar must be lit to open Aku'mai's door. On Initiative count 20 of each round of combat with Kelris, one of these braziers lights with purple flame, summoning Kelris's allies in unoccupied spaces within 20 feet of the altar, split between the east and west sides of the area:

items.name: First Flame:
items.entry: Eight makrura ({@creature Giant Crab|XMM|Giant Crabs})

items.name: Second Flame:
items.entry: One snapjaw ({@creature Archelon|XMM})

items.name: Third Flame:
items.entry: Eight makrura ({@creature Giant Crab|XMM|Giant Crabs})

items.name: Fourth Flame:
items.entry: Two {@creature Water Elemental|XMM|Water Elementals}

entries: Once all four braziers are lit, the doors open. If Kelris dies before they are all lit, the characters can light them without summoning any more creatures.

entries.name: Aku'mai's Lair
entries: A dank cavern filled with the bones of countless sacrifices leads to an inky pool where {@creature Aku'mai|WoW} (see "{@area Blackfathom Deeps Characters|43b|x}" below) awaits fresh tribute.

entries.name: About Blackfathom Deeps
entries: Blackfathom Deeps is a classic dungeon from the original {@i World of Warcraft}, originally designed for five characters of moderate level. In its first incarnation and as presented in this chapter, the dungeon focuses on the naga's budding alliance with the Twilight's Hammer cult.

After the Cataclysm, a new Twilight's Hammer leader came to Blackfathom, fed Twilight Lord Kelris to Aku'mai, and displaced most of the naga. In this era, the dungeon is populated with {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cult Fanatics}, {@creature Elemental Cultist|XMM|Elemental Cultists}, and {@creature Water Elemental|XMM|Water Elementals}, though the Blindlight murlocs are still numerous. {@creature Ghamoo-Ra|WoW} remains in the ruins, stubbornly resisting the Twilight's Hammer's attempts to turn the turtle into a weapon. The other dungeon bosses include these key characters:

{@b Domina} is a Forsaken {@creature Cultist Hierophant|XMM} with the Undead type. She sacrificed Sarevess to Aku'mai after the naga failed to protect the cult's operations and now occupies Sarevess's cave.

{@b Executioner Gore} is an orc {@creature Gladiator|XMM} who specializes in dragging screaming innocents to the altar for sacrifice to Aku'mai. He lurks in the Moonshrine Ruins and might come to Thruk's aid if combat breaks out near the entrance.

{@b Subjugator Kor'ul} is a n'raqi ({@creature Mind Flayer|XMM}) that was charged with bringing Blackfathom Deeps under the cult's firm control. Kor'ul slew Gelihast first, and the murlocs in Blindlight Grotto are now under Kor'ul's command.

{@b Thruk} is an ogre lord ({@creature Hill Giant|XMM}) who is focused on killing the Guardian of the Deep and claiming its treasure. The Guardian of the Deep is a monstrous crab ({@creature Chuul|XMM}) that displaced Old Serra'kis from the cave beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum. Thruk is most often encountered near the entrance to the Moonshrine Ruins, trying to lure the crab out of the depths.

{@b Twilight Lord Bathiel} was once mortal, but the power of the {@area Old Gods|3f9|x} transformed him into an elemental ascendant (use the {@creature Marid|XMM} stat block; Bathiel doesn't have access to {@spell Wish|XPHB}).

entries.name: Sample Encounters
entries: Use the Blackfathom Deeps Encounters table to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate.

entries.caption: Blackfathom Deeps Encounters
rows: One {@creature Murloc Oracle|WoW} leading {@dice 2d4} {@creature Murloc Forager|WoW|Murloc Foragers}
Two {@creature Naga Myrmidon|WoW|Naga Myrmidons} carrying an orc or night elf captive to {@creature Lady Sarevess|WoW}
A {@creature Naga Sea Witch|WoW} demonstrating her superior magic to three {@creature Murloc Oracle|WoW|Murloc Oracles}

Three Twilight's Hammer {@creature Cult Fanatic||Cult Fanatics} with three {@creature Voidwalker|WoW} servants chant around an impassive {@creature Water Elemental|XMM} to transform it into a glorious new form.

The characters hear the whispers of an Old God dreaming beneath the sea. They must succeed on a {@dc 19} Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of their next turn. Roll again on this table.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When the characters overcome an encounter, roll {@dice 2d6} on the Blackfathom Deeps Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll {@dice 4d6} or choose a treasure labeled with the boss's name.

entries.caption: Blackfathom Deeps Treasure
rows: A bag of 450 GP in occult ritual tools
Lady Sarevess: {@item Trident of Fish Command|XDMG}
Twilight Lord Kelris: {@item Rod of the Sleepwalker|WoW}
Twilight Lord Kelris: {@item Ring of Swimming|XDMG}

entries.name: Blackfathom Deeps Characters
entries: The leaders of multiple factions of villains lurk within this corrupted grotto. They're listed in the order they're most likely encountered.

entries.name: Deadmines
entries: {@i For Level 1–4 Characters • Alliance Versus Horde}

Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood plots Stormwind's downfall. These tunnels wind beneath the gold-mining town of Moonbrook in Stormwind's border province of {@area Westfall|375|x}. Amid the chaos of the First War, the mines were occupied by orcs and ogres, then were abandoned for years until the Defias Brotherhood arrived.

The Defias Brotherhood was once the Stonemasons Guild of Stormwind, which rebuilt the city after it was razed by the Horde in the First War. The guild was a symbol of hope among the common folk. But when the corrupt nobles of Stormwind refused to pay them for years of labor, the guild started a riot that swiftly turned bloody. In the chaos, Queen Tiffin Wrynn was slain by a stray stone, and the bereaved King Varian outlawed the guild.

{@creature Edwin VanCleef|WoW}, the guild's leader, tied a red bandanna over his mouth—a symbol of the innocent blood shed by corrupt nobility—and swore to raze the city. He forged the ragtag guild into the Defias Brotherhood, and his vow of vengeance against the nobility devolved into a reign of terror. He and his followers allied with gnolls and extorted the common folk to fund a weapon to destroy Stormwind City: a Juggernaut battleship being constructed in secret in the Deadmines. VanCleef's red-masked thugs coordinate kidnappings, smugglings, bribes, and assassinations across Alliance lands and are unwittingly in league with the dragon Onyxia.

entries.name: Deadmines Adventures
entries: The Defias Brotherhood has spread its tendrils through the heart of the Alliance. Its brigands bleed the villages of Goldshire, Lakeshire, Darkshire, and beyond and funnel the money to contractors working on the Juggernaut. Roll on or choose from the Deadmines Adventure Hooks table to determine how the characters learn of this conspiracy.

entries.caption: Deadmines Adventure Hooks
rows: When the characters help the victims of an extortionist called Morgan the Collector ({@creature Bandit Captain|XMM}), they eventually discover that his house in Elwynn Forest has a ledger of the protection fees he's sent to Westfall. (Renown: +1 with {@area Stormwind|2ba|x})

Riverpaw {@creature Gnoll Warrior|XMM|Gnoll Warriors} raid a town the characters are resting in. In the raiders' base, their leader, Hogger ({@creature Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu|XMM}), has a record of payment from "EVC" for raids. (Renown: +1 with {@area Stormwind|2ba|x})

Wilder Thistlenettle, a miner drinking in Stormwind, wants someone to find his brother, Eugene Thistlenettle of the Explorer's League. Wilder warns them the supposedly abandoned mine is full of bandits. (Renown: +1 with the {@area Explorers' League|306|x})

Edwin's right-hand man, a {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM} named Bazil Thredd, flees the Stormwind Stockade pursued by four {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}. He runs into the characters and asks them to help him flee to Westfall, promising to pay them the gold he stashed there for their help.

entries.name: Deadmines Areas
entries: The characters will likely travel through the following areas of the Deadmines in the listed order.

entries.name: Mine Tunnels
entries: Winding tunnels connect the entrance of the dungeon, the Mast Room, the Goblin Foundry, and Ironclad Cove. Heavy iron doors (AC 19, HP 72, open {@dc 20}) separate these areas from the mines.

entries.name: Laborers
entries: Dozens of captive Stormwind citizens ({@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM}) toil for {@creature Foreman Rhahk'Zor|WoW} (see "{@area Deadmines Characters|452|x}") who patrols the northern tunnels. These laborers aid the characters in killing Rhahk'Zor if they are freed. Their Speed is reduced to 5 feet by a ball and chain on their ankles, which can be removed by taking the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action and making a successful {@dc 13} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blasting Barrels
entries: Every 20 feet along the tunnel walls are wooden barrels of blasting powder (AC 10, HP 5, Vulnerability to Fire damage). They explode when destroyed, dealing 11 ({@dice 2d10}) Fire damage to creatures and objects in a 5-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}.

entries.name: Collapsed Passage
entries: The dwarves Wilder and Eugene Thistlenettle led a mining expedition into what they thought was an abandoned mine a few months ago. The tunnel collapsed, and only Wilder escaped. The Defias avoid this area, claiming they can hear the weeping of lost prospectors. Indeed, Eugene Thistlenettle ({@creature Wight|XMM}) and his crew ({@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls}) are now Undead.
This passage leads east to a tower overlooking Ironclad Cove. It also leads south to a 30-foot drop into the cold water of a flooded cave.

entries.name: Mast Room
entries: Sneed's lumber mill turns Duskwood pines into timbers for building ships. If intruders attack, Sneed ({@creature Goblin Boss|XMM}) leads the defense from inside {@creature Sneed's Shredder|WoW} (see "{@area Deadmines Characters|454|x}"). His six {@creature Goblin Minion|XMM|Goblin Minions} clamber onto a mast hanging from the ceiling and hurl bombs (from a stash of twelve), using the following action:

entries.name: Throw Bomb
entries: The goblin throws a bomb at a point it can see within 60 feet. Dexterity Saving Throw: {@dc 12}, creatures in a 5-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point. Failure: 10 ({@dice 3d6}) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

entries.name: Goblin Foundry
entries: Gilnid's foundry smelts the ore from the mine's upper levels into engines and artillery. An enormous crucible suspended from the ceiling pours molten metal into molds and discharges the slag into drains. A crew of {@creature Goblin Minion|XMM|Goblin Minions} and {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} patrols here, but they flee or surrender once {@creature Gilnid|WoW} (see "{@area Deadmines Characters|455|x}") activates his prototype Foe Reapers (use the {@creature Animated Armor|XMM} stat block, except their Slam attack deals Slashing damage).

entries.name: Ironclad Cove
entries: At the Deadmines' deepest point is Ironclad Cove, a cavern large enough to fit an ogre village. A series of locks has flooded the cavern, allowing goblin engineers to construct the nearly completed Juggernaut. The docks leading to the Juggernaut are crawling with Defias laborers ({@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits}) and Bloodsail Buccaneers ({@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates}) hired to crew the ship. Flocks of parrots ({@creature Blood Hawk|XMM|Blood Hawks}) swoop overhead, hunting for intruders.

To board the Juggernaut, the characters must defeat or avoid three random encounters (from the {@book Ironclad Cove Encounters table|WoW|6|Ironclad Cove Encounters}). They can avoid encounters by sneaking past or bluffing their way in with disguises (see the sidebar "{@area The Subtle Approach|44d|x}").

entries.name: Sneaking Aboard the Juggernaut
entries: The stacks of cargo on the pier make good hiding places. If the characters successfully hide, they evade one random encounter.

entries.name: Disguises and Suspicion
entries: The Defias and the Bloodsail pirates mistrust each other and avoid interacting. If the characters each wear a red bandanna or a pirate hat and succeed on a {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check, they evade one random encounter by being ignored.

entries.name: Exits
entries: A footpath tunnel on the eastern wall leads to the southern coast of Westfall. The sea gate that occupies the entire northern wall leads through a series of locks to another sea gate on the northwest coast of Stranglethorn.

entries.name: The Juggernaut
entries: The Juggernaut's crew serves under Captain Greenskin and his tauren first mate, Mister Smite, who in turn report to Edwin VanCleef for the duration of their contract. Destroying the Juggernaut won't stop VanCleef, nor will killing him stop his minions from using the Juggernaut—only doing both will end this threat.

entries.name: Reaching VanCleef
entries: {@creature Edwin VanCleef|WoW} (see "{@area Deadmines Characters|458|x}") is in his cabin on the top deck. He is scheming with Mister Smite ({@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}) and two {@creature Goblin Warrior|XMM|Goblin Warriors}. The characters face one random encounter as they climb the scaffolding outside the ship.

entries.name: Sabotaging the Juggernaut
entries: Captain Greenskin and Cookie oversee the skeleton crew constructing the Juggernaut's steam engine and cannons. The characters face one random encounter in the ship's interior. Damaging the ship's engines or arsenal alerts {@creature Captain Greenskin|WoW} (see "{@area Deadmines Characters|456|x}") and Cookie (a {@creature Murloc Oracle|WoW}). They arrive after 2 rounds and fight.

entries.name: The Subtle Approach
entries: The Deadmines is a good example of some of the principles outlined in the "{@area Adapting Azeroth|3c9|x}" section at the beginning of this chapter. In Dungeons & Dragons, a dungeon isn't necessarily just a gauntlet of combat encounters. Since characters can interact with the world in any way they can imagine, sometimes they concoct clever solutions to the challenges presented in a dungeon and take the adventure in unexpected directions. As the Dungeon Master, you might need to think on your feet to adapt to their plans.

For example, players might come up with a plan to reach Edwin VanCleef without fighting his entire pirate crew—they disguise themselves as pirates and plant a rumor that turns the crew against the Defias. It's up to you to determine how this plays out, relying on the guidelines in the "{@book Resolving Outcomes|XDMG|1|Resolving Outcomes}" section of the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}. If the characters' disguises are successful and they plant a convincing rumor, probably requiring more than one successful Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check, they might spark a brawl between the pirates and the Defias brigands.

entries.name: Sample Encounters
entries: Use the encounters tables here to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the tables if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. The Mine Tunnels Encounters covers the mines on the west half of the map, and Ironclad Cove Encounters covers the cove and ship on the east half of the map.

entries.caption: Mine Tunnels Encounters
rows: {@dice 1d4} {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls} and a dwarf {@creature Wight|XMM} (Eugene Thistlenettle; see "{@area Collapsed Passage|442|x}") chasing {@dice 1d4} Defias Bandits
A chain gang of {@dice 2d6} Stormwind {@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM} brawling with two Defias {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM|Mage Apprentices}
{@dice 1d6} Defias {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} tormenting captive Stormwind {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} whom they've forced to serve them cocktails while they work
Three prototype Foe Reapers ({@creature Animated Armor|XMM}) chasing {@dice 1d6} {@creature Goblin Minion|XMM|Goblin Minions}

entries.caption: Ironclad Cove Encounters
rows: An {@creature Ogre|XMM} shouting orders as {@dice 1d6 + 3} {@creature Goblin Minion|XMM|Goblin Minions} struggle to hoist a cannon
Three {@creature Murloc Forager|WoW|Murloc Foragers} looking for food
{@dice 1d4} parrots ({@creature Blood Hawk|XMM|Blood Hawks}) looking for intruders; if the characters aren't disguised or hidden, {@dice 1d4} {@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates} soon arrive to investigate

entries.name: About the Deadmines
entries: The Deadmines dungeon has been part of {@i World of Warcraft} from the launch of the game, and its story has roots in the very first Warcraft game. In its original version and as presented here, it is the lair of the Defias Brotherhood under that group's original leader, {@creature Edwin VanCleef|WoW}. During the Cataclysm, the dungeon's story advanced: Edwin VanCleef was slain, but his young daughter took his place and adopted his mission of revenge—fueled still further by watching her father die at the hands of adventurers. (Vanessa VanCleef uses the same stat block as her father.)
Besides the VanCleef family, some other personnel changes took place in the Deadmines:
{@b Glubtok}, a two-headed ogre mage (Large {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM} with the Giant creature type), took over Rhahk'Zor's role as foreman.

{@b Helix Gearbreaker} took over for Sneed in the Mast Room. Instead of a shredder, Helix ({@creature Goblin Boss|XMM}) is guarded by a hobgoblin called the Lumbering Oaf (use the {@creature Bugbear Stalker|XMM} stat block).

{@b Foe Reaper 5000} now keeps watch over the Goblin Foundry. An improved version of the earlier prototypes, this one uses the {@creature Scarecrow|XMM} stat block and is aided by molten slags ({@creature Magmin|XMM|Magmins}).
{@b "Captain" Cookie} has usurped the position of Captain Greenskin, though the worgen Admiral Ripsnarl ({@creature Werewolf|XMM}) commands the Juggernaut.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When the characters overcome an encounter, roll {@dice 2d6} on the Deadmines Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll {@dice 4d6} or choose the treasure labeled with the boss's name.

entries.caption: Deadmines Treasure
rows: A bag of 45 ({@dice 10d8}) GP in gold dust

entries.name: Deadmines Characters
entries: {@creature Edwin VanCleef|WoW} works with contractors from the Venture Company and Bloodsail Buccaneers, listed here in the order they're most likely encountered.
Remember your first time in the Deadmines? I remember it like it was tomorrow.
It's fun to watch Cookie, knowing what's in store for the humble murloc.

entries.name: Dire Maul
entries: {@i For Level 11–16 Characters • The Burning Legion}

Dire Maul is an ancient night elf ruin occupied by vengeful spirits, cruel arcanists, sinister satyrs, and opportunistic ogres. Once known as Eldre'Thalas, it was renamed Dire Maul by the Gordrunni ogres who dwell there now.

Twelve thousand years ago, the city was ruled by a scholarly Highborne prince named Tortheldrin and the Shen'dralar, his secret order of elf mages. They safeguarded the arcane libraries of Queen Azshara, which fell under attack by the {@area Burning Legion|3d2|x} during the War of the Ancients.

The war ended with the destruction of the Well of Eternity, the source of the Highborne elves' immortality. Prince Tortheldrin's people discovered with horror that they had become addicted to the well's boundless arcane power, and their cravings soon turned to lethargy and agony. Panicked, the prince summoned a demon called Immol'thar and imprisoned it so his people could nourish themselves by siphoning its endlessly replenishing magic.

The secluded mages kept this secret for millennia. During that time, the fel power Tortheldrin consumed made him cruel. When the mages' population grew beyond Immol'thar's ability to sustain, Tortheldrin ordered the culling of his own people, sparing only his Shen'dralar, who retreated into a solipsistic obsession with ancient lore. Now, thieves and squatters have made the ruin their home, reveling just out of sight of the tormented mages within.

entries.name: Dire Maul Adventures
entries: The night elves of Darnassus seek to cleanse Eldre'Thalas of corruption. Meanwhile, the Horde's Stonemaul ogre allies seek to make Dire Maul their new stronghold. Roll on or choose from the Dire Maul Adventure Hooks table to involve the characters with these plots.

entries.caption: Dire Maul Adventure Hooks
rows: Furgus Warpwood ({@creature Ancient of War|WoW}) pleads with the night elf General Shandris Feathermoon to send adventurers to the Capital Gardens to slay his corrupted kin, Tendris Warpwood. (Renown: +2 with {@area Darnassus|29c|x})

Orhan Ogreblade (Medium {@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}), leader of the Stonemaul clan of ogres, wants to conquer the Gordok ogres of Dire Maul by installing one of the characters as their king (see "{@area Ogre Tribute|474|x}" below).

A Highborne archmage named Mordent Evenshade casts {@spell Sending|XPHB}, begging the characters for rescue. He tried to flee Prince Tortheldrin's reign of terror but was captured by ogres (see "Gordok's Seat" in "{@area North Wing: Gordok Commons|46e|x}"). (Renown: +2 with the {@area Kirin Tor|30e|x})

Prince Tortheldrin craves entertainment and loves epics. He invites the characters through his hawk familiar to dine in Eldre'Thalas and share tales of their adventures. If they accept, they discover his villainy.

The Crimson Ring pit masters have captured one of the characters' allies. The friend was kidnapped from the arena by the satyr Zevrim Thornhoof (see "{@area Warpwood Quarter Characters|47b|x}"), to be sacrificed in the vile blood rites of Hydrospawn.

A druid in the party has a nightmare of a night elf being strangled by demonic vines controlled by a sinister satyr. She begs the druid to find Eldre'Thalas and save the "Fruit of Fertility" before its corruption destroys Feralas. This elf is Millicent Serene, and the satyr has corrupted her masterwork (see "{@area Alzzin the Wildshaper|47f|x}" below). (Renown: +2 with the {@area Cenarion Circle|2f9|x})

entries.name: About Dire Maul
entries: Dire Maul has been part of {@i World of Warcraft} almost since the beginning and includes three connected dungeons intended for a group of five mid-level characters. Its story is rooted in the ancient history of the world and is thus timeless, although current lore suggests that the dungeon has been cleared of its most dangerous inhabitants—including the Highborne elves that feed on Immol'thar's fel magic.

entries.name: Dire Maul Areas
entries: Dire Maul is a sprawling complex made of three wings accessible via a central ruin.

entries.name: Central Ruin
entries: The ruins at the center of Dire Maul house ogre commoners and other scoundrels.

entries.name: Eldreth Row
entries: The front gates of Dire Maul are smashed open. Ogre sentries extort tolls from the scoundrels that congregate in the Broken Commons, and crush them if they refuse to pay. The ogres avoid the side passage into the Warpwood Quarter, because an {@creature Ancient of War|WoW} with the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition blocks the path. It moves if the condition is ended.

entries.name: Broken Commons
entries: Throngs of scoundrels have set up tents and bonfires amid the ruins, cheering for bloodsport in the Maul. The games are held by the Crimson Ring, a band of thieves and outcasts from the Horde, with {@creature King Gordok|WoW|King Gordok's} permission. This rough-and-tumble group welcomes outsiders, if only so they have new rubes to fleece.

entries.name: The Maul
entries: The coliseum was originally a temple built in honor of Queen Azshara at the height of the Kaldorei Empire. A doorway on the west side of the Broken Commons leads to a tunnel into the pit (though showboating gladiators love to jump straight in).

entries.name: East Wing: Warpwood Quarter
entries: The east wing is a grand conservatory corrupted by fel magic, which has attracted a satyr cult.

entries.name: Warpwood Quarter (Outdoors)
entries: A balcony overlooks the canopy of the trees in the Conservatory below. Characters with a Passive Perception score of 15 or higher spot the imp Pusillin (see "{@area Warpwood Quarter Characters|478|x}") spying on them behind a statue in the north, clutching a silver key. He flees indoors; a character who takes the {@action Search|XPHB} action and succeeds on a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check can track him to the Hidden Reach.

entries.name: Warpwood Quarter (Indoors)
entries: The satyr servants of {@creature Alzzin the Wildshaper|WoW} lair here. A {@creature Shivarra|WoW} bound to Alzzin's service toys with a cult of satyrs who wish to earn her favor.

entries.name: Hidden Reach
entries: Alzzin and his cult snuck into Dire Maul through this secret back entrance. Pusillin (see "{@area Warpwood Quarter Characters|478|x}") hides in the loft in the south of this room. A character can find him by taking the {@action Search|XPHB} action and making a successful {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. If they leave here without finding him, he flees through the eastern passage, emerging in the wilds of Feralas.

entries.name: Conservatory (Indoors)
entries: Characters who enter this area from the southern ramp must pass through the pool of Hydrospawn ({@creature Marid|XMM}), a mighty water elemental. Zevrim Thornhoof (see "{@area Warpwood Quarter Characters|47b|x}") and his bodyguard ({@creature Doomguard|WoW}) conduct blood rituals from the loft above the pool. They join the fight the round after combat begins with Hydrospawn.

entries.name: Conservatory (Outdoors)
entries: Despite its corruption, this lush garden flourishes beneath a shady canopy. Old Ironbark (see "{@area Warpwood Quarter Characters|47e|x}") is petrified in the middle of the room. The heavy stone door to the Shrine of Eldretharr is flanked by two {@creature Infernal|WoW|Infernals} and can be opened only by a character who succeeds on a {@dc 25} Strength check or by Old Ironbark if he is freed.

entries.name: Shrine of Eldretharr
entries: Huge, thorny vines breach the walls of this shrine. {@creature Alzzin the Wildshaper|WoW} (see "{@area Warpwood Quarter Characters|47f|x}") has conjured a demonic power called the Felvine, which lets him sense all creatures within the Warpwood Quarter. Two {@creature Felhound|WoW|Felhounds} hide in the undergrowth near the Felvine sapling in the center of the chamber. Alzzin lurks invisibly on the east side of the room until his hounds attack, then he joins in.

entries.name: West Wing: Capital Gardens
entries: The west wing is the last remaining redoubt of the Shen'dralar. Their dependence on Immol'thar's magic prevents them from leaving. The stone doors within this wing are locked; the locks are simple (1 action to pick) and of superior quality ({@dc 20}). Alternatively, they can be opened with Pusillin's Crescent Key (see "{@area Pusillin|478|x}").

entries.name: Shield Generators
entries: The dome of force in the Prison of Immolthar is generated by five pylons in this wing. See "{@area Immol'thar|483|x}" for more information; they are shown on the map as bright blue crystals.

entries.name: Capital Gardens
entries: The courtyard of the Capital Gardens is a gnarled field of petrified trees oozing with fel sap. A ramp west of the garden leads down to Tendris Warpwood (see "{@area Capital Gardens Characters|481|x}"), who guards the gate to the Prison of Immol'thar (marked D on the map) with two {@creature Treant|XMM} allies (they lack the Animate Trees action). Stairs in the northwest part of the hall (marked E on the map) lead up to the Court of the Highborne.

entries.name: Court of the Highborne
entries: The undead forms of those {@creature Prince Tortheldrin|WoW} slaughtered linger in the Court of the Highborne as {@creature Wraith|XMM|Wraiths} and {@creature Graveyard Revenant|XMM|Graveyard Revenants}, endlessly repeating the motions of life. {@creature Illyanna Ravenoak|WoW} and her giant bear Ferra (see "{@area Capital Gardens Characters|482|x}") are cursed to guard this terrace. When she attacks, all remaining Undead in this area join in.

entries.name: Prison of Immol'thar
entries: Like a crass mimicry of the Well of Eternity, the imprisoned demon Immol'thar's fel magic is siphoned constantly by {@dice 2d6 + 10} Shen'dralar {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages} to slake their thirst for magic. A dome of force prevents Immol'thar from escaping (see "{@area Immol'thar|483|x}").

entries.name: The Athenaeum
entries: A passage from the northeast of Immol'thar's prison leads up a ramp (marked C on the map) to the Athenaeum—a library holding ten thousand years of lore in its countless precious tomes. Prince Tortheldrin scrawls endless, inane texts here, guarded by two {@creature Cultist Hierophant|XMM|Cultist Hierophants}. He is also attended by {@dice 2d10 + 10} {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}, who cower in fear if he's attacked. A narrow passage (marked B) connects the Athenaeum to Gordok Commons in the north wing.

entries.name: North Wing: Gordok Commons
entries: The north wing holds a temple to Elune desecrated by the upper echelons of the Gordrunni clan, while the common ogres of the clan live in the Broken Commons or in camps in the wilderness.

entries.name: Gordok Commons
entries: Ogres use Gordok Commons for raucous parties, brawls, and crude theatre. It is patrolled by Guard Mol'dar, Stomper Kreeg, and Guard Fengus (see "{@area Captain Kromcrush and His Guards|488|x}" and "{@area Ogre Tribute|474|x}" below).

entries.name: Halls of Destruction
entries: King Gordok's guards rest in the Halls of Destruction, protecting the only path to and from their king's chamber. Guard Slip'kik oversees this area. He reports to {@area Captain Kromcrush|488|x}, who wards the entrance to Gordok's Seat. A goblin thief named Knot Thimblejack is a prisoner in the northeast corner (see "{@area Gordok Commons Characters|489|x}"). A ramp in the southwest part of the hall (marked A on the map) leads up to Gordok's Seat.

entries.name: Gordok's Seat
entries: In Gordok's Seat, dozens of {@creature Hyena|XMM|Hyenas} sleep in the jungle heat while ogre servants swat flies and use giant palm leaves to fan {@creature King Gordok|WoW} and his vizier, {@creature Cho'Rush the Observer|WoW} (see "{@area Gordok Commons Characters|487|x}" for both). The ogres scramble to protect their king, but any ogre who challenges the king to a duel of honor can vie for the crown in single combat (see "{@area Ogre Tribute|474|x}" below). A Shen'dralar named Mordent Evenshade (see "{@area Gordok Commons Characters|48d|x}") is forced to be King Gordok's jester.

entries.name: Sample Encounters
entries: Use the encounter tables below to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. If the characters leave the dungeon and return after completing a Long Rest, new creatures replace those the characters defeated.

entries.caption: Warpwood Quarter Encounters
rows: Two {@creature Treant|XMM|Treants} oozing fel sap defend the gardens from invaders, despite being corrupted.
A cult of {@dice 2d4} {@creature Felsworn Satyr|WoW|Felsworn Satyrs} perform blood sacrifices while {@dice 2d6} {@creature Shadowstalker Satyr|WoW|Shadowstalker Satyrs} keep watch from afar.
Two {@creature Felguard|WoW|Felguards} and two {@creature Felhound|WoW|Felhounds} hunt a {@creature Mage|XMM} from the Maul.
A horde of {@dice 3d12} lashers ({@creature Vine Blight|XMM|Vine Blights}) try to immobilize the characters so a corrupted {@creature Ancient of War|WoW} can kill them.

entries.caption: Capital Gardens Encounters
rows: An ancient equine spirit is held captive within a {@creature Violet Fungus Necrohulk|XMM} made of elf corpses. If saved, it bestows a {@reward Charm of Heroism|XDMG} on each of the characters.
Two {@creature Graveyard Revenant|XMM|Graveyard Revenants} and three {@creature Wraith|XMM|Wraiths} vent their rage on intruders.
Four arcane elementals (see "{@area Immol'thar|483|x}") are incinerating a nosy {@creature Gladiator|XMM}.
A bored Shen'dralar {@creature Cultist Hierophant|XMM} and her arcane golem ({@creature Shield Guardian|XMM}) take potshots at the shambling skeletons of her kin.

entries.caption: Gordok Commons Encounters
rows: Stomper Kreeg has returned victorious from the Maul and is reveling. He has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, and his party of {@dice 1d12} drunken {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, but their {@dice 2d8} {@creature Hyena|XMM|Hyenas} and two {@creature Dire Worg|XMM|Dire Worgs} are alert and begging for scraps.
Four two-headed ogre mages ({@creature Oni|XMM}) are bullying another two-headed ogre ({@creature Ettin|XMM}) that can't use magic.

An ogre guard (see "{@area Captain Kromcrush and His Guards|488|x}") has taken four human {@creature Gladiator|XMM|Gladiators} alive as a prize from the Maul and plans to boil and eat them. The captured warriors are in chains and have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.

An Eye of Kilrogg (a visible, green sensor otherwise like that created by the {@spell Arcane Eye|XPHB} spell, with a Passive Perception of 20) drifts by. If it spots the characters, it summons two {@creature Doomguard|WoW}, then vanishes.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When the characters overcome an encounter, roll {@dice 2d6} on the Dire Maul Treasure table below. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll {@dice 4d6} or choose the treasure labeled with the boss's name.

entries.caption: Dire Maul Treasure
rows: {@item +2 Armor|XDMG} in sleek, Suramar City fashion
Hydrospawn: {@item Bowl of Commanding Water Elementals|XDMG}
Zevrim Thornhoof: A fel-seeping, vine-etched {@item +2 Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG}
Alzzin the Wildshaper: {@item Nine Lives Stealer|XDMG}
Tendris Warpwood: {@item Staff of the Woodlands|XDMG}
King Gordok: {@item Crown of the Ogre King|WoW}
Cho'Rush the Observer: {@item Staff of Healing|XDMG}

entries.name: Ogre Tribute
entries: Ogre tradition holds that any ogre who slays {@creature King Gordok|WoW} in a one-on-one battle becomes the new King Gordok. If at least one character is disguised as an ogre, killing King Gordok in such a duel makes them the king.

entries.name: Duel of Honor
entries: A solo fight against King Gordok is a death sentence for most characters. You can make the fight easier by not using his Legendary Actions. However, the goal of a solo fight is to survive until someone realizes that King Gordok cheats by letting {@creature Cho'Rush the Observer|WoW} secretly heal him (see the Adviser's Aid Bonus Action in his stat block). Revealing this causes the ogre audience to roar for the whole party to join the fight and kill the "cheater king."

entries.name: Aftermath
entries: If Cho'Rush survives, he declares the winner the new king. Without his declaration, the ogres all brawl to become the new king. To hail the new king, the surviving ogres bestow tribute or grant {@book Blessings|XDMG|2|Blessings} and {@book Charms|XDMG|2|Charms} (see the Dungeon Master's Guide) with shamanic magic:

items.name: Guard Mol'dar:
items.entry: {@reward Charm of Vitality|XDMG}

items.name: Guard Slip'kik:
items.entry: {@reward Charm of Clairvoyance|WoW} (functions as a {@item Potion of Clairvoyance|XDMG})

items.name: Stomper Kreeg:
items.entry: Strong rum worth {@dice 8d6 × 100} GP

items.name: Captain Kromcrush:
items.entry: {@reward Blessing of Valhalla|WoW} that summons {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} instead of {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers}

entries: {@b Cho'Rush the Observer}: Unread {@item Tome of Leadership and Influence|XDMG} pilfered from the elves

entries.name: Warpwood Quarter Characters

entries.title: Alzzin the Wildshaper

entries: Dire Maul's east wing has been taken over by the Wildspawn satyr cult, drawn to its demonic power. The creatures here are listed in the order they're most likely encountered.

entries.name: Pusillin

entries: Eeeheehee, you thinks you has Pusillin cornered? Just looks at what Pusillin has up his sleeve!
A craven {@creature Fel Imp|WoW} who knows every inch of Dire Maul, Pusillin has a Crescent Key, which opens any door in the Capital Gardens.

entries.name: Conjure Scapegoat
entries: Pusillin has learned a ritual from the warlocks of Dire Maul and keeps it on the brink of completion. He has the following Reaction:

entries.name: Ritual of J'eevee (1/Day)
entries: Trigger: Pusillin becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB} but is conscious. Response: Pusillin summons an {@creature Infernal|WoW}, which appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of him and remains until killed.

The summoned infernal is enraged at being yanked through the fabric of space and indiscriminately battles Pusillin, the characters, and any other creatures in the area. Pusillin attempts to use the distraction to escape the area.

entries.name: Zevrim Thornhoof

entries: Your blood shall catch Lord Xavius's eye! (Please?)

Zevrim is a {@creature Felsworn Satyr|WoW} and the second-in-command of the Wildspawn satyr cult. He has a secret deal with the Crimson Ring to sacrifice gladiators who lose their bouts but survive. His blood rites have whipped the elemental Hydrospawn into a murderous frenzy.
Zevrim hates living in Alzzin's shadow; he tries to impress the Burning Legion in hopes of a promotion.

entries.name: Magical Healing
entries: Zevrim has the following additional Bonus Action available:

entries.name: Gift of the Xavian (1/Day)
entries: Zevrim regains 13 ({@dice 3d8}) Hit Points.

entries.name: Old Ironbark

entries: Thank you, mortals. I shall act as your instrument of destruction before I return to the Emerald Dream.

Old Ironbark is a Friendly {@creature Ancient of War|WoW} that has the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition. If freed, he helps the characters defeat Alzzin the Wildshaper. Attempts to end the Petrified condition on him (such as with a {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell) fail unless Zevrim Thornhoof is slain first.

entries.name: Capital Gardens Characters
entries: Dire Maul's west wing is home to the Shen'dralar and the spirits of their victims. The Shen'dralar are initially {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} toward the characters but turn {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} if the characters fight them or steal their tomes. The Shen'dralar are bound to the demon Immol'thar's power and can't leave the Capital Gardens for long. The creatures here are listed in the order they're most likely encountered.

entries.name: Tendris Warpwood

entries: Ancients, rise up against these intruders!

Tendris Warpwood ({@creature Ancient of War|WoW}) was an unquestioning defender of Eldre'Thalas, his heart inexorably entwined with the fate of the city. Just as fel magic corrupted his prince, so too did it infect the ancient's spirit.

entries.name: Immol'thar's Prison
entries: Immol'thar's prison is a dome of force sustained by five shield generators (shown as blue crystals on the map). Each generator is powered by four arcane elementals (see below). A generator shuts down if its defenders die or move more than 30 feet from it. When all five generators are offline, the shield falls. The Shen'dralar mages in Immol'thar's prison try to restrain the demon, but it slays them all with a burst of arcane power and runs rampant through Dire Maul.

entries.name: Arcane Elementals
entries: The arcane elementals use the {@creature Fire Elemental|XMM} stat block, but they have Immunity to Force damage instead of Fire damage, and their traits and actions that deal Fire damage deal Force damage instead.

entries.name: Gordok Commons Characters
entries: The upper echelons of Gordrunni society have turned Dire Maul's north wing into their den. The creatures here are listed in the order they're most likely encountered.

entries.name: Captain Kromcrush and His Guards

entries: Who you callin' gnoll lover? You da gnoll lover!

Kromcrush is the captain of the guard. He got his position by sweet-talking {@creature King Gordok|WoW}, not through any exceptional skill. Kromcrush and his lieutenants use the {@creature Berserker Commander|XMM} stat block, but as ogres, their size is Large and their creature type is Giant.
Kromcrush has four lieutenants:

items.name: Guard Fengus
items.entry: Ever since {@creature Cho'Rush the Observer|WoW} told Fengus he was destined to meet a mate while on duty, Fengus has spent almost every waking moment patrolling Gordok territory.

items.name: Guard Mol'dar
items.entry: Mol'dar is a zealously loyal guard. He is convinced King Gordok gifted him with a pair of enchanted gauntlets that have made him the Gordrunni arm wrestling champion for six years running. In truth, King Gordok threw his old armor away—Mol'dar simply found it first.

items.name: Guard Slip'kik
items.entry: Slip'kik is treacherous but lazy. Rather than openly challenge King Gordok, Slip'kik tinkers with traps and magical devices, hoping to eventually deliver a coup de grace without an ounce of risk or a drop of sweat.

items.name: Stomper Kreeg
items.entry: Though Stomper Kreeg is often passed out drunk on duty, nothing rouses the ogre into a berserker fury faster than the sound of his precious drink splattering on the stone floor.

entries.name: Knot Thimblejack

entries: Please tell me that you came to get me out of here!

Knot Thimblejack ({@creature Goblin Minion|XMM}) is a tailor who made costumes for gladiators in the Maul, specializing in ogre suits. He was snatched in the night by ogres for his disrespect and thrown in irons. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, doing so with a successful {@dc 25} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check; alternatively, stealing the key from Guard Slip'kik's pocket requires a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. If the characters save Knot, he gives them a magic cap. It functions as a {@item Hat of Disguise|XDMG} that allows the wearer to appear as an ogre.

entries.name: Mordent Evenshade

entries: We Highborne must leave the past behind us.

Mordent Evenshade is a Shen'dralar {@creature Archmage|XMM} who has weaned himself off Immol'thar's fel magic. He feels the pangs of arcane withdrawals keenly, but he is disciplined enough to endure until he can unite with the night elves and their sustaining moonwells.

entries.name: Mordent's Goal
entries: Mordent aimed to flee to Teldrassil and beg Tyrande Whisperwind for aid in freeing the rest of the Shen'dralar from {@creature Prince Tortheldrin|WoW|Tortheldrin's} evil, but his escape was cut short by the Gordrunni ogres.

entries.name: One Last Trick
entries: Mordent put up a desperate struggle to escape but was nonetheless captured. His captors demand that he use his spells to entertain King Gordok as a jester. He plans to cast his {@spell Fly|XPHB} spell when adventurers free him and distract the ogres.

entries.name: Purifying the Felvine
entries: Mordent Evenshade knew Millicent Serene when they were young and gave her the nickname Milli. He thinks that her masterwork, the Fruit of Fertility, could be saved if it were watered with water from the roots of Nordrassil in Mount Hyjal—possibly starting an adventure arc that sends the characters to the ends of Azeroth and pits them against the Burning Legion.

entries.name: Onyxia's Lair
entries: {@i For Level 17–20 Characters • Dragonflights}

A jagged stone edifice looms in the southern wilds of Dustwallow Marsh. Near enough to threaten Theramore and spy on Orgrimmar, Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, spins her schemes from the seething depths of her volcanic lair. The regent of Stormwind and the Warchief of the Horde will both pay handsomely for Onyxia's head.

entries.name: Onyxia's Lair Areas
entries: Onyxia's fiery magic has created a magma tunnel. It has the following featured areas:

items.name: Cavern Mouth
items.entry: The pitch-black mouth of the cave slopes downward and contains a magical trap. When a Humanoid walks down the path as it loops under itself, the path above detonates, collapsing in a shower of boulders in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high {@variantrule Cylinder [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cylinder} centered on the triggering creature. This seals the exit, and creatures in the Cylinder make a {@dc 19} Dexterity saving throw, taking 99 ({@dice 18d10}) Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

items.name: Path of the Warders
items.entry: Two dragonspawn warders (use the {@creature Black Dragonflight Drake|WoW} stat block from chapter 7, but remove their Fly Speed) defend this cavern. They are Onyxia's loyal guards. Each has a quadrupedal lower body and a scaled, humanlike torso with vestigial wings and a draconic head. Two more warders appear here if characters try to fight Onyxia from this area.

items.name: Whelp Caves
items.entry: Onyxia's eggs incubate in the whelp caves. Each 10-foot square contains one whelp egg. If a Humanoid comes within 10 feet of an egg, the egg hatches into a {@creature Black Dragonflight Whelp|WoW} and begins combat. A creature can avoid causing eggs to hatch until the end of its turn by taking the {@action Hide|XPHB} action and making a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check.

items.name: Onyxia's Hoard
items.entry: Onyxia ({@creature Black Dragonflight Dragon (Gargantuan)|WoW|Black Dragonflight Dragon}) lairs here. In her lair, she can use Legendary Resistance five times per day, and she can use four Legendary Actions per round. Defeating her in her lair earns a party 50,000 XP. She starts the fight on the ground, starts flying when she is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, then lands to flee through the secret exit. When Onyxia is Bloodied, one {@creature Black Dragonflight Whelp|WoW} hatches on Initiative count 20 of each round. Replace Onyxia's Pounce Legendary Action with Tail Swipe:

entries.name: Tail Swipe
entries: Melee Attack Roll: +16 to hit, reach 20 ft. Hit: 36 ({@dice 6d8 + 9}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed 60 feet straight away from Onyxia.

items.name: Secret Exit
items.entry: An illusory wall in the northwest of Onyxia's hoard hides a secret exit that leads to the surface. A similar illusion conceals the tunnel, which opens into the rocky, southern hills of {@area Dustwallow Marsh|33e|x}. Physical interaction with either image reveals it to be illusory. A creature that takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful {@dc 22} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Onyxia's treasure hoard contains 50,000 GP in coins; also, roll three times on the Onyxia's Lair Art Objects table and three times on the Onyxia's Lair Magic Items table, rerolling duplicate magic items.

entries.caption: Onyxia's Lair Magic Items
rows: {@item Rod of Resurrection|XDMG} stolen by black dragons from the Sons of Lothar on Outland
Wildhammer dwarf bard Russell Brower's {@item Instrument of the Bards, Ollamh Harp|XDMG|Instrument of the Bards (Ollamh harp)}
{@item Cloak of Invisibility|XDMG} made of Nerubian silk
Vrykul {@item Belt of Cloud Giant Strength|XDMG|Belt of Giant Strength (cloud)}

entries.name: About Onyxia's Lair
entries: Onyxia's Lair was one of the forty-character raids that appeared in {@i World of Warcraft} when the game first launched. It is a classic adventure to slay a powerful, cunning dragon.

entries.name: Onyxia's Lair Characters
entries: Onyxia is the only character of note here. She might have guests, such as naga, Dark Iron supplicants, or her brother Nefarian.

entries.name: Onyxia

entries: How fortuitous. Usually, I must leave my lair to feed.

Onyxia is manipulating Azeroth's factions. She has her father's arrogance and enough cunning to deserve it. Unlike her brother, Nefarian, she has little desire to monologue or stroke her ego. She flees fights she doesn't think she can win—such as if her human visage is revealed deep in enemy territory—and swiftly and confidently attacks when confronted in her lair.

In {@area Stormwind|2ba|x}, she uses her visage to masquerade as Lady Katrana Prestor, adviser to King Varian Wrynn. In his addled state, the king hangs on her every word. There, she is protected by dragonspawn disguised with illusions as Stormwind guards. She has made fewer inroads within the Horde, but from her lair in {@area Dustwallow Marsh|33e|x}, she secretly stokes tensions between {@area Theramore|356|x} and {@area Orgrimmar|2df|x}, preventing the Horde and the Alliance from uniting against the black dragonflight forces mustering in {@area Blackrock Mountain|37a|x}.

entries.name: Scarlet Monastery
entries: {@i For Level 5–10 and 11–16 Characters • The Scourge}

The warriors of the Light have sacrificed much in the campaign to purge the ravening Scourge from the despoiled kingdom of Lordaeron. But pride and loss have warped zeal into fanaticism. The extremists of the Scarlet Crusade believe all who don't wear their scarlet tabard are plagued. The Crusade has abandoned the Alliance to purge Lordaeron not just of the Scourge, but of all non-humans.
The Scarlet Monastery is the Crusade's headquarters and looms on the edge of {@area Tirisfal Glades|372|x}. Scarlet Commander Renault Mograine has transformed this sprawling temple into a fortress.

entries.name: About Scarlet Monastery
entries: The Scarlet Monastery has been in {@i World of Warcraft} from the beginning, first appearing as four linked dungeons. They were designed for five characters, and each was more challenging than the one before it. The graveyard was suitable for characters not yet at the middle of the level range, while the cathedral was a challenge for high-level characters. The four dungeons were simplified into two in the {@i Mists of Pandaria} expansion, with many dungeon bosses remaining in place as the Scarlet Crusade resisted all efforts to oust them from their stronghold. During the {@area Burning Legion's|3d2|x} third invasion, however, the Knights of the Ebon Blade wiped out the crusaders and raised High Inquisitor Whitemane as a death knight.

entries.name: Scarlet Monastery Adventures
entries: Use the suggestions in the Scarlet Monastery Adventure Hooks table to draw adventurers there. An adventure could take place in one part of the monastery or take the characters from wing to wing.

entries.caption: Scarlet Monastery Adventure Hooks
rows: The leaders of the Argent Dawn ask the characters to claiming the Scarlet Commander's head. (Renown: +2 with the {@area Argent Dawn|2f3|x})
Another group of adventurers tried to storm the cathedral, but they were captured. A mutual friend asks the characters to save them from the {@area Chamber of Atonement|49e|x}.

Sages of Thunder Bluff mistrust the Forsaken and want to turn the tauren chieftain against them. They ask adventurers to retrieve the Compendium of the Fallen, a book of the Crusade's research on undead schemes, from the Athenaeum. (Renown: +1 with {@area Thunder Bluff|2e9|x})

{@creature Scarlet Commander Mograine|WoW|Mograine} and {@creature High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane|WoW|High Inquisitor Whitemane} have left the monastery on a mission. The Argent Dawn asks the characters to infiltrate the cathedral and steal intelligence on their next campaign. (Renown: +2 with the {@area Argent Dawn|2f3|x})

{@creature Scarlet Champion Herod|WoW|Herod}, a crusader who trains recruits, never takes off his helmet. A faction commander instructs the characters to kill Herod quietly and replace him with a spy. (Renown: +2 with one {@area Alliance|29b|x} or {@area Horde|2ca|x} subfaction)

An Argent Dawn priest who seeks information about the sword {@item Ashbringer|WoW} known only by Fairbanks, the first High Inquisitor, asks the characters to find and interrogate his corpse. (Renown: +1 with the {@area Argent Dawn|2f3|x})

entries.name: Scarlet Monastery Areas
entries: The Scarlet Monastery is a sprawling complex consisting of a graveyard, library, armory, and cathedral. Its exterior is covered with gleaming stained glass windows, which have AC 15 and 30 HP and have Immunity to all damage from sources outside the monastery's walls. Secret doors within the monastery are standard ({@dc 15} to detect). The monastery includes these featured areas.

entries.name: Grand Vestibule
entries: At any given time, {@dice 2d6} {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans} and {@dice 2d6} {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM|Mage Apprentices} loiter in the grand vestibule, drinking, brawling, and studying scripture. Two double doors to the north are sealed with {@spell Arcane Lock|XPHB} spells, but the Scarlet Key opens them (see "Athenaeum" in "{@area Library|4a1|x}"). Pulling a torch sconce in the statueless southwest alcove opens a secret door to the Forlorn Cloister. The grand vestibule is suitable for levels 5–10.

entries.name: Graveyard
entries: Despite the Scarlet Crusade's unending war against the Scourge, the curse of undeath has taken root within the monastery grounds. The graveyard is suitable for levels 5–10.

entries.name: Chamber of Atonement
entries: The Chamber of Atonement is a morgue that Interrogator James Vishas (Medium, Lawful Evil {@creature Assassin|XMM}) and his torturers ({@dice 1d4 + 1} {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}) use as a torture chamber, teaching foes and new recruits to fear the Light.

entries.name: Forlorn Cloister
entries: {@creature Bloodmage Thalnos|WoW} (see "{@area Scarlet Monastery Characters|4b0|x}"), who haunts the western mausoleum, unwittingly carried the plague of undeath to this graveyard. The lawn smolders with burning corpses. The northern double door leading into the Cathedral is sealed with an {@spell Arcane Lock|XPHB}, but the Scarlet Key opens it (see "Athenaeum" below). The secret door leading from the grand vestibule is plainly visible and easy to open from this side.

entries.name: Library
entries: The library wing of the monastery contains plundered treasures. It is suitable for characters of levels 5–10.

entries.name: Huntsman's Cloister
entries: Scarlet beastmasters (Medium, Lawful Evil {@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains}) train their tracking hounds ({@creature Dire Wolf|XMM|Dire Wolves}) in the Huntsman's Cloister. Passing them without being noticed requires a successful {@dc 13} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check. On a failed check, the hounds begin combat, which also draws {@creature Houndmaster Loksey|WoW} (see "{@area Scarlet Monastery Characters|4b1|x}") and his three tracking hounds ({@creature Dire Wolf|XMM|Dire Wolves}) from the south cloister.

entries.name: Gallery of Treasures
entries: The gallery overflows with gilded and marble art plundered from the few survivors of Lordaeron, ostensibly so the Crusade can protect them. A tapestry on the west wall hides a secret door to the Training Grounds in the Armory.

entries.name: Athenaeum
entries: The Athenaeum is a series of halls filled with tomes of lore and even heretical works hidden by {@creature Arcanist Doan|WoW} (see "{@area Scarlet Monastery Characters|4b2|x}"), who studies in the northernmost chamber. Doan holds the Scarlet Key, which opens the magically locked doors in the grand vestibule and the Forlorn Cloister. A ten-foot-tall portrait of {@creature High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane|WoW} on the west wall hides a secret passage to the Crusader's Armory.

entries.name: Armory
entries: The monastery's armory is the focal point of its military efforts—training soldiers, housing and equipping soldiers, and commemorating its victories. The armory is suitable for levels 11–16.

entries.name: Training Grounds
entries: The courtyard has been turned into a target range, and the covered halls on either side are blocked off with iron portcullises. A tapestry on the east wall hides a secret door to the Gallery of Treasures.

entries.name: Footman's Armory
entries: The rank-and-file soldiers of the Crusade eat, sleep, and train in the filthy, cavernous cells of the Footman's Armory. Levers here control portcullises between each cell.

entries.name: Crusader's Armory
entries: Elite crusaders instruct their disciples in the Crusader's Armory. Artillery, battering rams, and explosives line the walls. A ten-foot-tall portrait of {@creature Scarlet Commander Mograine|WoW|Commander Renault Mograine} on the west wall hides a secret door to the Athenaeum.

entries.name: Hall of Champions
entries: Marble statues of the Crusade's founders, heroes from Stromgarde to Kul Tiras and even to Quel'Thalas (before elves were banished from the Crusade) watch over the Hall of Champions. which is Scarlet Champion Herod's sparring arena. The westernmost statue (of high elf mage Arellas Fireleaf) has crumbled. Beneath its plinth is a secret passage to a tool room in the Chapel Gardens.

entries.name: Cathedral
entries: The cathedral is the ritual center of the monastery, where its corrupted priests continue to pray to the Holy Light even as they serve the forces of darkness. The cathedral is suitable for levels 11–16.

entries.name: Chapel Gardens
entries: Statues of crusaders overlook the two-tiered Chapel Gardens. The soil is wet with blood, and the grass is flaked with ashes of "heretics" burned at the stake before the cathedral. {@area Roll for encounters|4ba|x} in both the lower and upper gardens.

A tool room to the east of the gardens contains a statue of an ancient crusader-gardener surrounded by hoes, rakes, and shovels. The statue pivots easily to reveal a trap door; a ladder leads down to a tunnel connecting the gardens to the Hall of Champions.

entries.name: Crusader's Chapel
entries: {@creature Scarlet Commander Mograine|WoW} preaches in the Crusader's Chapel; {@creature High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane|WoW|High Inquisitor Whitemane} prays in the secret crypt behind him and emerges only when Mograine dies (see "{@area Scarlet Monastery Characters|4af|x}" for both). Former High Inquisitor Fairbanks ({@creature Revenant|XMM}) is interred in the secret crypt. The door can be opened from within or by pulling a candelabra on the chapel's altar.

entries.name: Sample Encounters
entries: Use the encounters tables here to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. If the characters leave the dungeon and return after finishing a Long Rest, new crusaders have mustered in the area. Unless otherwise specified, Humanoid NPCs found in the monastery are Medium and Lawful Evil.

entries.caption: Graveyard Encounters (Tier 2)
rows: A {@creature Ghast Gravecaller|XMM} and two {@creature Wraith|XMM|Wraiths} devouring a torture victim
{@dice 1d4 + 2} {@creature Flaming Skeleton|XMM|Flaming Skeletons} from a body pile

entries.caption: Library Encounters (Tier 2)
rows: Twelve studious {@creature Priest Acolyte|XMM|Priest Acolytes} guarded by two {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}* and a {@creature Mage|XMM}
Three {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages} bullying a paladin ({@creature Knight|XMM}†) who struggles to perform holy magic
An {@creature Elemental Cultist|XMM} purifying a relic from the {@area Plaguelands|36a|x} with {@dice 1d6} {@creature Priest|XMM|Priests}

entries.caption: Armory Encounters (Tier 3)
rows: Two {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages} with two {@creature Fire Elemental|XMM} bodyguards
An {@creature Elemental Cultist|XMM} disciplining {@dice 1d4 + 1} {@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains} for their poor aim
{@creature Berserker Commander|XMM} brutally sparring with a fearful and {@status Bloodied|XPHB} {@creature Knight|XMM}† before a crowd of {@dice 1d6 + 6} {@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM}
Reckless {@creature Mage|XMM} and {@dice 1d4 + 4} pyromaniac {@creature Knight|XMM|Knights}† eager to defend her

entries.caption: Cathedral Encounters (Tier 3)
rows: An {@creature Archpriest|XMM} and an {@creature Elemental Cultist|XMM} preparing to burn innocent civilians at the stake, cheered on by {@dice 1d10 + 10} {@creature Warrior Infantry|XMM}

Two {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants} brought to the chapel for execution who have broken free and are surrounded by the crusaders they slew (risen as {@dice 2d10} {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls}) and two {@creature Priest|XMM|Priests} begging for help
An {@creature Archmage|XMM} directing {@dice 1d6 + 4} {@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains} to fire on intruders as {@dice 1d4 + 4} {@creature Gladiator|XMM|Gladiators} move to intercept them
An {@creature Archpriest|XMM}, guarded by three {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans},* praying over six dead crusaders

entries: {@sup †}Can cast {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} (level 4 version) once

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When the characters overcome an encounter, roll {@dice 2d6} on the Scarlet Monastery Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll {@dice 4d6} or choose the treasure labeled with the boss's name.

entries.caption: Scarlet Monastery Treasure
rows: {@item +2 Armor|XDMG} with the Crusade's fiery heraldry
Loksey: {@item Pipes of the Sewers|XDMG} (whistle that affects dogs instead of rats, and summons a {@creature Mastiff|XMM} instead of a {@creature Swarm of Rats|XMM})
Doan: {@item Vithrak, Gaze of the Deadman|WoW}
Whitemane: Cloth miter {@item Helm of Brilliance|XDMG} that marks the Crusade's High Inquisitor

entries.name: Scarlet Monastery Characters
entries: These zealots of the Scarlet Crusade train crusaders for future battlefields. Characters are ordered by wing, matching the order in "Scarlet Monastery Areas": Graveyard, Library, Armory, and Cathedral.

entries.title: {@creature Arcanist Doan|WoW}
{@creature Scarlet Commander Mograine|WoW}

entries.name: Shadowfang Keep
entries: {@i For Level 1–4 Characters • Alliance Versus Horde}

For generations, Shadowfang Keep has stood on the boundary between {@area Silverpine Forest|36f|x} and the walled kingdom of {@area Gilneas|2a6|x}. The keep has been conquered countless times over the years, filling its halls with restless spirits.

Today, this accursed fortress is held by {@creature Lord Godfrey|WoW|Lord Vincent Godfrey}, a treacherous undead who's a fugitive from both the Alliance and the Horde. Both Packleader Ivar Bloodfang (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}), a worgen leader who supports the Alliance, and Deathstalker Commander Belmont (Medium {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}), a Forsaken leader of the Horde, lead attacks on the fortress, seeking to gain revenge on Lord Godfrey and to claim this crucial redoubt in the war for Silverpine.

entries.name: Shadowfang Keep Adventures
entries: Use the suggestions in the Shadowfang Keep Adventure Hooks table to draw adventurers there.

entries.caption: Shadowfang Keep Adventure Hooks
rows: A faction commander recruits the characters to retake Shadowfang Keep from {@creature Lord Godfrey|WoW}. (Renown: +1 with one {@area Alliance|29b|x} or {@area Horde|2ca|x} subfaction)
The characters decide to claim Shadowfang Keep for themselves and use it as a {@book Bastion|XDMG|10}.
A patron in the Kirin Tor seeks The Book of Ur, which contains secrets of the worgen curse and is rumored to be in Shadowfang Keep's library. (Renown: +1 with the {@area Kirin Tor|30e|x})
The characters have claimed the keep and must defend it until reinforcements arrive.

A faction leader wants adventurers to liberate a prisoner of war held in Shadowfang Keep: either the Forsaken Deathstalker Adamant (Medium {@creature Spy|XMM}) or the human Ashcrombe (Medium {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM}). (Renown: +1 with one {@area Alliance|29b|x} or {@area Horde|2ca|x} subfaction)
The Alliance or the Horde has conquered Shadowfang Keep; a faction commander asks adventurers to reclaim the keep. (Renown: +1 with one {@area Alliance|29b|x} or {@area Horde|2ca|x} subfaction)

entries.name: About Shadowfang Keep
entries: Shadowfang Keep was a five-player dungeon in the original {@i World of Warcraft}, designed for low-level characters to confront the archmage Arugal and the worgen he liberated from the Emerald Dream and set loose on the Eastern Kingdoms. In this first iteration, best suited for level 5–10 characters, the dungeon bosses are the living Arugal ({@creature Archmage|XMM}), the already ghostly forms of {@creature Baron Silverlaine|WoW} and {@creature Commander Springvale|WoW}, and several worgen ({@creature Werewolf|XMM|Werewolves}), some of whose spirits Baron Silverlaine later calls on: Rethilgore, Razorclaw the Butcher, Odo the Blindwatcher, Fenrus the Devourer, and Wolf Master Nandos. Other tormented spirits and ferocious worgs also populate the dungeon.

The version presented in this chapter represents a later stage in the keep's history, after a group of Forsaken converted the keep into a stronghold to protect themselves from enemies during the Cataclysm.

entries.name: Shadowfang Keep Areas
entries: Shadowfang Keep has the following featured areas:

items.name: Entry Gate
items.entry: An iron portcullis blocks access from the keep's entry to the courtyard. {@creature Baron Ashbury|WoW} (see "{@area Shadowfang Keep Characters|4bd|x}") leads the keep's defenses from the jail and gatehouse, which leads to the courtyard, and can raise the gate. {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} arisen from the keep's countless defeated assailants prowl here.

items.name: Courtyard
items.entry: This courtyard provides access to the dining hall and the keep's battlements and rooftops. It is patrolled by {@creature Pustulant Monstrosity|WoW|Pustulant Monstrosities} and restless {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters} of the keep's staff.

items.name: Silverlaine Manor
items.entry: The one area of the keep Lord Godfrey couldn't reclaim is Silverlaine Manor. It is prowled by feral worgen (use the {@creature Werewolf|XMM} stat block without its Bite attack) summoned by the keep's previous master. The worgen of {@area Gilneas|2a6|x} have been unable to negotiate with them.

items.name: Dining Hall
items.entry: A banquet was set here to celebrate Lord Godfrey's liberation of Pyrewood Village, but the feast now rots untouched. {@creature Baron Silverlaine|WoW} (see "{@area Shadowfang Keep Characters|4be|x}") haunts the hall, guarded by four {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters} of his staff.

items.name: Battlements and Rooftops
