items.entry: The ghostly {@creature Commander Springvale|WoW} patrols here with two {@creature Springvale's Specter|WoW|Springvale's Specters} (see "{@area Shadowfang Keep Characters|4bf|x}" for both), watched by leering {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles}. Loot from ancient battles is strewn across the battlements.

items.name: The Keep
items.entry: Wooden stairways and catwalks wind up a tower teeming with Undead. Above it is an abandoned magical laboratory that {@creature Lord Walden|WoW} (see "{@area Shadowfang Keep Characters|4c1|x}") is ransacking.

items.name: Godfrey's Chamber
items.entry: At the keep tower's apex is the two-story chamber of {@creature Lord Godfrey|WoW} and his two {@creature Pustulant Monstrosity|WoW} bodygards (see "{@area Shadowfang Keep Characters|4c2|x}" for both). Its upper floor has collapsed into the first, and he shoots intruders from the top of the stairs while the intruders are busy with the bodyguards below.

entries.name: Sample Encounters
entries: Use the Shadowfang Keep Encounters table to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. If the characters leave the dungeon and return after completing a Long Rest, Lord Godfrey has mustered new undead troops.

entries.caption: Shadowfang Keep Encounters
rows: {@dice 2d6} {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} ({@dice 1d6} have only {@item Shortsword|XPHB|Shortswords} and {@dice 1d6} have only {@item Shortbow|XPHB|Shortbows})
{@creature Pustulant Monstrosity|WoW} and {@dice 1d4} {@creature Springvale's Specter|WoW|Springvale's Specters}
Roll on this table again, and two {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles} join the combat at the start of round 2.
Roll on this table again, and add two skeleton {@creature Knight|XMM|Knights} with the Undead type to that combat.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When the characters overcome an encounter, roll {@dice 2d6} on the Shadowfang Keep Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll {@dice 4d6} or choose the treasure labeled with its name.

entries.name: Shadowfang Keep Characters
entries: The following characters occupy Shadowfang Keep. They are listed in the order they're most likely encountered.

entries.title: {@creature Baron Ashbury|WoW}
{@creature Lord Walden|WoW}

data.name: Chapter 7: Bestiary of Azeroth

entries.title: A night elf adventurer battles naga on the Zoram Strand.

entries: This chapter presents an assortment of creatures adventurers might encounter in their travels across Azeroth and beyond. The monsters in this chapter are arranged in alphabetical order for ease of reference and summarized in the list below.

entries.name: Black Dragonflight Whelp
entries: Black dragonflight whelps are murderous little creatures that dwell near volcanoes, hot springs, and geysers. They smother prey in their magma breath and pick the meat from the globs of scalding lava.

entries.name: Black Dragonflight Drake
entries: Black dragonflight drakes use their magic to heat objects made of earth or stone. They can momentarily melt stone into magma and reshape it before it cools. These drakes delight in stalking and disorienting prey.

entries.name: Black Dragonflight Dragon
entries: Fully matured black dragonflight dragons terrorize the lands of Azeroth from the skies and manipulate society by shape-shifting into humanoid disguises. A black dragon wearing a mortal visage usually has jet-black hair and red eyes.

entries.name: Blue Dragonflight Whelp
entries: Blue dragonflight whelps display uncanny intelligence for their age. Rather than attacking an ice fisher, a blue whelp might ask to pool their knowledge, striking a deal to share the fish they catch.

entries.name: Blue Dragonflight Drake
entries: Members of the blue dragonflight are devoted students of the arcane arts. Blue dragonflight drakes learn to create and dispel magical effects, protecting their secrets from prying mages.

entries.name: Blue Dragonflight Dragon
entries: Blue dragonflight dragons view themselves as stewards of the arcane, and they disdain mortals who misuse their gifts. Noble blue dragons take the role of sagely mentors to mortal mages—for example, Kalecgos long worked with the {@area Kirin Tor|30e|x} in a mortal visage. Cruel and jealous blue dragons such as Cyanigosa try to dominate and punish mortals for their misuse of magic.

entries.name: Bronze Dragonflight Whelp
entries: Bronze dragonflight whelps are patient. They stand still for hours on end in the middle of the desert, waiting for prey to pass before striking out with maw or claw. Many travelers mistake these whelps for statues.

entries.name: Bronze Dragonflight Drake
entries: Many a villain has tried to bend a bronze dragonflight drake to their will, hoping to take advantage of the creature's prophetic magic while the drake is still young. Such opportunists quickly learn the error of their ways when the bronze drake shreds and sears their skin with its red-hot sand breath.

entries.name: Bronze Dragonflight Dragon
entries: Mature bronze dragons task themselves with maintaining the one true timeline of Azeroth. They keep close to humanoid civilizations, watching for travelers from other timelines or those who seek to alter the timeways.

entries.name: Furbolg Totemic
entries: Furbolg totemics are shaman who use totems for healing and offense.

entries.name: Furbolg Ursa
entries: Ursas are warrior leaders in furbolg tribes, larger than their kin and empowered by elemental magic.

entries.name: Green Dragonflight Whelp
entries: Members of the green dragonflight raise their whelps in the Emerald Dream whenever possible. There, a whelp learns to appreciate and spread the beauty of nature in all its forms by observing cycles of birth and death.

entries.name: Green Dragonflight Drake
entries: Emerging from the Emerald Dream, green dragonflight drakes are wise enough to take action in Azeroth. They often ally with older dragons, night elf druids, and ancients of lore to eliminate evil cults and invading demons with nature magic.

entries.name: Green Dragonflight Dragon
entries: The mightiest of the green dragonflight battle the minions of the Old Gods and shape-shift into mortal visage forms to ally with humanoids. This battle against the Old Gods puts green dragons at risk for corruption by the Emerald Nightmare, which was created by one of the Old Gods' greatest champions.

entries.name: Murloc Forager
entries: Murloc foragers live near the edges of bodies of water, spending most of their time searching for food in the mud and shallow waters. Of all murlocs, foragers are the most likely to be found outside of a group, and they often serve as an early warning system to their community, drawing would-be attackers to the water's edge for their fellow murlocs to ambush.

entries.name: Murloc Oracle
entries: Oracles lead groups of other murlocs, using magic to defend and heal their allies. Murloc oracles are more willing than other murlocs to attempt communication with those who don't speak Nerglish.

entries.name: Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar
entries: In addition to the stat blocks presented in this chapter, any of the Humanoid stat blocks in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} can be furbolgs, murlocs, or quilboar. For murlocs, add a Swim Speed equal to the creature's Speed plus 10 feet and the Amphibious trait from the stat blocks here.
Humanoids in {@i World of Warcraft} often have names that describe their role and suggest a stat block that suits them. Here are some common Humanoid roles with suggested stat blocks.

entries.name: Naga Myrmidon
entries: Myrmidons are hulking male naga who serve as front-line warriors in battles against the naga's enemies. They wield tridents with attached ropes that allow them to pull foes into melee range.

entries.name: Naga Sea Witch
entries: Sea witches are female naga who wield the magic of stormy seas.

entries.name: Naga Siren
entries: Sirens are among the most powerful naga spellcasters, channeling the cold of the marine depths into mighty frost magic.

entries.title: {@creature Naga Siren|WoW}

entries.name: Nerubian Warrior
entries: Nerubian warriors use their arachnid limbs to quickly scurry across the ground and climb onto walls and ceilings, maintaining their balance even in treacherous terrain. When attacking, they use the two arms on their humanoid torso to claw at their enemies, and these warriors often rely on their webbing to encase or restrict their foes, leaving them motionless and helpless.

The few nerubians who survived the Scourge have organized a rebellion called the Azjol-anak to retake Azjol-Nerub. Their bitterness over the loss of their kingdom has made many distrustful of anyone who isn't nerubian, and they attack whoever they come across without restraint or warning.

entries.name: Nerubian Venomancer
entries: Nerubian venomancers use their lethal toxin as one of their primary weapons. Venomancers' mastery of poison extends to their webbing, which is toxic to those held within its grasp. Venomancers are quick to assault non-nerubians, driven by their rancor over their lost and scattered kingdom.

entries.name: Nerubian Crypt Fiend
entries: Though the Lich King couldn't infect the nerubians with his plague of undeath, he raised many dead nerubians using necromancy, turning them into crypt fiends. Crypt fiends wear the remnants of the cloth that they were mummified in and rake at their foes with their powerful claws. Crypt fiends use their webs to incapacitate their enemies, whose life force is sapped by the powerful necrotic energy in the webs' strands.

entries.title: N'raqi Faceless One

entries.name: N'raqi Faceless One
entries: The most common n'raqi, faceless ones telepathically communicate with nearby creatures. Whispering into the minds of those around them, they become like gods to the weak minded and invaluable tools to those blessed with otherworldly insight. They attack both through their minds and with the strength of their two pseudopods, one of which is always much larger and more fully formed than the other.

entries.name: N'raqi Faceless General
entries: Faceless generals, also called C'Thraxxi, lead the Old Gods' armies and defend their strongholds. Each C'Thrax has a deep well of magical ability, which it deploys to rip through the minds of those who get in its way, often leaving nothing more than drained husks in its wake. Even death is not a final end for these harbingers of doom; cultists have often tried, sometimes successfully, to awaken long-dead C'Thraxxi through sinister rituals and offerings of blood.

A faceless general's hulking form is covered in chitinous plates. Both its arms end in heavy pincers, and crablike legs sprout from its back, almost resembling wings. Each individual C'Thrax has its own unique characteristics, often reflective of the particular Old God it serves. For example, the Fury of N'Zoth has many eyes on its head and upper body, much like the Old God N'Zoth, while Warbringer Yenajz, drawn to Kul Tiras by the corruption of the Tidesages, has a mantle of teeth around its head that suggests the maw of C'Thun.

entries.name: Quilboar Thornweaver
entries: Quilboar thornweavers bear thorns they believe grew from the body of their demigod progenitor Agamaggan. Their magic uses those thorns, calling on the spirits of nature to protect their territory.

entries.name: Red Dragonflight Whelp
entries: Although red dragonflight whelps are small, their fiery breath is mighty. These creatures' sense of justice leads them to take on larger foes in the name of good. Red dragonflight whelps almost never flee from a fight, for their pride hasn't yet been tempered by the wisdom of age.

entries.name: Red Dragonflight Drake
entries: Red dragonflight drakes heal tainted lands across Azeroth. By breathing streams of blazing fire across the terrain, these drakes incinerate withered plant life and bring growth from the ashes. When need is greatest, these drakes allow mortal heroes to ride and fight on their backs.

entries.name: Red Dragonflight Dragon
entries: Members of the red dragonflight are considered the most noble dragons of Azeroth, sworn to protect all life. But their benevolence should never be misunderstood as weakness; they are capable of terrible destruction, outweighed only by the life-giving power that suffuses their fiery breath.

entries.name: Felsworn Satyr
entries: Felsworn satyrs wield the fiery power of the Burning Legion as its devoted agents. They are fierce enemies of night elves, using their magic to devastate night elf communities.

entries.name: Shadowstalker Satyr
entries: Shadowstalkers are satyrs who wield the subtle magic of the Void, using that power to lurk in the darkness and strike enemies from hiding.

entries.title: {@creature Shivarra|WoW}

entries.name: Voidwalker
entries: Warlocks highly prize ordinary voidwalkers as servants because of their ability to both attract and withstand enemy attacks.

entries.name: Voidcaller
entries: Voidcallers are magic-wielding voidwalkers that appear to be draped in rotting cloth. From their shoulders hang two lanterns, which are said to bridge the realm of the living and that of the dead and sometimes attract wayward ghosts. The lanterns hang from a glowing crystalline structure that hovers over and around the voidcaller's shadowy form.
